findings.title: A succession join re-points every transaction, trade anchor and contract term on the joined instrument, and the log keyed by instrument does not name them
findings.where: rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:611-616 (`COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)` in `transactions()`), rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:285-288 (trade anchors read through `instrument_joins`), rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:423-430 (`option_terms` canonicalises the underlying through joins), rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:640-723 (`settle_successions` writes `instrument_joins`; only contract records get `derived_version = 0`, at :718-723); plan lines 73 (`instrument_joins` → kind `instrument`, key the instrument's id), 82 (a change re-reads only the named things by key), 88 (`Change::Ledger(LedgerDelta)` applied by key).
findings.claim: The engine's whole ledger reads every transaction, every trade anchor and every contract's underlying *as the book reads them*, i.e. mapped through `instrument_joins`. A row inserted or deleted in `instrument_joins` therefore changes the `instrument` field of every live transaction naming the merged id (across every account), the anchor instrument of every trade on it, and `terms.underlying` of every contract on it, without touching `transactions`, `trades` or `option_terms`. The plan's trigger writes one `instrument` key for the join; the keyed re-read fetches the instrument row and nothing else, so the engine keeps those transactions under the old id while a fresh build reads them under `into_id`. None of the five couplings reaches this: it is not a match coupling but a change the log does not name.
findings.failing_scenario: Account A holds 100 X bought under broker id old-1. A pull brings a CUSIP change: Wealthsimple retires old-1 (`retired-by-event`) and lists new-2 for the same symbol; `settle_successions` inserts (old-1 → new-2) into `instrument_joins`, and the same pull stores a sale of 100 under new-2. Log: `instrument old-1`, `record <sale>`. Incremental engine: the buy stays on instrument old-1 (never re-read), the sale is read on new-2 and finds no lots → `Beyond { qty: 100 }` (status.rs:206 says "took 100 more than the book held"), no closed trade, a position of 100 X (old-1) still open with unrealized P&L. Fresh build: both rows on new-2, one round trip closed with its P&L, no position, no Beyond. `Engine::differences` is non-empty; the same happens on a part (the reverse), where only contract records are re-derived.
findings.required_change: On any `instrument_joins` write, the delta must name (and re-read) every record whose transactions name either side of the join, every trade anchored on either side, and every contract whose terms name either side as underlying — or the triggers on `instrument_joins` must write `record` keys for those records (e.g. `INSERT INTO ledger_changes SELECT 'record', record_id FROM transactions WHERE instrument_id IN (NEW.instrument_id, NEW.into_id)`) plus `trade` keys for the trades and `instrument` keys for the contracts. Add a join and a part to the property test's write sequence (acceptance criterion at plan line 128 does not list them).

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it. The engine's ledger is read from the book with the joins already applied: `engine_inputs::ledger` (server/src/engine_inputs.rs:53, :57, :36) calls `book.transactions()` → `transactions_where(.., Read::AsBook)`, whose instrument column is `COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)` over `LEFT JOIN instrument_joins` (book/src/records.rs:609-616); `book.trades()` reads the anchor as `COALESCE(j.into_id, anchor_instrument)` (book/src/trades.rs:287-288); `book.option_terms` canonicalises `terms.underlying` through the join (book/src/identity.rs:423-430). The engine itself has no notion of joins (grep of engine/src for joins/canonical finds only round-trip "joins", ledger.rs:806-920) and keys every holding by `(account, instrument)` as handed to it. `settle_successions` (identity.rs:707-726) rewrites `instrument_joins` (delete all, reinsert) and touches `transactions`/`trades`/`option_terms` for nothing; on a part it only sets `derived_version = 0` on contract records naming either underlying (:720-726), never on the share records. It runs after every store (records.rs:123, :147, :463, :495), on a standing/holdings write with no record (identity.rs:487, broker/src/pull.rs:383), and in repairs (identity.rs:840). Under the plan, the trigger on `instrument_joins` writes kind `instrument` (plan line 73) and an `instrument` key is re-read through `Book::instruments_by_id` (line 82) - the instrument row, its names and terms - not the transactions or trades that now read on a different id. The five couplings (lines 90-95) describe which held transactions are re-matched; re-matching cannot fix a held `Transaction.instrument` that is stale. The property test's write list (line 128) has no succession join or part and its generated books have no retired-by-event standings, so the "right to refuse" clause (line 148) would not fire. Two corrections to the finding's own scenario, which do not rescue the plan: (1) the head of a join is the instrument first seen (identity.rs:692-705), so the row is (new-2 → old-1), not (old-1 → new-2); (2) when the sale is stored in the same write that makes the join, its `record` key is re-read AsBook after commit and comes out on old-1, so that exact sequence matches a fresh build. The failure needs the re-pointed rows to have been stored before the join write, which is the ordinary case: a sale stored under the live id in one pull and the retired standing arriving with a later record or a holdings read; or the reverse, a part, which the repository's own test exercises (book/tests/successions.rs:223-234: buy under OLD, sell under NEW, joined; then the event row arrives and parts them). In that part case the log carries `record <event>` and the `instrument` keys only; the engine keeps the sale on the joined head while a fresh build reads it on NEW, giving a Beyond of 400 on OLD and 1000 held on NEW against the fresh build's 0 and 600. Wrong positions, a phantom "took more than the book held" problem (server/src/status.rs:214) and wrong realized P&L shown until a restart.

verdicts.why: The mechanism is real and the plan does not handle it. `transactions_where` (records.rs:608-617) and `trades_where` (trades.rs:285-288) read the instrument as `COALESCE(j.into_id, …)` through `instrument_joins`, and `option_terms` (identity.rs:423-430) canonicalises the underlying the same way; the engine has no join map of its own (`Ledger.transactions: Vec<Transaction>`, input.rs:68-82; `match_lots` keys lots on `t.instrument`, ledger.rs:2162-2214). `settle_successions` (identity.rs:707-726) rewrites `instrument_joins` without touching `transactions` or `trades`, and resets `derived_version` only for contract records, only on a part. The plan routes `instrument_joins` to an `instrument` key (line 73), reads named things by key with transactions keyed by record (lines 82, 88), and its families (line 97) are built over the engine's held transactions, which still carry the stale id — so rematching the family does not help. The property test's generator and write list (line 128) have no retired standing, join or part. One detail of the finding's literal scenario is wrong: the head is the instrument first seen (identity.rs:692-705), so the join maps new-2 into old-1, and when the join and the only new row arrive in the same pull the keyed re-read of that new record lands it on old-1 already, and nothing diverges. But the part the finding also names diverges in one later pull, and a join whose retired standing arrives after rows under both ids exist diverges the same way. Corrected failing scenario: pull 1 stores buy 1,000 under old-1; pull 2 stores sell 400 under new-2 with old-1 stated retired-by-event → joined, engine and fresh both read the sale on old-1 (correct). Pull 3 brings the event row (−1,000 old-1, +1,000 new-2): `event_gives_up` (identity.rs:733-739) parts them (:711-716), log = `record <event>`, `instrument new-2`. Incremental engine: the sale is never re-read, stays on old-1 → old-1 1,000 −1,000 −400 = `Beyond { qty: 400 }` ("took 400 more than the book held", server/src/status.rs:214) and 1,000 of new-2 shown open; fresh build: old-1 closed by the event, new-2 600 open, no Beyond. `Engine::differences` (engine.rs:644) is non-empty and the page shows the wrong position until restart. The successions test header (book/tests/successions.rs:5-7) states this arrival order is supported. The required change (record/trade/contract keys for everything naming either side of a join, and a join and a part in the property test's writes) is the right one; the trade anchor (trades.rs:287) and `terms.underlying` (identity.rs:429) have the same gap.

findings.title: A multi-leg record naming no instrument is not a cash-only row: it taints every holding of its account, and the plan files it in the unmatched cash family
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1289-1317 (`apply`: a `leg-unstated` record with `t.instrument == None` sets `account_taint` at :1309-1312 and taints every book of the account), rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:840-849 (`book()` merges `account_taint` into every holding touched afterwards); plan line 97 ("Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only") against line 95 (coupling 5).
findings.claim: The plan's family rule and its cash-family rule contradict each other for the one row kind that drives coupling 5. A no-instrument transaction whose record carries the `leg-unstated` problem is applied by `match_lots` (it is in `txs`, it reaches `apply`, and it writes `account_taint`), and from its day on every holding the account touches carries `LegUnstated`. If such rows live in a per-account "cash family" that is only summed for cash totals and never passed through `apply`, or if a family match for instrument X in account A does not include that row in its transaction set, the taint is never set and every figure of the account loses its gap.
findings.failing_scenario: The shared case `engine/tests/cases/multileg.json` #2: A buys 100 X (a1), a leg-unstated row a2 in A names no instrument, A sells 100 X (a3). Fresh build: A's round trip has `pnl: {gaps: ["leg-unstated"]}`. Incremental: the sale a3 arrives; the change reaches family(X); if a2 is in A's cash family and not matched with X's family, `account_taint` is empty when a3 is applied and the trade shows `pnl 100.00`. The reverse also fails: a2 added later reaches only the cash family, the cash total moves, and no holding of A gains the gap; removing a2 (or its `record_problems` row) must likewise split the account-wide family again.
findings.required_change: State the rule precisely: a no-instrument record carrying `leg-unstated` makes its whole account one family, and that family's transaction set includes the account's no-instrument rows (at least the tainting one) so `apply` runs over it. The `record_problems` trigger (plan line 72) must cause a family recomputation, since the problem row, not the transaction, decides the coupling. Add the multileg.json #2 shape (add, then remove, the no-instrument multi-leg row) to the property test's writes.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's text is self-contradictory for this one row kind. On master, `apply` (rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1289-1317) treats a `leg-unstated` record naming no instrument by setting `account_taint` (:1310) and tainting every book the account holds (:1311, :1314-1316); `book()` (:840-849) merges that taint into every later holding of the account. Cash totals are a separate pass (:2244-2251) that never goes through `apply`, so the plan's line 97 sentence "Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only" is true for every no-instrument row except the one that drives coupling 5 (line 95). The plan says "plus the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint" but never says that family's transaction set includes the account's no-instrument rows, nor that a `record_problems` change (logged as kind `record`, line 72) must re-derive the family topology. Built as written, matching X's family on a3's arrival runs `apply` over X's rows without a2, `account_taint` stays empty, and multileg.json #2's A trip shows `pnl 100.00` instead of `gaps: ["leg-unstated"]`; adding or removing a2 later reaches only the cash family and no holding gains or loses the gap. Not refuted. Severity lowered to low because the plan's own gate catches it before merge: acceptance criterion line 128 generates books with "a multi-leg order naming no instrument", applies insert/revise/remove writes, and holds equality with a fresh build after every step, and line 148 commits to adding any coupling the property test exposes to the families. The finding's third required change (the test shape) is thus already mostly in the plan; what remains is making line 97 state that a no-instrument leg-unstated row joins (and its problem row decides) the account-wide family and is in the transactions that family's match runs over.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1289 `let multi_leg = self.inputs.ledger.records.get(&t.id.record).is_some_and(|r| r.problems.iter().any(|p| p.code == "leg-unstated"));` ... :1309-1312 `None => { self.account_taint.entry(account).or_default().merge(&gaps); self.out.books.keys().filter(|(a, _)| *a == account).map(|(_, i)| *i).collect() }` ... :1314-1317 taints each and `return self.unapplied(t, gaps);`. :1319 `let Some(instrument) = t.instrument else { return };` (a no-instrument row without the problem does nothing). :840-849 `book()`: `let whole = self.account_taint.get(&account).cloned(); ... for g in [under, own, whole] ... book.taint.merge(&g);`. :2244-2251 cash totals summed over `ledger.transactions` outside `apply`. :2142-2143, :2202-2242 `match_lots` applies every transaction in order with no special path for no-instrument rows. rust/crates/engine/tests/cases/multileg.json #2 expects `{"opened_by": "a1", "pnl": {"gaps": ["leg-unstated"]}}` with a2 = `{"account": "A", "kind": "buy", "cash": "-30", "problems": ["leg-unstated"]}` naming no instrument. Plan line 95 lists coupling 5 (`account_taint`); line 97: "a family is a set of instruments joined by any of the first three, extended by the fourth across accounts. Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only." Line 72 logs `record_problems` as kind `record`. Line 128: property test books include "a multi-leg order naming no instrument" and hold `Engine::differences` against `Engine::build` after every write; line 148: a coupling the property test exposes "is added to the families, never worked around".

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's text is contradictory for exactly the row that drives coupling 5. On master, `match_lots` (rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2142-2143) puts every transaction of the ledger into `txs`, instrument or not, and runs each through `apply` (:2229/:2239). In `apply` (:1289-1317), a transaction whose record carries a `leg-unstated` problem and whose `t.instrument` is `None` writes `account_taint` (:1310) and taints every book of the account already open (:1311, :1314-1316); `book()` (:840-849) then merges `account_taint` into every holding of that account touched afterwards. Only a no-instrument row WITHOUT `leg-unstated` is cash-only (:1319 `let Some(instrument) = t.instrument else { return }`, with the cash sum at :2244-2251). The producer confirms the shape is real: rust/crates/book/src/import/mapping.rs:338-356 emits `leg-unstated` for any MULTILEG row, including one whose instrument lookup returned `None`. The shared case rust/crates/engine/tests/cases/multileg.json #2 ("a multi-leg order whose row names nothing: everything the account holds waits, and only that account") is exactly the finding's scenario: a1 buys 100 X in A, a2 is a no-instrument `leg-unstated` row in A, a3 sells; expected `opened_by: a1, pnl: {gaps: [leg-unstated]}` while B's trade is `100.00`. The plan (line 95) lists `account_taint` as coupling 5 and line 97 says families include "the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint", but the same paragraph then states "Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only", and "a change reaches the families of every transaction ... it names". Built as written, a2 (and a change to its `record_problems` row, logged under kind `record` at line 72) reaches only A's cash family, whose match produces cash totals; `account_taint` is never set and a3's family match for X gives pnl 100.00 where a fresh build gives a gap. The plan nowhere says which family the tainting no-instrument row belongs to, that the account-wide family's transaction set includes it so `apply` runs over it, or that a `record_problems` change recomputes families. The finding is not refuted by "the plan handles it": the plan names the coupling and contradicts its mechanism in the next sentence. Severity stays medium rather than high because acceptance criterion line 128 includes "a multi-leg order naming no instrument" in the generated books, so the property test would likely expose the wrong figure if its writes add and remove that row, and the "Right to refuse" (line 148) commits to adding the coupling, but the design text as written would steer the build wrong and the test's coverage of adding/removing the row (and of its `record_problems` row alone) is not stated.

findings.title: A saved group that spans families must be rebuilt when any of its trips is rematched
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:305-326 (groups collapse the slices and open lots of every member trip into one `TradeKey::Group` figure and mark those trips `used`), :327-338 (a used trip emits no figure of its own), rust/crates/core/src/journal.rs:84 (`Group.members: Vec<TradeId>`); plan line 101 ("`build_trades` … take the families (or their trips …) to build").
findings.claim: A group's members are trade ids whose round trips can be on unrelated instruments in unrelated accounts; nothing in the match couples them, so a change to one trip's family must still rebuild the group figure that pools it. If keyed derivation rebuilds only `TradeKey::Trip` entries of the recomputed families, the group's `TradeFig` (its slices, qty, pnl, pnl_cad, status, last_on) stays as it was, and the trip's own figure is not emitted because the trip is `used`, so the page keeps showing the stale group.
findings.failing_scenario: Group G = {T1 (trip on X in account A), T2 (trip on Y in account B)}, both open. A sale of 100 X is added. Fresh build: G's figure has a new slice, `pnl` includes the X sale, `status` may turn Closed. Incremental: family(X) is rematched; `build_trades` for family(X)'s trips skips the X trip as `used` and never touches `TradeKey::Group(G)` → G's `pnl` and `slices` are the old ones; `Moved` reports nothing for G. `Engine::differences` against a fresh build is non-empty on `Trade(Group(G))`.
findings.required_change: Keyed `build_trades` rebuilds, for every recomputed trip, each group whose members include that trip's trade (`identity.trade_of`), and does the same when `settle_trades` changes which trade a trip carries (a trip joining or leaving a group). Add a group spanning two accounts/instruments to the property test's generated books (plan line 128 lists groups nowhere).

verdicts.why: The finding holds. On master a saved group is an arbitrary list of trade ids (rust/crates/core/src/journal.rs:84; trade_group_members(group_id, position, trade_id) in rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:421-425 has no account or instrument constraint; SPEC.md line 51 says a saved group joins "any trades"). build_trades (rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:305-326) resolves each member via identity.trade_of to a TripKey, pools every member trip's slices and open lots into one TradeKey::Group figure, marks the trips used, and then skips a used trip at :327-331 so it emits no TradeKey::Trip figure. Nothing in match_lots or identify references groups (no "group" in rust/crates/engine/src/identity.rs), so the plan's five couplings at plan lines 90-97 cannot bring a group's other members' instruments into the family a change reaches. The plan's derivation section (line 101) says build_trades takes "the families (or their trips…)" and that the trades collection is held by key with "only the recomputed entries compared"; it never says a group is rebuilt when any member trip's family is rematched, and settle_trades (plan line 107; figures.rs:74-119 moves, opens and orphans trade ids, which is what a group member points at) is likewise scoped to "the round trips the change produced or moved" without naming the groups those trades sit in. The acceptance tests cannot catch it: the property test's generated books (plan line 128) list no groups, and the existing each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would runs on tests_common::pulled_book, which creates no group (no "group" in rust/crates/server/src/tests_common.rs); the plan's right-to-refuse clause (line 148) only triggers when the property test shows a coupling. Scenario: G = {T1 on X in account A, T2 on Y in account B}; a sale of X is written; family(X) is rematched and X's trip gets a new slice; a keyed build over family(X)'s trips either skips X's trip as used (group figure untouched) or, if it does not consult used, emits a duplicate TradeKey::Trip figure beside the stale group; either way Engine::differences against Engine::build is non-empty on Trade(Group(G)) (pnl, pnl_cad, slices, status, last_on), and the Trades page shows the group's old P&L and status until a restart. Severity stays medium: on master groups are created only by the old-app import (add_group is called only from rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:277), so the population is imported books, but for those the page shows a wrong figure that the suite would not detect.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:305-326 (group collapse over identity.trade_of, used.extend(trips)); :327-331 (`if used.contains(key) … continue` — a used trip emits no figure); rust/crates/core/src/journal.rs:81-85 (Group { id, locked, members: Vec<TradeId> }); rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408-429 (add_group inserts members with no account/instrument check); SPEC.md:51 ("a saved group joins them, as it does any trades"); rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:290-294 and :448-461 (today rematch/Change::Trades/Change::Groups rebuild every trade, which the plan replaces with keyed builds); rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:74-119 (settle_trades moves/opens/orphans trade ids); rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:589-595 and :612-614 (same_as_fresh over pulled_book, which has no groups); plan lines 90-97 (five couplings, none a group), 101 (build_trades takes families/trips, trades held by key), 107 (settle_trades by key), 128 (property test's books: no groups), 148 (refusal only on what the property test shows).

verdicts.why:
The finding stands. The code does what it says: `build_trades` (rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:305-326) maps each group member's TradeId to its TripKey via `identity.trade_of`, pools every member trip's slices and open lots into one `TradeKey::Group(g.id)` figure through `collapse`, and marks those trips `used`; the per-trip loop (:327-338) then skips a used trip, so a trip in a group emits no figure of its own. `Group.members` is a plain `Vec<TradeId>` (rust/crates/core/src/journal.rs:84); `Book::add_group` (rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408-429) and the legacy import's `import_groups` (rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:262-280) place no constraint on members sharing an instrument or account, `TradeFig.instruments: Vec<InstrumentId>` (trades.rs:56) is designed for a multi-instrument trade, `collapse` does not reject mixed instruments (it names the figure after the first trip's last instrument, :183-188), and SPEC.md line 51 says a saved group joins "any trades". So a group spanning two families is a legal, designed state.

The plan does not handle it. Its five couplings under "What a change can reach" (plan lines 90-97) are coin places/last price per instrument, contract-underlying, corporate-event legs, transfer links and account-wide taint; a saved group is not among them, and nothing in `match_lots` couples two trips because a group pools them. Line 101 says `build_trades` takes "the families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts) to build" and that "only the recomputed entries are compared": a change to family(X) recomputes X's trips, finds the X trip `used`, and never recomputes `TradeKey::Group(G)`, so G's `slices`, `qty`, `pnl`, `pnl_cad`, `status`, `last_on` and `closed` stay as they were and `Moved` reports nothing for G. Line 30's keyed rebuild for `Change::Groups` covers a change to the group's own rows, not a record change reaching a group. The acceptance property test (line 128) lists no groups among the generated books, and the fixture behind the existing `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` (`tests_common::pulled_book`) seeds no group; the engine's `every_change_equals_a_fresh_build_and_says_what_moved` (rust/crates/engine/tests/changes.rs:153-155, 181-187) applies the ledger change to a base that has no group (the group arrives as a separate change applied to the same base), so no test named in the plan can catch the stale group. `Engine::differences` compares trades by `Entity::Trade(t.key)` (engine.rs:232-234, 609-611, 644-652), so the failing scenario would surface exactly as the finding says: a non-empty difference on `Trade(Group(G))`.

Severity stays medium: in this port groups are created only by the legacy import (no server route or page call creates one; `add_group` has one caller, import/mod.rs:277), so only owners whose old-app groups span instruments or accounts are affected, but for them the page would silently show a stale trade figure after every record change touching one member until a restart, with nothing to show it.

SPEC.md:51 "a saved group joins them, as it does any trades". findings.title: A record's legs on uncoupled instruments: `record_rank`, `by_record` and the single-leg test are computed from the family subset, not the whole record
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2137-2143 (`by_record` from the transactions matched; `record_rank(&by_record[..])` feeds `order_key`), :690-700 (`record_rank` is over every leg of the record), :2211-2216 (an `Effect::Open` pulls a same-instant close forward only when `by_record[close.record].len() == 1`), :2193-2242 (a one-day record's legs are applied together at the first leg's place); rust/crates/wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:692-715 (a corporate-action record with a given-up leg on one instrument and received legs on others; the adjustment at :722-731 is drafted only for `continues` cases) and :950-995 (a move record with one `move-n` leg per instrument moved); plan line 99 ("runs exactly as today over their transactions only, in the same order").
findings.claim: A record is a unit of ordering: every leg's sort key carries the rank of the whole record, a close is pulled before an open only for single-leg records, and a one-day record is applied as one order. Wealthsimple produces records whose legs name instruments none of the five couplings join (a merger's given-up X and received Y before the person enters an adjustment; an account move's X, Y, Z). Matching family(X) over X's transactions only gives the X leg a different `record_rank` and makes it look single-leg, so its position among same-instant records, and the look-ahead, differ from the full match; for an untimed record the legs sit in different buckets (:680-687) and the family-alone leg is applied at its own bucket instead of the first leg's.
findings.failing_scenario: Timed: corporate-action record R at instant T with legs r/trade (X, −100, effect None) and r/receive-0 (Y, +50); no adjustment yet. Full match: `record_rank(R)` = 1 (a leg acquires), so R sorts before a sale S of 100 X at the same instant T (rank 2): the event takes the 100 units (`apply_event` without anchor, :1746-1750), S then finds nothing → `Beyond 100` on S, no closed trade. Family(X) alone: R's X leg alone ranks 2, ties with S, order falls to `source_key`; with S first the sale closes the lots with P&L and the event's take is `Beyond` on R instead. Untimed (what a generated book can produce): the +Y leg is bucket 0, the −X leg bucket 2; full match applies both before the day's timed sale of X (the sale is Beyond), family(X) applies the −X leg after it (the sale realizes P&L).
findings.required_change: Either make a record's legs a sixth coupling (all instruments one record names, with no instrument counted as the account's cash family and ignored), or keep `by_record`/`record_rank`/the `len() == 1` test over the whole record from the held `BTreeMap<RecordId, Vec<Transaction>>` while iterating only the family's legs — and then define the one-day loop on the family's subset of `in_order[record]`, which preserves relative order only when every leg of the record shares (date, bucket, at); an untimed multi-leg record still needs the coupling. Say which, and put a multi-leg record on two uncoupled instruments (timed and untimed) in the property test.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not cover it. On master, `match_lots` builds `by_record` from every transaction it is given (ledger.rs:2137-2140) and that map feeds three ordering decisions: `record_rank` over all legs of a record (ledger.rs:690-700, used at :2143), the `len() == 1` test that pulls a same-instant stated close before an open (:2214), and the `one_day` test that applies a multi-leg record as one order at its first leg's place (:2225-2240). The plan's §B says the family match "runs exactly as today over their transactions only, in the same order" (plan line 99) and lists five couplings (lines 90-96); its third coupling is the instruments a corporate event's legs name "(`event_groups`, `adjustments`)", and on master `event_groups` is formed only from `facts.adjustments` (ledger.rs:2180-2192), so a corporate-event record with no adjustment couples nothing. Wealthsimple produces exactly that: `corporate_action` (mapping.rs:685-716) drafts one given-up leg on the old security and one `receive-n` leg per security received, all timed (`Base::draft` sets `occurred_at: Some`, `effect: None`, mapping.rs:355-363), and drafts an adjustment only for `continues` sub-types (splits, symbol changes; mapping.rs:717-734), so a merger record R names X and Y with no adjustment. Walking the scenario: whole-record rank is 1 (the +Y leg acquires, :693); X's leg alone ranks 2; a plain DIY_SELL row has `effect: None` (only multi-leg order legs set an effect, mapping.rs:514-527) so it ranks 2. Full match sorts R before S at the same instant; `apply_event` with no anchor takes the units (:1746-1750) and S then finds no lots, so `apply_trade` lists S as `Beyond` with no closed trade (:1485-1496). Family(X) alone ties R's X leg with S and `source_key` decides; when S sorts first it closes the lots with realized P&L and R's take is `Beyond`. A realized P&L and a broker-check row differ from the fresh build. The untimed variant (`instant` buckets at :680-687: +Y in bucket 0, −X in bucket 2; full match applies both at the bucket-0 place via `one_day`, family(X) applies −X at bucket 2 after the day's timed sale) needs an untimed multi-leg record, which the pull does not produce (statement rows at statement.rs:275/314 are untimed but single-instrument); it is reachable from a generated or hand-entered book only. The plan's property test (line 128) generates "corporate events with their adjustments", which the third coupling joins, so as specified it cannot generate the uncoupled case and the "right to refuse" clause (line 148), which relies on that test, would not fire. Two caveats that narrow but do not refute it: the account-move record (mapping.rs:950-995) does not reproduce the difference, since its legs all go one way (`this_way`), so whole-record and single-leg ranks agree and the legs share a bucket with no other record between them; and the timed case needs a sale at the exact `occurredAt` of the corporate action, which is rare on a real book. Severity medium stands: when it occurs the figure is wrong with nothing to show it, and it is a design gap the plan has to state (keep `by_record`/`record_rank`/the single-leg test over the whole record, or add the record as a coupling), not something a reviewer can read as implied.
verdicts.evidence: ledger.rs:2137-2143 `by_record` built from `ledger.transactions`, `record_rank(&by_record[&t.id.record])` in the sort key; ledger.rs:690-700 `record_rank` returns 1 when any leg has effect None and acquires; ledger.rs:636-641 `acquires`: Sell → false, else sign of quantity; ledger.rs:2214 `by_record.get(..).is_some_and(|l| l.len() == 1)`; ledger.rs:2225-2240 `one_day = legs.len() > 1 && all same trade_date`, legs applied together from `in_order[record]`; ledger.rs:2180-2192 `event_groups` built only from `inputs.facts.adjustments`; ledger.rs:1728-1753 `apply_event` without anchor takes units via `take` and lists `beyond` on what is left; ledger.rs:1472-1496 a sale with no lots and effect None is `beyond`, no role closed; ledger.rs:680-687 `instant` buckets. mapping.rs:355-363 `Base::draft` sets `occurred_at: Some(self.occurred_at)`, `effect: None`; mapping.rs:685-716 corporate action drafts given-up leg on `old` and `receive-n` legs on other securities in one record; mapping.rs:717-734 adjustment drafted only when `continues` (CONSOLIDATION/SPLIT/.../SYMBOL_CHANGE), so a merger gets none; mapping.rs:514-527 only order legs set `d.effect`; mapping.rs:958-981 move legs filtered by `this_way` (one direction). statement.rs:275,314 `occurred_at: None` rows. Plan lines 90-97 (five couplings; third cites `event_groups`, `adjustments`), line 99 ("over their transactions only, in the same order"), line 128 (generator: "corporate events with their adjustments"), line 148 (right to refuse relies on the property test showing the coupling).

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle the case. `match_lots` (ledger.rs:2137-2143) builds `by_record` from `ledger.transactions` and feeds `record_rank(&by_record[record])` (:690-700, over every leg) into `order_key` (:660-676) as the fourth sort component; the one-day loop (:2225-2241) applies a multi-leg same-day record at its first leg's slot from `in_order[record]`, which is built from the sorted `txs` (:2197-2200); the look-ahead at :2214 tests `by_record[close.record].len() == 1`. The plan's five couplings (lines 91-95) join a corporate event's instruments only through `event_groups`/`adjustments`, and `event_groups` (:2180-2191) is seeded only from `inputs.facts.adjustments`, so a merger record (mapping.rs:685-716: one `row_leg` on the given-up X with `quantity = -given`, plus `receive-n` legs on Y) whose adjustment is not drafted (:717-718, only `continues` sub-kinds) leaves X and Y in separate families. Plan line 99 ("runs exactly as today over their transactions only") in its natural reading builds `by_record` from the family's subset; the X leg alone ranks 2 (`acquires` :636-641 gives Some(false) for a negative event quantity; no Open, no acquiring None-effect leg) where the whole record ranks 1 (the +Y leg acquires). A Sell of X at the same instant also ranks 2, so the tie falls to `source_key` (:675); when S's key sorts first, S closes X's lots into a trip (`apply_trade` :1473-1483) and the event's `take` at :1746 then reports `beyond` on R, whereas the full match applies R first (`take` moves the lots out, :1746-1747) and S finds nothing and is `beyond` (:1493-1496, a share with effect None may not open short). Even with `by_record` kept over the whole record, an untimed event record (possible from an import or the plan's generator; Wealthsimple always stamps `occurred_at`, mapping.rs:359) has its +Y leg in bucket 0 and −X leg in bucket 2 (:680-687); the full match applies both at bucket 0 via the one-day loop (`meets_opposite` :1525-1532 is false for events, so legs go in order), before any timed sale of X that day, while a family(X) iteration meets the −X leg at bucket 2 after the sale. The plan's safety net (line 148, "the property test would show it") does not reliably cover it: line 128 generates "corporate events with their adjustments" and the existing `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` (figures.rs:612-666) is a fixed scenario on a pulled fixture that removes one record, not a generator. One part of the claim does not hold: an account-move record (mapping.rs:958-995) is one-sided, every instrument leg the same direction and the same timestamp, so its rank and bucket are identical over any subset; its cash legs differ in rank/bucket but only feed the order-independent cash totals (:2244-2251). The corporate-action case alone carries the finding. Medium stands: a rare state on real data (an unexplained merger and a same-instant sale of the given-up instrument, or an untimed same-day event from an import), but a figure that differs from a fresh build against the plan's own first acceptance criterion, with no listed test case to catch it.
verdicts.evidence: ledger.rs:2137-2143 — `by_record` from `ledger.transactions`; `txs.sort_by_cached_key(|t| order_key(t, record_rank(&by_record[&t.id.record]), &key_of(t)))`. ledger.rs:690-700 — `record_rank` returns 0 if any leg is Open, 1 if any leg has effect None and `acquires == Some(true)`, 2 if any leg has effect None, else 3. ledger.rs:636-641 — `acquires`: Buy→Some(true), Sell→Some(false), else sign of a nonzero quantity (so a −X event leg is Some(false), a +Y receive leg Some(true)). ledger.rs:680-687 — bucket 0 for (None, Some(true)), 1 for timed, 2 for (None, other). ledger.rs:2197-2200 — `in_order` built from `txs`; :2225-2241 — one-day record applied at the first leg's place, `left = in_order[&t.id.record].clone()`, leg chosen by `meets_opposite` else position 0. ledger.rs:2214 — `by_record.get(&c.id.record).is_some_and(|l| l.len() == 1)`. ledger.rs:1525-1532 — `meets_opposite` false unless `Move::Trade(None | Some(Close))`. ledger.rs:2180-2191 — `event_groups` seeded only from `inputs.facts.adjustments`. ledger.rs:1728-1754 — no anchor: `take(account, instrument, q.abs())` then `moved_out`, `beyond` if `left` positive. ledger.rs:1473-1496 — a share Sell with effect None closing nothing is `beyond`. mapping.rs:685-716 — one record with the given-up leg (`quantity = given.abs().neg()`) on `old` and `receive-n` legs on the instruments the positions show arriving; :717-734 — the adjustment drafted only when `continues` (split/consolidation/code or name change). mapping.rs:359 — every Wealthsimple draft carries `occurred_at: Some(self.occurred_at)`. mapping.rs:958-995 — move legs all `this_way(q)` from `row.account`, so same direction and instant. Plan lines 91-97 — the five couplings and the family definition; line 99 — "runs exactly as today over their transactions only, in the same order"; line 128 — generator lists "corporate events with their adjustments"; line 148 — relies on the property test to reveal a missed coupling. figures.rs:612-666 — the existing test is a fixed fixture scenario, not a generator.

findings.title: The adjustment coupling must include the anchor row's own instrument, not only the legs' `from`/`to`
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2180-2192 (the anchor is grouped on itself at :2186 whatever its instrument; rows are grouped by `named`, the legs' instruments), :1728-1800 (`apply_event` runs in the anchor's `apply`, reading and writing the legs' books), rust/crates/book/src/person.rs:231-237 and rust/crates/server/src/entries.rs:225-236 (a spin-off entry's `parent` is the person's choice, not checked against the event row's instrument); plan line 93 ("the instruments a corporate event's legs name").
findings.claim: The anchor transaction is applied in the family of its own instrument, and that `apply` moves the legs' instruments. If the person's spin-off adjustment names a parent other than the event row's instrument, or a distribution adjustment's legs name another instrument, the anchor's family and the legs' families are distinct under coupling 3 as written, and matching one without the other either skips the legs' moves or writes into books that belong to another family's result.
findings.failing_scenario: Event row E on instrument P (waiting, `Wanted::Event`); the person enters SpinOff { event: E, parent: Q, children: [C] }. Family(P) is rematched for a later P sale: `apply_event(E)` runs `apply_leg` from Q to C — books (A,Q) and (A,C) are created in family(P)'s `Matched` slice and then replaced or ignored when family(Q∪C) is written, so C's lots appear twice or not at all; a fresh build has them once.
findings.required_change: Define the adjustment coupling as the union of `applies_to`'s transaction instrument and every leg's `from` and `to`, for every adjustment kind (corporate event, dividend return of capital, cost of arrival), or refuse an entry whose legs do not name the anchor row's instrument.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's wording does not cover it. On master the anchor row is grouped on itself whatever its instrument (ledger.rs:2186), apply_event runs when the anchor's own row is applied (ledger.rs:1332) and reads and writes the books of every leg's from/to (ledger.rs:1787-1799, 1809, 1813), and neither entries.rs:225-236 nor Book::enter (person.rs:344-357) checks that the spin-off's parent or children include the event row's instrument. Plan line 93 defines the third coupling as "the instruments a corporate event's legs name", line 97 joins instruments only by the listed couplings, and line 103 sends an adjustment change to "the families of the transactions the changed adjustments apply to": nothing joins the anchor's instrument P to the legs' Q and C. With family(P) matched alone (a later P sale), event_groups holds E, apply_event(E) finds Q's book empty in that slice, the spin-off leg (no units_per_unit, ledger.rs:1870-1878) errors EventUnknown and taints (A,Q) and (A,C) and marks E unapplied; family(Q,C)'s slice has no E, so C's lot from the spin-off never opens. A fresh build opens C's lot with Q's cost share. The figure differs; the finding's "twice or not at all" is the right conclusion though the mechanism is a bogus taint plus a missing lot. Reaching both families (line 97) does not fix it, since two separate slices still diverge; the join must be in the disjoint-set. The property test at line 128 does not say its generator makes an adjustment whose legs omit the anchor's instrument, so the right-to-refuse clause is not guaranteed to catch it. Severity stays low: the page's own form (web/src/lib/EventEntry.svelte:19-36) always sends the event row's instrument as the child, so the state is reachable only through the HTTP/MCP entry directly or an issuer-feed adjustment (facts.rs:252-258 names legs by ISIN independently of the anchor's row); the person's return-of-capital and cost-of-arrival entries set the leg to t.instrument (entries.rs:222-223, 243-244), so those kinds coincide through the person's path.
verdicts.evidence: ledger.rs:2180-2192 — `let named = adj.legs.iter().flat_map(|l| [l.from, l.to])...; m.event_groups.insert(anchor.id.clone(), anchor.id.clone());` (anchor grouped on itself regardless of its instrument; other rows by the legs' instruments). ledger.rs:1332 `Move::Event => return self.apply_event(t)` inside the anchor's own `apply`. ledger.rs:1787-1791 `for i in adjustment.legs.iter().filter_map(|l| l.from) { let lots = self.book(account, i).lots...` and 1792-1799 `self.apply_leg(account, &anchor, ...)` writing the legs' books; 1870-1878 spin-off leg needs `stated.get(&to)` or `held * units_per_unit`, else `unknown()`. entries.rs:225-236: `let parent = instrument_id(parent)?; currency_of(parent)?;` — no comparison with `t.instrument`. person.rs:344-357: `Entry::SpinOff` refuses only shares outside (0,1] and a total above 1. web/src/lib/EventEntry.svelte:21 `.filter((i) => ... i.id !== event.instrument)` and :36 `children: [{ instrument: event.instrument, ...}]` — the page always names the anchor's instrument, the API does not require it. book/tests/facts.rs:252-258 — an issuer-source adjustment names legs by ISIN on an `applies_to` row chosen independently. Plan line 93: "the instruments a corporate event's legs name (`event_groups`, `adjustments`)"; line 97: "a family is a set of instruments joined by any of the first three"; line 103: "`Change::Adjustments` reaches the families of the transactions the changed adjustments apply to"; line 128: the generator says only "corporate events with their adjustments".

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's coupling, as written, leaves the gap. ledger.rs:2186 groups the anchor on itself whatever its instrument; only same-day event rows are grouped by `named`, the legs' instruments (2185-2191). apply_event (1728-1800) runs when the anchor transaction is applied and reads and writes the books of the legs' `from`/`to` (1787-1799 via book()/basis_mut()), never the anchor's own instrument. A spin-off entry's parent and children are the person's choice: entries.rs:230-236 only parses the ids and checks currency_of(parent); person.rs:344-357 checks shares, never the event row's instrument. So an entry SpinOff { event: E on P, parent: Q, children: [C] } is accepted. Plan line 93 defines coupling 3 as "the instruments a corporate event's legs name" (Q, C), and line 103 says Change::Adjustments reaches "the families of the transactions the changed adjustments apply to" (family(P)); nothing joins P to Q∪C. Under that, a later C sale or Q buy rematches family(Q∪C) alone, whose transactions do not include E, so apply_event(E) never runs: C has no spin-off lots and Q's cost is unreduced, while a fresh build (Engine::build, which applies E after Q's buys) has them. A later P change rematches family(P) alone and runs apply_event(E) against an empty Q book, producing different lots again, written into books outside the family. Either way acceptance criterion line 128 ("equal to a fresh build, for every kind of change") fails. The plan's right-to-refuse (line 148) is a generic net conditioned on the property test generating a parent other than the event row's instrument, which line 128's generator description does not say it does, so the plan does not already handle it. I checked the other adjustment paths and they are sound: CostOfArrival's leg `to` is t.instrument (entries.rs:222-223) and apply_leg returns at 1805-1807 for from=None; ReturnOfCapital's leg from=to=t.instrument (entries.rs:243-244, applied by apply_distribution 2047-2056, dividend anchors skipped at 2182); the broker's own adjustment (wealthsimple mapping.rs:718-733) anchors on the row leg carrying `old`, which is leg.from, so the anchor's instrument is always in the legs there. Only the person's spin-off path produces the split, and it is a mis-entry the app accepts, so low severity is right: the fix is to define the coupling as applies_to's instrument ∪ every leg's from/to, or to refuse a spin-off whose legs omit the event row's instrument.

findings.title: Keying `beyond`, `stock_dividends`, `unit_disagreements` by transaction alone and `unapplied` by transaction drops rows a fresh build reports
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1949-1967 (`Beyond` pushed per `from` leg with the same anchor), :1832 (`StockDividend` per leg), :1520 (`UnitsDisagree` per leg/instrument), :1156-1158 with :1792-1799 (`unapplied` pushed once per failing leg of one anchor) and :1317/:1349/:1753; rust/crates/server/src/status.rs:206-215 (one status line per `Beyond`), rust/crates/server/src/compare.rs:497-503; plan line 99 ("a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about").
findings.claim: Several of these rows are produced more than once per transaction, one per instrument or per failing leg. A map keyed by transaction keeps the last and loses the rest, so the page's status and the comparison tool show fewer lines than a fresh build's list, and the property test comparing figures would not see it unless it compares `Matched` too.
findings.failing_scenario: An adjustment on anchor E with two cash legs, `from: X` and `from: Y`, each closing more than held: full match lists `Beyond{E, X, 5}` and `Beyond{E, Y, 3}` and status.rs prints two lines; keyed by `E` only one survives. An event whose two legs fail with different gaps lists `unapplied` twice; keyed by `E` one gap set is lost and compare.rs:497 counts it differently.
findings.required_change: Key these by (transaction, instrument) and merge `unapplied`'s gaps per transaction (or key by (transaction, leg index)); compare `Matched` as well as the figures in the equality property test.

verdicts.why: The finding stands on the code. On master every collection the plan's line 99 turns into "a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about" is a Vec that can hold several rows sharing either key: ledger.rs:1792-1799 loops an adjustment's legs and calls `self.unapplied(t, g)` once per failing leg of one anchor (1156-1158 pushes `(t.id, gaps)` with no merge); apply_leg pushes `Beyond` (1965), `StockDividend` (1832) and `UnitsDisagree` (1520, via check_units) per leg with the same `anchor` and the leg's own `from`, and nothing restricts an adjustment's legs to one `from` (facts.rs:430-449 stores legs as given; ledger.rs:2185-2190 builds the event group from the `named` set of every leg's from/to, so multi-instrument events are designed in). Under the other reading, keyed by holding, the non-event helper `beyond` (1200-1205) pushes one row per transaction on the same (account, instrument), so two sales each taking more than held on one holding give two rows that a holding-keyed map collapses to one — a more ordinary scenario than the one the finding gives, and the same defect. The rows are page-visible: status.rs:118 extends the header's `sources` with `broker_failures`, whose 206-215 prints one line per `Beyond`; compare.rs:497-505 counts `unapplied` and lists `beyond` per row. `Engine::compare` (engine.rs:609-640) diffs trades, positions, cash, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, brokers and the book figure, never `Matched`, so the acceptance criterion "equal to a fresh build" (plan line 128) cannot see the loss; and because a fresh build under the plan would use the same map, the plan's own claim that "Nothing on screen changes" (line 36) is unguarded by any listed test. The plan does not handle it: "(or holding)" names a choice of single key, not a composite one. Severity low is right: what is lost is header lines and the comparison tool's counts; the one figure touched, dividend income from `stock_dividends` (cashflow.rs:83-96), needs a multi-`from` stock-dividend adjustment that no person-entry path in person.rs produces, and master already keys those cash rows by transaction id (`Entity::CashRow(r.id)`, engine.rs:617), so two per anchor collide there today. Two corrections to the finding's remedy: `(transaction, instrument)` still collapses two rows the holding reading would keep apart only if it includes the transaction, so the key must carry both; and adding `Matched` to the equality property test would not catch this, since both sides would use the map — a shared case carrying two rows under one key (checked as a count, not the BTreeSet of labels cases.rs:814/826 collapses to), or a status-line test, would.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:323-344 (`Matched.beyond`, `stock_dividends`, `unit_disagreements`, `unapplied` are Vecs); :1156-1158 (`unapplied` pushes `(t.id, gaps)` unmerged); :1792-1799 (`for leg in &adjustment.legs { if let Err(g) = self.apply_leg(..) { .. self.unapplied(t, g); } }`, one push per failing leg of one anchor); :1965 (`self.out.beyond.push(Beyond { transaction: anchor.clone(), account, instrument: from, qty: left })` inside apply_leg, per leg); :1832 (`stock_dividends.push(StockDividend { transaction: anchor.clone(), .. instrument: from, .. })` per leg); :1520 (`unit_disagreements.push(UnitsDisagree { transaction: anchor.clone(), .. instrument, .. })` per leg); :1200-1205 (`beyond` helper pushes one row per transaction on a holding, so two transactions on one holding give two rows sharing the holding key); :2185-2190 (`named` built from every leg's from/to, event rows of several instruments grouped under one anchor); rust/crates/book/src/facts.rs:430-449 (legs stored as given, no single-`from` rule); rust/crates/server/src/status.rs:118 (`sources.extend(app.figures.get().and_then(|f| f.read(broker_failures)))`, the page header) and :206-215 (one line per `Beyond`); rust/crates/server/src/compare.rs:497-505 (per-row counts of `unapplied` and `beyond`); rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:609-640 (`compare` covers no `Matched` collection) and :644-652 (`differences` uses it); rust/crates/engine/src/cashflow.rs:83-96 (a CashRow per StockDividend, id = the anchor); rust/crates/engine/tests/cases.rs:814, 826 (`beyond`/`unit_disagreements` checked as BTreeSet of labels, which already collapses duplicates per transaction). Plan: docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md line 99 ("every collection in `Matched` that is a list today ... becomes a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about"), line 36 ("Nothing on screen changes"), line 128 (equality held through `Engine::differences`).

verdicts.why: The plan's line 99 names a single key ("a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about") for collections that master produces more than once per transaction, and neither reading of that key is unique. On master one anchor can push several `Beyond` (one per cash-merger leg, ledger.rs:1949-1966; plus the fill paths at :1384/:1398/:1407/:1496/:1590/:1688 keyed on `t.id`), several `UnitsDisagree` (one per child `to` of a spin-off, :1871-1875 via `check_units` :1520; and per `from` :1822/:1844), several `StockDividend` (:1832, per leg), and several `unapplied` entries (:1792-1799 pushes once per failing leg of the same anchor; `unapplied()` at :1156 is a plain push). The leg model admits any number of legs under one anchor with any `from`/`to` (core/src/adjustment.rs:26-48; facts.rs:426-474 writes whatever drafts come, no uniqueness on `from`). A map by transaction keeps the last entry per anchor; a map by holding is worse for `Beyond` (every sale of a holding with missing early history closes beyond held, so one holding routinely carries several Beyond on different transactions). Observable effect: status.rs:206-215 prints one header line per `Beyond` entry with its instrument, so an anchor with two cash legs each beyond held loses a line; cashflow.rs:83-97 makes one CashRow per `StockDividend`, so a two-leg stock dividend loses an income row (a figure); compare.rs:497-502 counts `unapplied` words per entry. None of these is caught by the plan's acceptance test: both `same_as_fresh` (figures.rs:589-595) and the planned property test (plan line 128) hold `Engine::differences`, which runs `compare` over a `Snapshot` of trades/positions/cash/payers/equity/checks/benchmarks/brokers/book (engine.rs:609-640, 644-652, 695-705) and never `matched`; and on the branch the fresh build would populate the same map and collapse identically, so even comparing `Matched` between branch-fresh and branch-incremental would not expose the loss against master. No shared case carries an adjustment with two `from` legs or two children, and none asserts `beyond` at all (tests/cases: no "beyond" key), so the suite is silent too. The plan also claims "Nothing on screen changes" (line 36). Severity stays low: the page-visible drops need a one-anchor event with two cash legs on different instruments or two stock-dividend legs, both contrived; `unit_disagreements` has no page reader (only cases.rs:826, which already collapses to a set by label), and `unapplied` reaches only the comparison tool's count (compare.rs:497) and cases.rs:819 (already a BTreeMap by label). The fix is small: key by (transaction, instrument) or (transaction, leg index), merge `unapplied` gaps per transaction. One caveat on the finding's required change: "compare Matched in the equality property test" would not by itself catch this, since both sides on the branch would use the same lossy map; a test must assert the count against the leg count or against master's list shape.

`Beyond`/`UnitsDisagree`/`StockDividend` (:203-257) each carry `transaction` + `account` + `instrument`, i.e. the natural key is (transaction, instrument), not transaction. ledger.rs:1792-1799: `for leg in &adjustment.legs { if let Err(g) = self.apply_leg(...) { ...; findings.title: The log's seq restarts at 1 after the start's prune, so the holder's kept seq skips every later change
findings.where: Plan lines 68 (`seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`, no AUTOINCREMENT) and 82 ("built from the book as it stands at MAX(seq), and rows at or below that are deleted"; the holder "keeps the highest seq it has applied"); line 139 (`Book::clear` empties the log). Code: rust/crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:27-50 (open_db sets no pragma that changes rowid assignment), rust/crates/book/schema/v27.sql:315 (the one table that uses AUTOINCREMENT, `notifications`), rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:176-191 and 196-205 and 362-368 (the three builds), rust/crates/server/src/clear.rs:155-177 (clear, then rebuild).
findings.claim: Without AUTOINCREMENT SQLite gives a new row max(rowid)+1, and 1 when the table is empty. The plan prunes every row at or below MAX(seq) at a start, which empties the table, while the holder keeps that MAX as its applied seq. The first write after the start gets seq 1, and `SELECT ... WHERE seq > <MAX>` returns nothing until as many changes have been written as were pruned; those changes are never applied. The same happens after Clear data (the log emptied, then `rebuild` reads MAX of an emptied table) and at the first `state_zone` build, and it would happen on any mid-run prune the plan later adds.
findings.failing_scenario: A book whose log holds 300 rows at a start. The start builds whole, sets the holder to 300 and deletes the 300 rows. The person adds a trade (entries.rs:259 -> record_changed): the trigger writes seq 1; the reader runs `WHERE seq > 300`, reads nothing, applies nothing; the trade is in the book and absent from every figure. The next 299 changes (pulls, imports, journal) are the same. The 301st is applied alone, its predecessors lost until the next restart rebuilds whole.
findings.required_change: Declare `seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` so `sqlite_sequence` keeps the high-water mark across deletes (the precedent is `notifications`, v27.sql:315), and read the holder's seq from the same snapshot as the build's whole read (see the next finding). With that, the prune at a start, the prune in `Book::clear` (done last in its transaction, after the per-row DELETE triggers have written their rows) and any periodic prune of rows at or below the holder are all safe. Add a test: start, prune, one write, one `record_changed`, the figure moves.

verdicts.why: The finding holds for the start path as the plan is written. Plan line 68 declares `ledger_changes (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ...)` with no AUTOINCREMENT; line 82 says the start builds whole "from the book as it stands at MAX(seq), and rows at or below that are deleted", and the holder "keeps the highest seq it has applied". Nothing in the plan resets the holder after the prune or mentions `sqlite_sequence` (grep of the plan for reset/sqlite_sequence/zero: no hits). Without AUTOINCREMENT, SQLite assigns a new rowid of max(rowid)+1, or 1 when the table is empty, so after the prune empties the table the next trigger write gets seq 1 while the holder is N; `WHERE seq > N` returns nothing until N+1 rows have been written. I reproduced this with sqlite3: 300 rows, prune at MAX=300, next insert gets seq 1 and `count(*) WHERE seq>300` is 0; the same with AUTOINCREMENT gives seq 301 and count 1. The precedent the finding cites is real: `notifications` is the one table in v27.sql using AUTOINCREMENT (line 315). The code paths cited exist: `Figures::open` builds whole at figures.rs:185-189, `rebuild` at 196-205, `state_zone`'s first build at 362-368, and `entries.rs:259` calls `record_changed`, which under the plan becomes the log reader. The acceptance-criteria property test (plan line 128) applies writes and compares against fresh builds without ever performing a start's prune, so it would not catch this. One sub-claim is weaker than stated: the Clear data case (clear.rs:155 then rebuild at :177) depends on whether `Book::clear` empties the log before or after the other tables' DELETE triggers fire; if the log is emptied last, MAX(seq) is NULL, the holder would start at 0 and the path is fine. The plan does not specify that order (line 139 only says clear "empties the log"), so that part is plausible rather than confirmed, but the start path alone is a confirmed, silent loss of every write to the figures, so high stands.
verdicts.evidence: Plan: line 68 `ledger_changes (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL, key TEXT NOT NULL)`; line 82 "built whole, as now, from the book as it stands at MAX(seq), and rows at or below that are deleted" / "keeps the highest seq it has applied" / "SELECT kind, key FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq > ?"; line 139 "Book::clear (clear.rs) empties the log with the record"; no mention anywhere of resetting the holder's seq or of sqlite_sequence. Code on master d6824aa7: rust/crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:27-52 open_db_hooked sets only journal_mode/synchronous, nothing affecting rowid assignment; rust/crates/book/schema/v27.sql:315 `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` on notifications (the only AUTOINCREMENT in the schema; lines 186, 266, 411 are plain INTEGER PRIMARY KEY); rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:185-189 (start build), 196-205 (rebuild after clear), 362-368 (state_zone first build), 411-413 record_changed -> pulled, 420-461 pulled reading the whole ledger today; rust/crates/server/src/clear.rs:155 book.clear then :177 f.rebuild; rust/crates/server/src/entries.rs:259 `f.record_changed(now)`. Empirical check (python3 -I, sqlite3): table without AUTOINCREMENT, 300 inserts, DELETE WHERE seq<=300, next INSERT gets seq 1, `SELECT count(*) WHERE seq>300` = 0; with AUTOINCREMENT the next INSERT gets 301 and the count is 1; MAX(seq) of an empty table is NULL.

verdicts.why: The finding stands. The plan (line 68) declares `ledger_changes (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, ...)` with no AUTOINCREMENT, and line 82 specifies both halves of the failure together: the holder "keeps the highest seq it has applied", the start builds "from the book as it stands at MAX(seq), and rows at or below that are deleted", and a change reads `WHERE seq > ?`. Nothing in the plan resets the holder after the prune, and nothing in `open_db` (rust/crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:19-53) changes rowid assignment. SQLite's documented rule for a rowid table without AUTOINCREMENT is max(rowid)+1, and 1 for an empty table; I reproduced it: three rows, `MAX(seq)`=3, `DELETE WHERE seq <= 3`, one insert gets seq 1, and `SELECT count(*) WHERE seq > 3` is 0, while the same table declared AUTOINCREMENT gives the new row seq 4. So on any book whose log holds N rows at a start, the N writes after that start are written by the triggers and never read by `Figures`; the trade added at entries.rs -> record_changed is in the book and absent from every figure until the next restart's whole build. The same rule applied at the first `state_zone` build (figures.rs:362-368) has the same effect. The Clear-data path (clear.rs:155 then :177 `rebuild`) is only wrong if the holder is left at its old value when the emptied log's MAX is NULL, which the plan does not settle either way, so that part is plausible rather than certain; the start case alone is sufficient and high. None of the acceptance criteria can catch it: the property test (line 128) starts from an empty book with no restart and no prune; the owner's-book criterion (line 134) and the `add-trade` capacity probe (capacity.rs:584-590) time the entry and do not check the figure moved; the trigger test (line 130) does not exercise a prune.
verdicts.evidence: Plan: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Bagholder/d40edf86-5d80-558d-b87f-f87f9ea4ccf4/scratchpad/p506/docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md line 68 "A table `ledger_changes (seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL, key TEXT NOT NULL)`"; line 82 "The engine's holder (`Figures`) keeps the highest `seq` it has applied. At a start the engine is built whole, as now, from the book as it stands at `MAX(seq)`, and rows at or below that are deleted ... A change reads `SELECT kind, key FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq > ?`"; line 139 "`Book::clear` (`clear.rs`) empties the log with the record". Code: rust/crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:27-53 (open_db_hooked: busy_timeout, journal_mode WAL, synchronous FULL, no pragma touching rowid assignment); rust/crates/book/schema/v27.sql:315 `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` (notifications, the only AUTOINCREMENT table; lines 186 and 266 are plain INTEGER PRIMARY KEY); rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:185-189 (start build), 196-205 (rebuild after clear), 362-368 (first state_zone build); rust/crates/server/src/clear.rs:155 `book.clear(...)` then :177 `f.rebuild(now)`; rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:584-590 (AddTrade probe returns `since(&m, 1)` only, no figure check). Empirical, sqlite3 in this session: `CREATE TABLE t(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, k TEXT); INSERT 3 rows; SELECT MAX(seq)` -> 3; `DELETE FROM t WHERE seq <= 3; INSERT one row; SELECT seq FROM t` -> 1; `SELECT count(*) FROM t WHERE seq > 3` -> 0. Same with `AUTOINCREMENT`: new row seq -> 4.

findings.title: The log read, the keyed reads and the seq the holder keeps are not one snapshot, so a change can be marked applied unread, or an older key state applied over a newer one
findings.where: Plan lines 82 ("A change reads `SELECT kind, key FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq > ?` ... and then reads each named thing by its key") and 123 ("`Figures::pulled` keeps its shape"). Code: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:420-428 (the read happens before the engine's write lock is taken, on a fresh autocommit connection from `Figures::book()`, :208-216), rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:26-60 (today's whole read is already many autocommit statements), rust/crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:9-12 (WAL: one statement sees one snapshot; a transaction holds one), figures.rs:74-120 and 668-710 (settle_trades and the test that guards the trade-replaced case), rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:105-139 (`anchored_as`, `orphan_unclaimed`).
findings.claim: Under the plan a change is a sequence of statements: the log read, then one keyed read per named thing, then the holder's seq advanced. (1) If the seq the holder keeps is taken after the keyed reads (or from a MAX(seq) read at the end), a change committed between a keyed read and that MAX is marked applied without having been read, and is never re-read. (2) Even with the seq taken from the log read, the keyed reads are separate statements: a writer committing between them gives the engine record R from before the commit and trade T from after it, the inconsistent state figures.rs:431-434 exists to prevent. (3) Two change handlers on two threads (a pull at broker_reads.rs:409, an entry at entries.rs:259) read at different snapshots and apply under the lock in either order; the one that read earlier applies its older key values after the newer ones, and if the holder is set to the larger seq those stale values stand until the keys change again.
findings.failing_scenario: A pull's `store_superseding` (records.rs:132-150) supersedes imported record R by broker record R' and moves trade T (with the owner's note) from R to R' in one transaction. A concurrent `record_changed` has read the log (seq N, before the pull) and is reading keys: it reads R (live, its transactions) before the pull commits and T after it (anchored on R', which it has not read). The engine now holds T anchored on an opening absent from its ledger; `identify` lists T as unclaimed; `settle_trades` calls `orphan_unclaimed(T, seen = R')`; `anchored_as` compares with the book's anchor R' and agrees; T is orphaned and its note cut loose, in the book. On master the same window exists only between the two whole statements at engine_inputs.rs:53 and :57; under the plan it is as wide as the number of keys read.
findings.required_change: Read the log and every keyed thing inside one read transaction on the reading connection (`BEGIN` ... reads ... `COMMIT`; WAL makes it one snapshot), take the applied seq from that same snapshot (MAX(seq) read inside it, before or with the log), and either do that read while holding the engine's write lock or never let the holder advance past a seq read under an older snapshot (apply, then set holder = max(holder, this read's seq) only if this read's base equals the holder it started from; otherwise re-read). The build at a start must take its seq the same way, inside the whole read's transaction. Add a test with two connections: a write committed between the log read and a keyed read is applied exactly once; the trade-replaced test re-run with the write interleaved.

verdicts.why: The plan does not handle this and the code does what the finding says, but part of the finding is pre-existing on master and part is conditional, so it is medium, not high. What stands: (a) the plan never says the log read, the keyed reads and the seq come from one snapshot. Line 82 describes a sequence ("reads SELECT kind, key FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq > ? ... and then reads each named thing by its key"), line 123 keeps Figures::pulled's shape, which on master (figures.rs:420-428) is a read on a fresh autocommit connection (Figures::book, :208-216) before the engine write lock at :428; the words transaction, snapshot and lock never appear in the plan's Approach, and the acceptance tests (lines 128-130) are single-threaded sequences that cannot see it. Book reads are single autocommit SELECTs (book/src/lib.rs:122-130 begins a transaction only for writes; records.rs:608-617 is one statement), so WAL gives one snapshot per statement, not per handler. (b) The handlers really are concurrent: record_changed/pulled is called from the broker thread (broker_reads.rs:409, :429), the orders loop (orders/readback.rs:177) and HTTP handler threads (entries.rs:259, csv_import.rs:273, :351); the commit hook (app.rs:326, store_signal) only signals the bus and serialises nothing. (c) The genuinely new wrong behaviour is sub-claim 3: on master a stale whole-ledger apply is healed by the next record_changed from anywhere, because every change re-reads everything; under the plan the holder keeps "the highest seq it has applied" (line 82), so when handler A (log read at seq N, keys read before a pull's commit) applies after handler B (the pull's own pulled, seq N+1, keys read after), A's older key values overwrite B's and the holder already stands at N+1: nothing re-reads those keys until they are written again or the server restarts. That is a figure that differs from a fresh build and that the page shows indefinitely, with no test in the plan able to catch it. What weakens it: sub-claim 1 (seq taken from a trailing MAX(seq)) is an implementation choice the plan does not make, and its natural reading takes the seq from the log rows read; sub-claim 2 (R old, T new, trade orphaned via orphan_unclaimed/anchored_as at trades.rs:131-139) is exactly master's existing window between live_record_facts (engine_inputs.rs:39-44) and trades() (:57), with ~400 statements in the whole read, so the claim that the plan widens the window is wrong (it narrows it to the handful of keys named, and needs both R and T to be in an unconsumed key set). The required change (one read transaction for log plus keys plus seq, and the holder advanced only under the lock from that snapshot's base) is cheap and belongs in the plan, since the plan replaces master's self-healing whole re-read with a cursor that makes a stale apply permanent.

verdicts.why: The plan does not handle it, the code does what the finding says, and the interleaving produces a wrong figure and a wrong write in the book. The plan (line 82) describes a change as a sequence of separate statements (the log read, then one indexed read per named key) on the connection `Figures::book()` hands out, with `Figures::pulled` keeping its shape (line 123: reads before the engine lock, figures.rs:420-428). `Book` has no read transaction: `lib.rs:107-130` wraps only writes in `atomically`, and every reader is an autocommit statement (engine_inputs.rs:26-60), each its own WAL snapshot (sqlite/src/lib.rs:9-12). Unlike master, whose next change handler re-reads the whole record and converges, the plan's next handler reads only `seq > holder`, so the stale state stands until the key changes again. Severity high stands: the plan's central invariant (line 36, line 128: equal to a fresh build after every change) fails under its stated concurrency, with a durable wrong figure or a trade orphaned in the book.
