findings.title: A trigger must name every key whose read changes, not only the row's own: successions, moved adjustments, re-pointed option terms and REPLACEd transfer links name a second key the plan's table omits
findings.where: Plan lines 70-78 (the kind/key table: `instrument_joins` -> "the instrument's id"; `adjustments` -> "the transaction it applies to"; `transfer_links` -> "both sides' records"), 82 (reads "each named thing by its key") and 97 ("before and after the change"). Code: rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:706-714 (settle_successions deletes every join and reinserts), :378-384 and :421-431 (`names`, `option_terms` of the head fold the member's rows through `group_sql`), rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:610-617 and trades.rs:286-288 and facts.rs:540-541 (transactions, trades and adjustment legs on the member read as the head), rust/crates/book/src/facts.rs:530-536 with links.rs:77-91 (`move_adjustment` UPDATEs the key columns applies_record/applies_leg), identity.rs:591 (option_terms UPDATE underlying_id), rust/crates/book/src/statements.rs:541-547 (`INSERT OR REPLACE INTO transfer_links`), rust/crates/sqlite/src/lib.rs:27-50 (no `recursive_triggers`, so REPLACE's implicit delete fires no DELETE trigger), rust/crates/server/src/wire/build.rs:120 and rust/crates/engine/src/scope.rs:164-174 (the page's symbol and the search read `InstrumentInfo.names`).
findings.claim: The log names the row's own key, but several writes change what is read under another key. (a) A succession joins member B into head A: only B is in the plan's key; A's `InstrumentInfo` (names now folding B's sightings, terms) and every transaction, trade and adjustment leg on B (now read as A) are what changed. (b) `move_adjustment` changes the key column itself; an AFTER UPDATE trigger that logs NEW leaves `Adjustments.chosen` holding the OLD key. (c) `option_terms` re-pointed to another underlying changes the old underlying's family. (d) `INSERT OR REPLACE` on transfer_links does not fire the DELETE trigger, so a link re-made with a different in side leaves the old in side unnamed. The plan's "before and after" covers families the engine can compute from its own state, but a key it never re-reads stays stale in `inputs`.
findings.failing_scenario: (a) A listing changes ticker: the broker retires id A (first seen, so the head) and states B live; a pull's `settle_successions` inserts (B -> A). The trigger logs `instrument B`. The reader re-reads B: not in `instruments()` any more, removed. A is not named, so A's `names` stay the retired symbol: the page shows the old ticker for the holding (wire/build.rs:120) and the symbol search misses the new one (scope.rs:174), and the engine's transactions on B are not re-read as A unless the reader goes looking, so the holding is matched under an instrument the ledger no longer lists. A fresh build shows the new ticker and one holding under A. (b) Supersede X by Y where record Z's adjustment explains X.leg1: after `move_adjustment`, `facts.adjustments` holds both X.leg1 and Y.leg1 -> Z's adjustment; the fresh build holds only Y.leg1.
findings.required_change: In the trigger table: `instrument_joins` logs OLD/NEW `instrument_id` and `into_id`; `adjustments` logs OLD and NEW applies on UPDATE; `option_terms` logs OLD and NEW underlying_id as `instrument`; `transfer_links` either becomes `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` (fires UPDATE with OLD) or the book sets `PRAGMA recursive_triggers = ON` on every connection, and its trigger logs OLD.in_record on UPDATE/DELETE. The reader, for an `instrument` key, re-reads every record whose transactions name it in its current state and the instrument it is joined into. The property test's generator (line 128) must include a succession (join and part), a supersede with an adjustment on another record, and a re-linked transfer; none is listed there now.

verdicts.why: Part (a) holds and the plan does not handle it; parts (b), (c) and (d) are weaker or already covered, so the severity stays medium rather than rising. (a) Plan line 82 defines the reader as reading "each named thing by its key" (`Book::instruments_by_id` for an `instrument` key, `Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])` for a `record` key). A succession is a write to `instrument_joins` only (identity.rs:711-713 deletes every join and reinserts), yet it changes what is read under keys no trigger names: every transaction on the member is read as the head through `COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)` (records.rs:610-616), every trade anchored on it likewise (trades.rs:287-288), `names(head)` folds the member's sightings through `group_sql` (identity.rs:378-384) so `current_name()` (engine input.rs:47-48, `names.last()`) becomes the member's ticker, and `instruments()` stops listing the member (identity.rs:239). The records holding those transactions and the trades are untouched, so no `record` or `trade` entry is logged, and the engine's `ledger.transactions` keep the old instrument while a fresh build reads the new one. The plan's "before and after the change" (line 97) is about which families the engine rematches from its own state, not about re-reading inputs; and the plan's own table (line 73) gives `instrument_joins` a single key, "the instrument's id", for a row with two instrument columns. The property test's write list (line 128) has no succession, and the existing `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` (figures.rs:612-666) exercises `mark_removed` on an ordinary row only, so the acceptance criterion cannot catch it. A succession can appear or vanish with no record on the member touched: `mark_removed` of a corporate-event row ends with `settle_successions` ("a removed event row no longer states a succession", records.rs:494-495), flipping `event_gives_up` (identity.rs:674, :731-739); a pull whose retirement standing arrives after the member's rows were stored in an earlier pull (pull.rs:383) does the same; and a part resets `derived_version` only for contracts on the pair (identity.rs:720-726), never for the member's own rows. (b) is real as a stale key in `Adjustments.chosen` (input.rs:182-184 is keyed by `applies_to`; `move_adjustment` UPDATEs that key, facts.rs:530-536) but produces no wrong figure on master's consumers: the superseded transaction leaves the ledger, ledger.rs:2181 `continue`s when no anchor is found, and the other reads are `get(&t.id)` on live transactions. (c) is covered by line 97: the old underlying's family is known from engine state and the contract's `InstrumentInfo` is re-read under its own key. (d) is correct about SQLite (no `recursive_triggers` pragma in sqlite/src/lib.rs:27-52, so REPLACE's implicit delete fires no DELETE trigger; transfer_links PK is (out_record, out_leg), schema v27.sql:566-572) but whether it leaves a stale input depends on how the delta keys `transfer_links`, which the plan does not say; keyed by out side, the put replaces the pair.
verdicts.evidence: Plan line 73: `instrument` kind, key "the instrument's id", tables `instruments`, `instrument_joins` (one merged into another), `instrument_sightings`, `option_terms`. Plan line 82: "reads each named thing by its key through indexed readers ... (`Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])`, `Book::instruments_by_id`, `Book::trades_by_id`, …)". Plan line 97: "A change reaches the families of every transaction, instrument and adjustment it names, before and after the change" (families, in the engine). Plan line 128 write list: insert/revise/remove a record, transfer link, adjustment, trade, journal; no succession. Code: identity.rs:711-713 `DELETE FROM instrument_joins` then INSERT per (member, head); identity.rs:239 `SELECT id FROM instruments WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT instrument_id FROM instrument_joins)`; records.rs:610 `Read::AsBook => "COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)"` with :616 `LEFT JOIN instrument_joins j ON j.instrument_id = t.instrument_id`; trades.rs:287-288 `COALESCE(j.into_id, anchor_instrument) ... LEFT JOIN instrument_joins j`; identity.rs:380-384 names over `instrument_id IN (SELECT ?1 UNION SELECT instrument_id FROM instrument_joins WHERE into_id = ?1)` (group_sql, :874-876); engine input.rs:47-48 `current_name` is `names.last()`, read at wire/build.rs:120-123 and scope.rs:172-174; records.rs:494-495 `// a removed event row no longer states a succession` then `self.settle_successions()?`; identity.rs:674 `if old == new || self.event_gives_up(old)? { continue; }`; identity.rs:720-726 resets `derived_version` only for contract records on the parted pair; pull.rs:383 `book.settle_successions()?` after storing rows. For (b): input.rs:182-184 `chosen: BTreeMap<TransactionId, Adjustment>` keyed by applies_to; facts.rs:531-533 `UPDATE adjustments SET applies_record = ?, applies_leg = ?`; ledger.rs:2180-2181 `for (applies_to, adj) in inputs.facts.adjustments.iter() { let Some(anchor) = ledger.transactions.iter().find(...) else { continue };`. For (d): statements.rs:543 `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO transfer_links`; schema v27.sql:571 `PRIMARY KEY (out_record, out_leg)`; sqlite/src/lib.rs:27-52 sets journal_mode, synchronous and the commit hook only. Test: figures.rs:648-652 removes `live_records(wealthsimple)[0]`, an ordinary row, then `same_as_fresh`.

verdicts.why:
Sub-claim (a), successions, stands and is enough to carry the finding; (b), (c) and (d) do not produce a wrong figure and should be dropped from it.

(a) confirmed. `settle_successions` (identity.rs:707-714) writes only `instrument_joins` (DELETE all, INSERT the wanted pairs) and, for *parted* pairs only, resets `derived_version` on contract records (identity.rs:720-726); a *join* touches no row of `source_records`, `transactions`, `trades`, `adjustment_legs` or `instrument_sightings`. Yet every one of those reads differently after the join: `transactions_where` reads the instrument as `COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)` (records.rs:610-616), `trades_where` likewise (trades.rs:287-288), `adjustments()` maps legs through `joined()` (facts.rs:540-541, 569), `names(A)` and `option_terms(A)` fold the member's rows through `group_sql` (identity.rs:378-384, 423-431), and `instruments()` drops the member (identity.rs:239). The plan's table (line 73) gives `instrument_joins` the key "the instrument's id" and its reader (line 82) "reads each named thing by its key"; nothing says an `instrument` key re-reads the records, trades or adjustments naming it, and line 97's "before and after" is about which families are re-matched from `inputs`, not which rows are re-read into `inputs`. So after a join of B into A where B's records arrived in an earlier write, `inputs` keeps those transactions under instrument B while `ledger.instruments` no longer holds B: `Matcher::info(B)` is None (ledger.rs:742-759), so the holding is matched under (account, B) with currency defaulting to CAD and never as a coin or contract, separate from A's holding; a fresh build has one holding under A. Even when B's rows arrive in the same write (logged as `record` keys and re-read as A), A's `InstrumentInfo.names` is not re-read unless `into_id` is logged, so `shown` (wire/build.rs:120) keeps the retired ticker and `searched` (scope.rs:172-174) misses the new one. The property test's generator (line 128) lists no succession, so the acceptance criterion "equal to a fresh build" cannot catch it, and line 148's refusal clause depends on that test. The same path runs on every `store` and `store_superseding` (records.rs:123, 147), not only a pull (pull.rs:383).

(b) refuted as a figure. `move_adjustment` has one caller, `supersede` (links.rs:87), which sets the old record superseded in the same write, so its transaction leaves the ledger via the `record` key. A stale `chosen` entry keyed by a transaction that no longer exists reaches nothing: `event_groups` skips an adjustment whose `applies_to` has no transaction (ledger.rs:2181), and `adjustments.get` is only called with ids of transactions being matched (ledger.rs:900, 1566, 1755, 2048). The NEW side is logged, so Y.leg1 gets its adjustment.

(c) refuted. Re-pointing a contract's `underlying_id` (identity.rs:591) changes the contract's own terms, re-read under its own key; the old underlying's own `InstrumentInfo` does not change, and the engine knows the old underlying from its previous inputs, which is what line 97's "before" covers.

(d) not shown to be wrong. `transfer_links`' primary key is `(out_record, out_leg)` (migrations/006:78-84); no `recursive_triggers` pragma exists in the workspace, so REPLACE's implicit delete fires no DELETE trigger, as claimed. But the INSERT trigger fires with NEW naming both out and in records (line 72), and a link collection keyed by its primary key (the out side) is replaced on re-reading the out record; the old in side's family is in the engine's prior state. Only a collection keyed by the pair would go stale, and the plan does not say it is.
verdicts.evidence: Plan lines 73 (`instrument_joins` -> "the instrument's id"), 82 (reads "each named thing by its key"), 97, 128 (generator: no succession), 148. identity.rs:239 (`instruments()` excludes joined members), :378-384 and :423-431 (`names`/`option_terms` fold members via `group_sql`, :874-876), :707-714 (join writes only `instrument_joins`), :720-726 (`derived_version = 0` for parted only). records.rs:610-616 (`COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)`), :123/:147 (`settle_successions` on every store). trades.rs:287-288. facts.rs:540-541. ledger.rs:742-759 (`info(i)` None -> CAD, not coin/option), :2181 (adjustment with no transaction skipped). wire/build.rs:120, scope.rs:172-174. links.rs:87 (sole `move_adjustment` caller). migrations/006-the-broker-s-statements.sql:78-84 (transfer_links PK). No `recursive_triggers` anywhere under rust/.

findings.title: Two tables the whole ledger read touches have no trigger in the plan, and the coverage test as described cannot see them
findings.where: Plan lines 70-78 (the table list), 80 and 130 ("a test reads every table `engine_inputs::ledger` ... read (through `work::statements_naming`, the counter built for brief 25) and fails on one with no trigger"). Code: rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:34-37 (`book.names(i.id)` per instrument), rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:404-417 (`names` reads `instruments_described` only when the instrument has no live sighting, after `listing_named`), rust/crates/book/src/watched.rs:117-127 (`listing_named` reads `listings_named`), identity.rs:473-490 (`instrument_stated`, written by every pull for a holding the broker states that no row brought, `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` of symbol/name), watched.rs:103-111 (`listings_named` written by the person's pick), rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs (holds only the step counter; `statements_naming` does not exist on master d6824aa7), rust/crates/server/src/tests_common.rs:71 (`pulled_book`, whose instruments all have sightings).
findings.claim: `InstrumentInfo.names` comes from `names()`, which falls back to `listings_named` then `instruments_described` for an instrument no live record names. Neither table is in the plan's trigger list. `instruments_described` is rewritten by `instrument_stated` on a pull; today `pulled` re-reads every name whole (engine_inputs.rs:34-37), so a statement-only holding renamed by the broker shows its new symbol after the pull. Under the plan nothing logs it. The test meant to catch a missing trigger counts tables by the statements `ledger()` runs: the fallback statements run only for an instrument without a sighting, which the test fixture has none of, so the test passes with both tables untriggered. The counter it relies on is not on master.
findings.failing_scenario: A holding the broker states in its units statement but whose rows the activity feed never listed (a transfer-in the feed omitted, booked from a statement with no sighting): `instrument_stated` writes `instruments_described` with symbol OLD. The broker renames it; the next pull's `instrument_stated` updates the row to NEW. No trigger fires; `record_changed` names nothing for it; the page shows OLD (wire/build.rs:120) until a restart, where the fresh build shows NEW. The coverage test, run on `pulled_book`, never executes the `instruments_described` statement and reports every table triggered.
findings.required_change: Add `instruments_described` and `listings_named` to the trigger table with key `instrument` (the row's instrument_id). Make the coverage test enumerate tables from the SQL text of every statement `names()`, `option_terms()`, `instruments()`, `transactions()`, `trades()`, `groups()`, `journal_entries()`, `problems()`, `live_record_facts()`, `transfer_links()` and `adjustments()` prepare (or run it on a book seeded with an instrument that has no sighting and a person-named listing), and say in the plan where `statements_naming` comes from if it is in another open PR, since this plan's criterion depends on it.

verdicts.why:
The core of the finding holds, but its concrete failing scenario is wrong and must be replaced.

What holds: `engine_inputs::ledger` (engine_inputs.rs:34-37) reads `book.names(i.id)` for every instrument; `names()` (identity.rs:404-417) reads `listings_named` (through `listing_named`, watched.rs:117-127, used as a gate: when a listing exists the description is skipped and `names()` returns empty) and `instruments_described` when the instrument has no live sighting. Neither table is in the plan's trigger table (plan lines 70-78). The plan's safeguard (line 80, line 130) is a test that reads "every table ... read (through `work::statements_naming`)" — a dynamic count of statements executed. The fallback statements run only for an instrument with no live sighting, so on any fixture whose instruments all have sightings the test cannot see these two tables; the plan names no fixture and does not require one with an unsighted instrument. `work::statements_naming` and "brief 25" do not exist anywhere in the checkout at d6824aa7 (grep: no matches; `rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs` holds only the step counter), so the plan's criterion rests on something unstated. The page reads the names from engine inputs, not the book: `shown()` (wire/build.rs:112-127) uses `InstrumentInfo::current_name()` (input.rs:47-49), and the broker check's units line uses `symbol(inputs, *instrument)` (status.rs:197). `Figures.names` (figures.rs:159, 313-321) holds only broker ids, not symbols, so its reset at figures.rs:458 does not help.

What is wrong in the finding: "the broker renames it; the next pull's `instrument_stated` updates the row to NEW" cannot happen. pull.rs:324-331 calls `instrument_stated` only for a holding with `book.current_name(i).is_none()` and no option terms; `current_name` (watched.rs:131-136) returns the described name through `names()`, or the listing when one exists, so a described instrument is already "named" and the `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` at identity.rs:481-483 is unreachable from a pull. The rename never reaches the book on master either, so a fresh build would also show OLD; no divergence there.

A corrected scenario that does diverge: an instrument created by a record whose only live record is later removed (`mark_removed`, records.rs:471 — the writer the existing test at figures.rs:649-650 exercises) has no live sighting, no listing, no description; the `record` trigger fires and the keyed re-read gives `names = []`. The broker still states units of it, so the next pull's `!named` branch calls `instrument_stated`, which finds the instrument by its broker-security ref and writes only `instruments_described` (the Wealthsimple draft always carries a name: mapping.rs:454-457). No trigger fires. The same pull's `store_units` applies `Change::Broker`, producing `Difference::Units` for that instrument, rendered with an empty symbol ("" in `shown`, status.rs:197), whereas a fresh build shows the described symbol — until restart. Second path: the person's watchlist pick on an existing described, unsighted instrument inserts `listings_named` only (watched.rs:105-111, no `instruments` insert at :91-94 since it was found); `names()` goes from [described] to [] in a fresh build while the engine keeps [described].

Severity lowered to low: both paths need an unsighted instrument the broker states, and what differs is a symbol label in the broker check (not a money figure); but it is a state the page can show that a fresh build would not, violating the plan's own "equal to a fresh build" criterion, and the plan's listed test (line 128's writer set, line 130's counter) cannot catch it.
verdicts.evidence:
- Plan lines 70-78: trigger tables are `source_records, transactions, record_problems, transfer_links, instruments, instrument_joins, instrument_sightings, option_terms, accounts, broker_connections, trades, trade_groups, trade_group_members, journal, journal_tags, adjustments, adjustment_legs`; neither `instruments_described` nor `listings_named`.
- Plan line 80 / 130: the test "reads every table `engine_inputs::ledger` ... read (through `work::statements_naming`, the counter built for brief 25)". findings.title: A pull that stores most of the book does N keyed reads where one scan did; the plan's growth claim and budget do not cover it
findings.where: Plan lines 82 ("One write to the record is then a handful of indexed reads, whatever the size of the book") and 133 (budgets only for add-trade and import). Code: rust/crates/book/src/links.rs:28-113 (a supersede per imported row on the first pull after a carry), rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:243-337 (derive: delete and insert per leg, several log rows per record), rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:395-409 (the pull then `pulled`), rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:608-648 (each keyed transaction read is a JOIN with parse per row).
findings.claim: The first pull after the legacy carry supersedes every imported row and stores every broker row; a mapping version bump handled at open is before the build and fine, but a pull that stores or revises thousands of records writes several log rows per record and the reader then issues one indexed read per deduplicated key (records, instruments, trades), each a JOIN with per-row parsing, where today one ordered scan reads them all. For that pull the keyed path costs more than the whole read, and no budget in the plan measures it.
findings.failing_scenario: Owner's book after the carry: 7,151 live imported transactions. The first sync stores ~7,000 broker records and supersedes ~7,000 imported ones in one pull; the log holds ~30,000 rows naming ~14,000 record keys; `pulled` runs ~14,000 `record_transactions` statements plus the instruments and trades named, more SQLite steps than the one scan it replaces, with the page waiting on "Saving…" (broker_reads.rs:407).
findings.required_change: When the deduplicated log names more than a set share of the records the engine holds (or more than some count), read the ledger whole as a start does and advance the holder the same way; list that call in the boundary test's allowed set; add the first-sync-after-carry pull to the capacity table so the choice of threshold is measured, not asserted.

verdicts.why: The scenario produces no wrong figure and no wrong page state; it is a constant-factor performance concern on an operation the plan, the capacity job and the growth rule do not budget on master either, and the plan's own rule covers it as stated. (1) The plan's rule is work in proportion to the change (title, line 1; line 59). A first pull after the carry that stores ~7,000 broker records and supersedes ~7,000 imported ones changes ~14,000 records; reading ~14,000 keys is proportional to that change, not to the book. The claim the finding cites at line 82 ("One write to the record is then a handful of indexed reads") is about one write; a pull that makes 7,000 writes is not one write, and the plan nowhere claims a pull reads a handful. (2) The dominant cost of that pull is unchanged by the plan and identical under both paths: the pull itself performs ~7,000 `store_superseding` calls, each a `derive` (records.rs:243-337: DELETE/INSERT per leg, sightings, problems, orders) and a `supersede` (links.rs:28-113), before `f.pulled` is ever called (broker_reads.rs:395-409); and when every family is touched the plan's keyed rematch and derive (lines 97-101) match exactly what a full build matches, so that part costs the same as today. The keyed read is a minority of the whole, so "the keyed path costs more than the whole read" cannot make the pull slower end to end than today by more than the read's share. (3) "~14,000 `record_transactions` statements" is the finding's assumption, not the plan's text: line 82 names `Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])`, a reader taking a slice, which can be one statement over the set; and ~7,000 of those keys are superseded records whose transactions `clear_derived` deleted (records.rs:502-507, called at links.rs:93), so a seek on the `(record_id, leg)` primary key (schema: `PRIMARY KEY (record_id, leg)`) returns nothing for half of them. (4) No budget measures the pull on master either: `capacity::Op` has no pull probe (capacity.rs:92-99: Startup, AddTrade, Import, Brokers, PriceChanged, FeedStep) and `docs/architecture.md` §16 line 240 lists the growth-rule operations as `brokers`, `price_changed`, `Feed::step`, an added trade's write and an import's linking; the plan's line 133 budgets exactly the two it takes on (#419, #420). A pull storing the whole book is a one-time event (the first sync after a carry), not an operation a person's input waits on under RAIL. (5) The "Saving…" step the page shows (broker_reads.rs:407) exists today and shows the true state; it is not a wrong state. (6) The required change (a threshold fallback to the whole read) would add a reader of the record whole that the plan's boundary criterion at line 131 is built to forbid, with no shown figure or behaviour benefit. Nothing in the finding is a figure different from a full rebuild, a change missed or applied twice, a wrong page state, or a test that cannot catch what it claims.
verdicts.evidence: Plan: line 1 "work in proportion to the change, never to the book"; line 59 objective; line 82 "One write to the record is then a handful of indexed reads" and the slice-taking reader `Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])`; lines 97-101 families recomputed for what changed; line 131 boundary test forbids whole reads by change handlers; line 133 budgets for add-trade and import only. Code on master d6824aa7: rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:394-409 (the pull's stores complete before `f.pulled`), :407 "Saving…"; rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:544-554 (`store_superseding` per row whose imported record is still live, `report.superseded`); rust/crates/book/src/links.rs:93 `clear_derived` and :94 `set_state(Superseded)`; rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:502-507 `clear_derived` deletes a superseded record's transactions; records.rs:243-337 `derive` per stored record; records.rs:608-648 `transactions_where` (a filter on `t.record_id`, seek on PRIMARY KEY (record_id, leg), schema v9.sql:330 ff., latest schema PRIMARY KEY (record_id, leg)); rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:420-461 `pulled` (one apply pass per pull); rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354 `link` (per-row `supersede` at :341, one `record_changed` at :351); rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:92-134 (`Op` has no pull probe; `OVER_BUDGET` lists import, add-trade, feed-step); docs/architecture.md:240 (growth rule's list: brokers, price_changed, Feed::step, an added trade's write, an import's linking; no pull).

verdicts.why: The finding is a performance speculation about one one-time background event, not a wrong figure, a missed or doubled change, a wrong page state, or a test that cannot catch its claim, so it falls outside the review's stated scope. Taken on its own terms it does not hold up either. (1) The plan's keyed reader is batched by signature, `Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])` (plan line 82): "one statement per deduplicated key" is the finding's assumption, not the plan's design. (2) A by-record read is an index seek on master: `transactions` has `PRIMARY KEY (record_id, leg)` (001-the-book.sql:163), so even unbatched reads are seeks, not scans. (3) Master already does per-key reads inside the "one scan": `engine_inputs::ledger` calls `book.names(i.id)` and `book.option_terms(i.id)` per instrument (engine_inputs.rs:34-37), so the "one ordered scan reads them all" baseline is overstated. (4) The pull in the scenario already does ~7,000 `store_superseding` calls, each a transaction running record lookups, a derive (delete and insert per leg), `trades_anchored_on`, `adjustments_applying_to`, `clear_derived` (three deletes), `set_state`, link inserts and `settle_successions` (records.rs:132-150, links.rs:33-113): the write phase of that pull is already on the order of 100k+ statements, so 14,000 indexed reads cannot make "the keyed path cost more than the whole read" matter to the operation's time, and the engine's rematch after a pull touching every record reaches every family, i.e. equal to today's full match, not worse. (5) The page does not wait: the pull runs on the `bagholder-broker` thread (main.rs:239), "Saving…" is a header step label (broker_reads.rs:407), and `pulled` reads the book before taking the engine write lock (figures.rs:421-428), a shape the plan keeps (line 123). (6) No pull budget exists on master to be missed: `Op::ALL` has no pull op and `waited_on` covers only startup, add-trade and import (capacity.rs:101-118); the plan's line 133 budgets match the two issues it closes (#419, #420). A one-time migration pull growing with the whole book is work in proportion to the change, which is the rule the plan builds (line 22), not a breach of it. No scenario in the finding yields a figure different from a fresh build or a wrong state on the page.
verdicts.evidence: Plan line 82: "reads each named thing by its key through indexed readers the book gains beside its whole ones (`Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])`, `Book::instruments_by_id`, `Book::trades_by_id`, …)" — a slice argument, i.e. a batched reader, not one statement per key. Plan line 123: "`Figures::pulled` keeps its shape: it reads the log instead of the whole record". Plan line 133 budgets add-trade and import only, matching #419/#420. rust/crates/book/migrations/001-the-book.sql:163 `PRIMARY KEY (record_id, leg)` on transactions — a by-record read is an index seek. rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:34-37 — master's whole read already issues `book.names(i.id)` and `book.option_terms(i.id)` per instrument. rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:544-554 — each broker row with a live imported record of the same ref goes through `store_superseding`; rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:132-150 and links.rs:33-113 — each such call runs record lookups, derive, trades_anchored_on, adjustments_applying_to, clear_derived (records.rs:502-507, three deletes), set_state, link inserts, settle_successions, so the pull's write phase already dominates. rust/crates/server/src/main.rs:239 `a.spawn_with("bagholder-broker", broker_reads::run)` — the pull is a background thread; broker_reads.rs:407 `set_step(app, "Saving…")` is a header step; figures.rs:421-428 — `pulled` reads the book before `self.engine.write()`. rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:101-118 — `Op::ALL` lists startup, add-trade, import, brokers, price-changed, feed-step; no pull op, and `waited_on` is startup/add-trade/import only. figures.rs:173-180 confirms the carry exists and "the first pull then supersedes its rows" — a one-time event.

findings.title: An ambiguous file row never resolves once a competitor is taken: the plan re-examines only the rows an operation stored
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:325 (csv_rows = every live file row), :331-337 (taken, then `used` accumulating through one pass), :345-347 (ambiguity); rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:422 (link runs on every pull, stored or not); plan lines 111-115 ("each row the file stored", "each broker row the pull stored", "A pull that stored nothing links nothing") and the Scope table rows at lines 32-33
findings.claim: Today a file row left ambiguous (two free broker rows in its first non-empty tier) is examined again on every later import and every later pull, against the `taken` set as it stands then, so it links as soon as one of its candidates has been taken by another file row. Under the plan a later import looks up only its own rows and a later pull only the broker rows it stored, so a row whose candidate set shrank through another file row's taking is never looked at again, and stays live and counted beside the broker's row. The plan also leaves open whether a row an import reports `unchanged` (Outcome::Unchanged, csv_import.rs:247) counts as "stored"; today it is re-examined because it is live.
findings.failing_scenario: Broker fills B1 (5 units at 10.123) and B2 (5 units at 10.124), same account, day and instrument. File 1 row F1 states 10.12 (two places): both match at two places (csv_import.rs:371) -> ambiguous (2), F1 live and counted. File 2 row F2 states 10.124: F2 takes B2 (`used` now holds B2). Today the next pull, even one that stores nothing, runs link over every live file row: F1's free tier is [B1] -> F1 superseded by B1; the holding is 10 units, the broker's. Under the plan the next pull "stored nothing, links nothing" and import 2 looked up F2 alone: F1 stays live, the holding reads 15 units and its book cost carries F1's 10.12, indefinitely (until B1 or B2 happens to be revised). The same if the user re-imports file 1: F1 comes back Unchanged, and if Unchanged is not "stored" the report says neither linked nor ambiguous for it, where today it says linked.
findings.required_change: Make the unit of linking the movement key, not the stored row. An operation yields the set of keys it touched (every record it stored, revised, removed or superseded, under the record's movement before and after the change, read from the ledger delta of part A so every writer is covered, statements.rs:322/:337/:540 and fills.rs:212 included); for each touched key run today's rule (csv_import.rs:335-348) over all live file rows and all free broker rows under that key, in the ledger's order, with `used` shared across the operation. Candidates are per key, so a taking under one key reaches only that key's file rows, and the work stays bounded by rows per movement. Equivalently: keep each ambiguous row keyed by its candidates and re-examine it whenever one of them is taken, revised or removed. State that an import's Unchanged rows are among the rows examined.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it. On master, `link` (csv_import.rs:323-354) examines every live file row on every run (`csv_rows` at :325 from `book.live_records(&csv::source())`), seeds `used` from `book.superseding(&csv::source())` (:331, records.rs:734-743: every broker record that has already taken a file row's place), and lets `used` grow through the pass (:342). A row is ambiguous only relative to the free candidates at that moment (:337, :345-347). `link` runs on every pull whether or not it stored anything (broker_reads.rs:422, unconditional after `f.pulled`) and after every import (csv_import.rs:274). So today an ambiguous file row re-resolves as soon as any later operation shrinks its free candidate set, including a taking by another file row, a pull's own `store_superseding` of an imported row (pull.rs:550-554, `report.superseded`), or a broker row's removal. The plan (lines 111-115) makes the unit of linking "each row the file stored" and "each broker row the pull stored", and states "A pull that stored nothing links nothing"; nothing in parts A-E or the acceptance criteria re-examines a previously ambiguous row when one of its candidates is taken by a different file row, and the only linking test (line 132) counts rows compared, so it would pass while the row stays unlinked. The failing scenario is valid: the price rule at :371 rounds the broker price to the file's places (10.123 and 10.124 both round to 10.12), so F1 is ambiguous (2); F2 stating 10.124 takes B2 in a later import; today the next pull links F1 to B1 (free tier [B1]); under the plan F1 is never looked up again, stays live, and the holding counts F1+B1+B2 (15 units) with F1's 10.12 in book cost until B1 or B2 happens to be revised. The Unchanged point also holds: a re-import counts Unchanged rows in `lines` (:246-250) and reports them linked when `link` links them (:275-279), and the plan does not say whether Unchanged rows are "stored". The plan's premise at line 115, "only which rows are compared changes", is therefore false: which rows are compared decides which links are made, and this is a change missed. I lower the severity to medium rather than high: the figure error is real, user-visible and persistent, but reaching it needs a later file (or pull) that distinguishes two same-day, same-quantity broker fills the first file could not, and the import report did tell the person at the time that the row was ambiguous; what is silent is only its later non-resolution.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:325 `let csv_rows: BTreeSet<RecordId> = book.live_records(&csv::source())...` (every live file row, every run); :331 `let taken: BTreeSet<RecordId> = book.superseding(&csv::source())...`; :334-347 `let mut used = taken; for (row, tiers) in found { let free = tiers...filter(|b| !used.contains(b))...find(|t| !t.is_empty()); match free.as_slice() { [] => {} [one] => { book.supersede(...); used.insert(*one); ... } more => { out.ambiguous.insert(row, more.len()); } } }`; :371 `.filter(|b| price(b).is_some_and(|bp| bp.round(p.places(), Rounding::HalfEven) == p))` (10.123 and 10.124 both equal 10.12 at two places); :246-250 `Outcome::Unchanged => report.unchanged += 1, ... lines.insert(stored.record, line);` and :275-279 counting `linked` for any record in `lines`. rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:732-743 `superseding`: "The records that have superseded a record of `source`: each has taken the place of one already, and takes no other's" (SELECT DISTINCT t.record_id FROM link_records ... WHERE f.side = 'from' AND r.source = ?). rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:421-422 `// a file's row the broker's own row now reports is linked to it` / `let linking = crate::csv_import::link(f, now)?;` (unconditional on every pull). rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:550-554 `if replaces.is_empty() { book.store(...) } else { report.superseded += replaces.len(); book.store_superseding(adapter.mapping(), &incoming, &replaces, "the broker's own row", now)? }` (a pull's own taking of an imported row, a second path that shrinks another file row's candidates). Plan lines 111-115: "`link` then takes the records the operation stored: after an import, each row the file stored is looked up in the index for broker rows of the same movement ...; after a pull, each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement. ... only which rows are compared changes. A pull that stored nothing links nothing."; Scope table lines 32-33 "each row the import stored" / "each broker row the pull stored"; acceptance criterion line 132 counts rows compared only ("an import of N rows into a book of any size compares N rows with their index lookups; a pull that stored nothing compares none"), nothing checks that an ambiguous row resolves when a candidate is later taken.

verdicts.why: The finding holds on the code and on the plan's words. Today `link` (csv_import.rs:323-354) re-examines every live file row on every call: line 325 collects every live csv record, line 331 seeds `taken` from `Book::superseding` (records.rs:734, every broker record that has already taken a file row), and the candidate filters at 369/389/412 drop taken rows, so a row left ambiguous earlier links as soon as its competitor set shrinks to one. It is called after every import (csv_import.rs:274) and unconditionally on every pull (broker_reads.rs:422), stored rows or not. The plan replaces this with lookups of only the rows an operation stored (plan lines 32-33, 111-115: "each row the file stored", "each broker row the pull stored", "A pull that stored nothing links nothing") and pins that in an acceptance criterion (line 132: "a pull that stored nothing compares none"). Nothing in parts A-E keeps ambiguous rows keyed by their candidates or re-examines them when a candidate is taken, revised or removed; the "equal to a fresh build" property test (line 128) cannot catch it because linking is a book write (supersede), not engine derivation, and a fresh build from a book where F1 is still live counts F1 too. The scenario is concrete and reproducible from the code: B1 (5 @ 10.123) and B2 (5 @ 10.124) both round half-even to 10.12 at the two places F1 states (line 371), so F1 is ambiguous (2) and stays live and counted (the existing test at csv_import.rs:946-955 asserts "kept, and counted"); F2 at 10.124 takes B2; on master the next pull links F1 to B1 (its free tier is [B1]); under the plan nothing ever looks at F1 again, so the holding reads 15 units with F1's 10.12 in its book cost, which SPEC.md line 78 ("linked to the broker's row and not counted twice") forbids. The same gap applies when the broker removes B2 on a later pull (a removal is not a store), which is the more realistic trigger. The Unchanged point is also real: csv_import.rs:250 records every row, Unchanged included, in `lines`, and `link` runs over all live rows, so a re-import reports an earlier-ambiguous row as linked today; the plan does not say Unchanged rows are examined. Severity lowered to medium: the wrong figure is silent and permanent and the plan's own AC locks it in, but the precondition (a row already ambiguous, which master also counts wrongly until a candidate is taken or removed) is narrow.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:325 `let csv_rows: BTreeSet<RecordId> = book.live_records(&csv::source())...` (every live file row, every call); :331 `let taken: BTreeSet<RecordId> = book.superseding(&csv::source())...`; :334 `let mut used = taken;` :337 `.filter(|b| !used.contains(b))` (free tier against takings so far); :345-347 `more => { out.ambiguous.insert(row, more.len()); }` (ambiguous row left live, nothing written); :371 `price(b).is_some_and(|bp| bp.round(p.places(), Rounding::HalfEven) == p)` (10.123 and 10.124 both match a file price of 10.12); :247 `Outcome::Unchanged => report.unchanged += 1,` then :250 `lines.insert(stored.record, line);` (Unchanged rows are among those reported linked/ambiguous). rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:734-743 `superseding`: "each has taken the place of one already, and takes no other's". rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:422 `let linking = crate::csv_import::link(f, now)?;` runs on every pull with no condition on rows stored. Existing test csv_import.rs:946-955 asserts an ambiguous row is "kept, and counted". Plan lines 32-33 ("each row the import stored" / "each broker row the pull stored"), 111-115 ("A pull that stored nothing links nothing"), 132 ("a pull that stored nothing compares none"); no clause re-examines ambiguous rows on a competitor's taking, revision or removal. SPEC.md:78 "is linked to the broker's row and not counted twice, when there is exactly one such row".

findings.title: Looking up from the broker row's side decides ambiguity and tier from the stored rows alone, linking what today is left ambiguous
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:337 (the first tier with a free candidate), :338-347 (exactly one links, more than one is ambiguous), :398-404 and :413-419 (feed tier before statement tier); plan lines 113-114 ("each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement") and 115 ("the tiers, a broker row taking one file row only, ambiguity reported ... unchanged")
findings.claim: The rule is defined from the file row: its candidates are every free broker row of the movement, by tier, and it links only when exactly one is free in the first non-empty tier. A lookup that starts from a stored broker row and finds the file rows of its movement cannot apply that rule unless it then re-runs the file row's own lookup against the whole index; taken literally (the stored row takes the file row it finds) it links where today nothing links, and it ignores the tier of candidates the pull did not store.
findings.failing_scenario: (A) File row F1 live with no candidates. A pull stores B1 and B2, two feed fills of the same units and price (two partial fills). Today link reports F1 ambiguous (2) and nothing links. Under the plan B1 is looked up, finds F1, takes it; B2 finds nothing: F1 superseded by B1 although B2 is equally its fill, and the holding is understated by one fill. (B) F ambiguous over feed rows B1, B2; a pull books statement row S for the same movement (statements.rs:337). Today the feed tier is non-empty so F stays ambiguous and the statement tier is never reached (:337); under the plan S is looked up, finds F, and F links to a statement row. (C) F ambiguous over B1, B2; a pull stores B3 of the same movement: today ambiguous (3); under the plan, with the stored rows as the candidates, F links to B3.
findings.required_change: For every live file row a stored, revised or removed broker row reaches, re-run that file row's own lookup against the whole index under its key (every free broker row, feed tier then statement tier, csv_import.rs:337), never against the stored rows alone; the stored row only names which keys to examine. State this in part D and in the acceptance test (a pull storing two identical fills leaves the file row ambiguous; a statement row booked beside two free feed rows links nothing).

verdicts.why: The finding reads plan line 113 ("each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement") as "the stored row takes the file row it finds", and builds its three scenarios on the file row's candidate set being the stored rows alone. The plan does not prescribe that. Line 111 defines the index as the movement key "to the records holding it", i.e. every record with that key, broker and file alike; looking up a stored broker row's key returns the whole bucket, and the bucket's broker rows are exactly today's candidate set, because csv_import.rs:366-371 and :387-397 filter candidates on precisely the key's fields (account, instrument, kind, quantity, day; cash for a movement), with the price check applied after. Line 115 then fixes the rule as a contract: "the tiers, a broker row taking one file row only, ambiguity reported ... unchanged", which a stored-rows-only candidate set cannot satisfy. Under the plan as written: (A) B1's lookup yields the bucket {F1, B1, B2}; F1's free feed tier is {B1, B2}, ambiguous (2), nothing links, as today (csv_import.rs:337-347). (B) S's lookup yields {F, B1, B2, S}; the feed tier {B1, B2} is non-empty, so the statement tier is never reached and F stays ambiguous, as today. (C) B3's lookup yields {F, B1, B2, B3}: ambiguous (3). No figure comes out different from today in any of the three. The finding's own "required change" (the stored row only names which keys to examine; the file row's lookup runs over every free broker row of that key) is what the index as specified already does. What remains true is narrower than claimed: the plan's acceptance criteria (line 132) count comparisons and do not assert a pull-side ambiguity outcome, and the engine-equality property test (line 128) does not cover link, a book write; the existing tests cover ambiguity and tiers only from the import side (csv_import.rs:946-955, :762-787) and the pull-side link test (:958-968) has a single candidate. So a build that misread line 113 would not be caught by a named test. That is a missing test for a rule the plan states, not a figure the plan would get wrong; low severity, not high.
verdicts.evidence: csv_import.rs:323-354 (link: candidates per file row, first non-empty tier of free candidates, exactly one links, more is ambiguous); csv_import.rs:358-425 (candidates: fill filter on account, trade_date, instrument, kind, quantity then price rounded to the file's places at :370-371; movement filter on account, kind, instrument, quantity, cash and the day disjunction at :387-397; tiers feed-then-statement at :398-404 and :413-419); broker_reads.rs:422 (every pull calls link whole); plan lines 111 (index "for each fill or movement on an instrument, the key csv_import::candidates matches on ... to the records holding it"), 113 (pull side looked up in that index), 115 ("the tiers, a broker row taking one file row only, ambiguity reported ... unchanged"), 132 (acceptance test counts comparisons only); existing tests csv_import.rs:946-955 (ambiguity, import side), :762-787 (tiers, import side), :958-968 (pull-side link, one candidate); SPEC.md:78 (linked only when exactly one such row; with more than one nothing is linked).

verdicts.why:
The code does what the finding says: today's rule is defined from the file row. `candidates` (csv_import.rs:358-425) builds, for each live file row, every free broker row of its movement (fills: one tier, :366-377; instrument movements and cash moved: feed tier then statement tier, :398-404, :413-419), and `link` (:335-348) supersedes only when exactly one is free in the first non-empty tier, else records the row as ambiguous with the count. A pull runs this over every live file row (broker_reads.rs:421), so a row left ambiguous stays ambiguous as more candidates arrive (scenario C) and a statement row booked beside two free feed rows is never reached (scenario B, held on the import side by the test at :773-787).

The plan's part D inverts the direction for a pull: line 114, "each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement", and line 115, "only which rows are compared changes". Line 115 also asserts the tiers and ambiguity are unchanged, but the plan nowhere says that the file row's candidate set is still every free broker row of the movement from the index rather than the stored rows; read as the stored rows being the compared rows, scenarios A and C link where today nothing links, and the figures and the "linked / ambiguous" counts the pull logs differ from the rule the code and SPEC define. The plan's own index (line 111, key -> records holding the movement) would give the full set if the implementer looks the key up again, so a careful build gets it right, which is why this is not refuted outright but also not high: it is an underspecification plus a missing test, not a design that cannot work.

Nothing in the acceptance criteria catches a wrong build: line 132 counts rows compared, not outcomes; line 128's property test compares the engine with a fresh build, and a wrong supersede is a book write both builds reflect alike. The existing suite covers ambiguity only on the import side (:946-955) and the pull side only for one broker row arriving (:958-968); a literal implementation of line 114 passes all of them.

Severity corrected to medium: the plan's line 115 does pin the rule in words and the index design yields the right candidates under one lookup, so the risk is a build that reads 114 literally and a suite that would not notice. Minor inaccuracies in the finding: fills have a single tier (:377), not feed-then-statement, so scenario B must be a cash or instrument movement (where the tiers exist); and `statements.rs:337` (crates/book/src/statements.rs) is the holds query, not where statement rows are booked, though booked statement rows do land in the second tier (test helper `statement_row`, csv_import.rs:744-754).
verdicts.evidence: csv_import.rs:335-348: `for (row, tiers) in found { let free = tiers...filter(|b| !used.contains(b))...find(|t| !t.is_empty()); match free.as_slice() { [] => {}, [one] => supersede, more => out.ambiguous.insert(row, more.len()) } }` -- the rule is per file row over every free broker row of its movement. csv_import.rs:366-373 (fills: every broker transaction of same account/day/instrument/kind/quantity with price rounded to the file's places, one tier); :398-404 and :413-419 (`tier(false)` then `tier(true)`: feed before statement). broker_reads.rs:421: `crate::csv_import::link(f, now)` after every pull, over all live file rows. Plan line 111: index "to the records holding it"; line 114: "after a pull, each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement"; line 115: "the tiers, a broker row taking one file row only, ambiguity reported) is unchanged ... only which rows are compared changes"; line 132: the only linking acceptance test counts "the rows link compares", not what links. Existing tests: csv_import.rs:946-955 (ambiguity at import), :958-968 (one broker row arrives, links), :762-787 (feed tier before statement tier, import side); none for two fills arriving in one pull or a third candidate arriving beside two.

findings.title: A revision or removal that shrinks a file row's candidates is missed: the lookup is under the row's movement after the change only, and a removed row is not "stored"
findings.where: rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:243-279 (derive deletes and re-inserts a revised record's transactions), :471-498 (mark_removed clears a removed record's transactions); rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:247-249 (removed rows) and :556-560 (outcome counted); rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:334-337 (free = candidates not used); plan line 114
findings.claim: Today a candidate that stops matching (its units, cash, day changed, or its transactions cleared by removal) leaves the ambiguous file row's free set smaller on the next link, which then links it. Under the plan the pull looks a revised row up under its new movement, where the file row no longer is, and a removed row stored nothing, so the file row is never examined.
findings.failing_scenario: F (5 units) ambiguous over B1 and B2 (5 units each). A pull revises B2 to 4 units, or marks B2 removed as no longer listed (pull.rs:248). Today the next link finds F's free tier [B1] and links F to B1. Under the plan B2's lookup is under (account, instrument, kind, 4 units, day), which holds no file row, or does not happen at all for a removal; F stays ambiguous and counted beside B1.
findings.required_change: Touched keys include each changed record's movement before the change (from the delta's removed and changed transactions, records.rs:296-308) as well as after, and removed and superseded records are touched like stored ones; then the file rows under those keys are re-examined by their own rule (finding 2).

verdicts.why: The finding reads both the code and the plan correctly. Today `link` is re-run on every pull (broker_reads.rs:422) and `candidates` recomputes each live file row's candidate set over the whole ledger (csv_import.rs:363-373, 386-399), so a broker candidate that stops matching (its quantity revised via derive's delete-and-reinsert, records.rs:275-279; or its transactions cleared by `mark_removed` → `clear_derived`, records.rs:486, reached from pull.rs:248) drops out of the file row's tier, the free set shrinks to one, and the file row is superseded (csv_import.rs:340-343). The plan replaces this with a lookup driven only by the records the pull stored, keyed by their movement after the change (plan line 113: "each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement") and states "A pull that stored nothing links nothing" (line 115), reinforced by the acceptance test "a pull that stored nothing compares none" (line 132). A revised B2 is stored (Outcome::Revised, pull.rs:558) but looked up under its new movement key (4 units), where F (5 units) is not; a removed B2 is not stored at all (mark_removed is not store_row), so no lookup happens. Nothing in the plan re-examines a file row whose candidate set shrank: the index being "maintained by the same delta" (line 111) only keeps the index current, it does not trigger a lookup for F. Result: F stays live and ambiguous beside B1 indefinitely, so the holding counts 10 units where today's next pull resolves it to B1's 5. That contradicts the plan's own claims that "Nothing on screen changes" (line 36) and that only which rows are compared changes, not the outcome (line 115). Severity medium is right: a persistent double count on a figure, but only reachable from an already-ambiguous file row (two broker fills identical in account, day, instrument, side, quantity and rounded price) followed by a revision or removal of one of them, which is the pending-row-withdrawn case `unlisted` exists for (pull.rs:474-475).
verdicts.evidence: csv_import.rs:323-354 (`link` recomputes candidates on every call, supersedes when exactly one free candidate remains); csv_import.rs:363-373 (`candidates` filters every ledger transaction by account/day/instrument/kind/quantity/price, so a revised quantity or cleared transactions remove B2 from F's tier); broker_reads.rs:421-422 (`link` called on every pull); records.rs:275-279 (derive deletes and re-inserts the record's transactions on revision); records.rs:471-498 and 502-507 (mark_removed clears the removed record's transactions; it is not a store); pull.rs:247-249 (unlisted rows go through mark_removed, outside store_row); pull.rs:556-561 (store_row returns the stored id, with Revised counted; this is what the plan's "rows the pull stored" would be). Plan lines 111-115 ("looked up in the index for ... rows of the same movement", "each broker row the pull stored", "A pull that stored nothing links nothing"), line 132 (test asserting a pull that stored nothing compares none), line 36 ("Nothing on screen changes"). engine_inputs.rs:53 reads `book.transactions()` (live records), so an unlinked F remains counted with B1.

verdicts.why: The finding stands. On master, link() (rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354) re-examines every live file row on every pull (broker_reads.rs:422), building each row's candidates from the ledger as it stands now (candidates(), :358-424, quantity equality at :370, transactions read from the engine's ledger at :359-363). A broker row revised to a different quantity is re-derived by deleting and re-inserting its transactions (records.rs:275-279), and a row the broker no longer lists is marked removed via unlisted() -> mark_removed (pull.rs:247-249), which clears its transactions (records.rs:486, clear_derived :502-507). Either way the once-ambiguous file row's free tier shrinks to one on the next link and it is superseded (:340-343), which is SPEC.md:78's standing rule ("linked ... when there is exactly one such row"). Under the plan, link after a pull looks up only "each broker row the pull stored" under its own movement key (plan lines 111-115), and "a pull that stored nothing links nothing" (line 115; acceptance line 132 "a pull that stored nothing compares none"). The pull only stores rows whose payload changed (pull.rs:209-220 skips unchanged rows before store_row), so B1 is never stored on a later pull; the revised B2 is looked up under (account, instrument, kind, 4 units, day), where the 5-unit file row is not; a removal is not a store at all. Nothing in the plan names the before-change movement or treats removed records as touched for linking, so the file row stays live and double-counted indefinitely, which contradicts the plan's own "nothing on screen changes" (line 36). No acceptance test catches it: line 128's property test compares Engine vs fresh build (linking is a book write, not an engine derivation), and line 132 counts rows compared, not whether a row that should now link does. Default to not refuted is overridden because the code and plan text were read and the scenario produces a concrete wrong holding count.
verdicts.evidence: Scenario traced: file row F (Buy ZZQQ 5 @ 20.00, day D) imported with broker rows B1, B2 identical on (account, D, ZZQQ, Buy, 5, price) -> ambiguous (existing test a_row_with_more_than_one_broker_row_it_could_be_links_nothing_and_says_so, csv_import.rs:946-955). Master, next pull: (a) B2 revised to 4 units: pull.rs:218/236 -> store_row -> Book::store -> derive (records.rs:243-279) replaces B2's transactions with quantity 4; candidates() :370 (b.quantity == c.quantity) excludes B2; free tier for F = [B1]; :340-343 supersedes F to B1; holding = B1 5 + B2 4 = 9. (b) B2 unlisted within the read span: pull.rs:247-249 mark_removed -> clear_derived (records.rs:486, :502-507) deletes B2's transactions; same result. Plan: line 113 "after a pull, each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows of the same movement"; line 111 index key is (account, instrument, kind, quantity, trade day, ...); line 115 "A pull that stored nothing links nothing"; line 132 test only counts compares. In (a) the only stored row is B2 looked up under quantity 4 -> F not found; in (b) nothing is stored (pull.rs:209-220 stores only changed rows, and mark_removed is not a store) -> no lookup. F stays live: holding counted as F 5 + B1 5 + B2 4 = 14 (or 10 after removal) instead of 9 (or 5), with no path that re-examines F short of a re-import of the file. SPEC.md:78 states the link as a standing condition ("when there is exactly one such row"), which master meets and the plan does not. Severity medium is appropriate: requires a prior ambiguity (two identical fills same day plus a file row) followed by a revision or removal of one, but the resulting double count persists on the page and nothing in the plan's tests would show it.

findings.title: The index key as written does not reproduce today's match: cash moved ignores kind, and the day match is a disjunction over trade and settle days, not a tuple
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:410-412 (cash moved: account, cash, `b.trade_date == c.trade_date || Some(b.trade_date) == c.settle_date`, no kind), :385-396 (movement on an instrument: three-way day disjunction including `b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)`), :370 (fill: trade day only); rust/crates/broker/src/csv.rs:595-596 (a file's "withdrawal" is Kind::Withdrawal); rust/crates/core/src/transaction.rs:26-33 (Deposit, Withdrawal, TransferIn, TransferOut are distinct kinds); plan line 111 ("(account, instrument, kind, quantity, trade day, and for a movement its cash and settle day)")
findings.claim: The plan's one key puts kind into every match and pairs trade day with settle day, but today cash moved with no instrument is matched without kind (a file's deposit links a feed's transfer-in of the same cash and day), and the days are matched as alternatives on either side. An index keyed as the plan says misses rows today links, which then stay counted twice.
findings.failing_scenario: (1) File row "withdrawal" -50 CAD on 2025-11-04 (Kind::Withdrawal); the feed's row for it is TransferOut -50 CAD on 2025-11-04. Today linked (csv_import.rs:412 compares account, cash and day only); under a kind-keyed index no candidate, so the account's cash reads -100. (2) File dividend row on 2025-11-04 with no settle day; the broker's dividend row trade 2025-11-02, settle 2025-11-04: today linked through `b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)` (:396); a (trade day, settle day) tuple key (2025-11-04, None) against (2025-11-02, 2025-11-04) misses it, and the dividend counts twice.
findings.required_change: Define the index per match exactly as the three filters stand: fills by (account, trade day, instrument, kind, quantity) with the price compared per pair at the file's places; movements on an instrument by (account, kind, instrument, quantity, cash), each broker row entered under its trade day and its settle day and a file row looked up under its trade day and its settle day; cash moved by (account, cash) with the same day treatment and no kind. Hold it by a test that links one row of each of the three kinds through each day alternative.

verdicts.why: The code is as the finding says and the plan does not handle it. On master, `csv_import::candidates` applies three distinct filters: a fill matches on (account, trade day, instrument, kind, quantity) plus a per-pair price comparison (csv_import.rs:370-371); a movement on an instrument matches on (account, kind, instrument, quantity, cash) with a three-way day disjunction `b.trade_date == c.trade_date || Some(b.trade_date) == c.settle_date || b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)` (:396); cash moved with no instrument matches on (account, cash) only, with no kind, and a two-way day disjunction (:412). The no-kind rule for cash moved is deliberate and documented in `link`'s own doc comment (:316-318: "for cash moved, the same account, currency and exact signed amount, on the same day") and was written that way in a5f7feaa; it is not in SPEC.md (trade-42 and trade-44 cover only fills and movements on an instrument), so the plan's line 115 claim that the rule "is SPEC.md's" leaves the cash-moved rule undescribed anywhere but the plan's own line 111. Line 111 gives one composite key "(account, instrument, kind, quantity, trade day, and for a movement its cash and settle day)" for "each fill or movement on an instrument": it puts kind into every match, pairs trade day with settle day as fields of one key rather than as alternatives on either side, and names no case for a movement with no instrument at all. An index built as line 111 states cannot reproduce either disjunction and would miss the cross-kind cash link. The failing scenarios are real: a file's "withdrawal" action is Kind::Withdrawal (broker/src/csv.rs:596) while the feed's row for the same money out can be TransferOut (broker/src/codes.rs:78, 81; core/src/transaction.rs Withdrawal/TransferOut distinct), which today links at :412 and under a kind-keyed index does not, so the account's cash counts the withdrawal twice; a file dividend with no settle day against a broker dividend whose settle day equals the file's trade day links today only through the third alternative at :396 and misses under a (trade day, settle day) tuple, so the dividend counts twice. No acceptance criterion holds `link`'s outcome equal to today's: criterion at line 128 compares engine figures against a fresh build (linking is a separate write, `supersede`, not a derivation), and line 132 counts rows compared, not rows linked. The existing tests at csv_import.rs:762-787 link Deposit to Deposit (statement code CONT is Kind::Deposit, codes.rs:75) and so would not catch the lost cross-kind match either. Severity stays medium: a wrong figure (cash or a dividend counted twice) on the import and pull linking path, caught by no test the plan names, but not a figure in the derived model and avoidable by an implementer who reads the three filters rather than the plan's key.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:370 `.filter(|b| b.account == c.account && b.trade_date == c.trade_date && b.instrument == c.instrument && b.kind == c.kind && b.quantity == c.quantity)` (fill: trade day only, kind); :396 `&& (b.trade_date == c.trade_date || Some(b.trade_date) == c.settle_date || b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date))` (movement: three-way disjunction); :412 `moved(b) && b.account == c.account && b.cash == c.cash && (b.trade_date == c.trade_date || Some(b.trade_date) == c.settle_date)` (cash moved: no kind, two-way disjunction); :316-318 doc comment "for cash moved, the same account, currency and exact signed amount, on the same day". rust/crates/broker/src/csv.rs:595-596 `"deposit" => Kind::Deposit, "withdrawal" => Kind::Withdrawal`; rust/crates/broker/src/codes.rs:75-81 `"CONT" => Kind::Deposit`, `"WD" => Kind::Withdrawal`, `"TRFOUT" => Kind::TransferOut`, `"TRFOUTTF" => Kind::TransferOut`. Plan line 111: "for each fill or movement on an instrument, the key `csv_import::candidates` matches on (account, instrument, kind, quantity, trade day, and for a movement its cash and settle day)"; line 115: "The matching rule itself ... is unchanged: it is `SPEC.md`'s"; acceptance criteria lines 128 and 132 test figures against a fresh build and count rows compared, neither holds link's outcome per kind and day alternative. Existing linking tests csv_import.rs:762-787 pair a file "deposit" with a feed Deposit and a statement CONT (both Kind::Deposit), so none exercises the cross-kind cash match.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's key, as written, does not reproduce it. On master, `candidates` (rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs) has three matches with three different keys: a fill at :370 compares (account, trade day, instrument, kind, quantity) with the price per pair at :371; a movement on an instrument at :391-396 compares (account, kind, instrument, quantity, cash) and the day as a three-way disjunction `b.trade_date == c.trade_date || Some(b.trade_date) == c.settle_date || b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)`; cash moved with no instrument at :412 compares only (account, cash) and a two-way day disjunction, with no kind. The plan (line 111) defines one index key for "each fill or movement on an instrument" as "(account, instrument, kind, quantity, trade day, and for a movement its cash and settle day)": kind in every key, and the two days as components of the key rather than alternatives; cash moved with no instrument is not described at all. Line 115 claims the matching rule is unchanged, but the index as specified is narrower than the filters it replaces. Both scenarios are real on master: (1) the file vocabulary has only "deposit"/"withdrawal" (broker/src/csv.rs:589-596), while the feed books an internal transfer's cash leg as Kind::TransferOut/TransferIn with no instrument (wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:803-810) and a statement books TRFOUT/TRFOUTTF as TransferOut (broker/src/codes.rs:78,81); today :412 links a file withdrawal to that row by (account, cash, day) alone, and a kind-keyed lookup finds no candidate, so the file row stays live and the cash counts twice. (2) A statement row has trade_date = the executed day and settle_date = the statement day (wealthsimple/src/statement.rs:315-316), and a file row has settle None (csv.rs:577); today a file dividend dated on the statement day links through `b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)` (:396), and a (trade day, settle day) tuple key (D, None) vs (D-2, D) misses it. No test on master or in the plan holds either: the existing link tests (csv_import.rs:761-787, 826-847) use same-kind rows (file deposit vs feed Deposit; statement CONT maps to Kind::Deposit at codes.rs:75) on one day; the plan's property test (line 128) compares engine figures with a fresh build of the same book, which both see the unlinked state identically; and the linking criterion (line 132) counts rows compared, not which rows link. Severity medium is right: a wrong cash figure after an import for a subset of rows, not a general corruption, and fixable by defining the index per match as the finding's required change states.

findings.title: Which of two live file rows a broker row takes is the ledger's order today; a set lookup from the broker row's side does not fix it
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:335 (file rows examined in `ledger.transactions` order), rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:617 (ORDER BY account, trade_date, occurred_at, record_id, leg; a file row's occurred_at is None, csv.rs:732, so record id, a v7 uuid of the import's `now`, lib.rs:134-138, orders rows of different imports by import), :340-343 (the first takes it, `used` keeps the second off); plan line 114-115
findings.claim: Two live file rows for one movement (from two files) can state different prices or fees; the one that stays live carries its own figures into the book cost. Today the earlier-imported row gives way. The plan's broker-side lookup returns a set and names no order, so the build may leave the other row live and the cost basis differs from today.
findings.failing_scenario: File 1 row F1: 5 units at 10.12, fee 0; file 2 row F2: 5 units at 10.123, fee 1.50 (same movement). No broker row yet. A pull stores B (10.123). Today F1 (the earlier record id) is superseded and F2 stays: cost = B's 5 units + F2's 5 at 10.123 plus 1.50 fee. If the build takes F2, cost = B + F1's 5 at 10.12 with no fee: a different average cost and realised P/L.
findings.required_change: Examine the file rows under a key in the ledger's order (account, trade day, occurred_at, record id, leg), and say so in part D; the test for "a broker row taking one file row only" should use two rows that differ in a stated field so the one left live is observable.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not name the order. On master, `link` (csv_import.rs:335-343) walks `found` in the order `candidates` produces it, and `candidates` iterates `ledger.transactions` directly (csv_import.rs:363, 386, 411), which is `book.transactions()` unsorted (engine_inputs.rs:53; no re-sort of `ledger.transactions` anywhere in the workspace), i.e. records.rs:617's `ORDER BY account, trade_date, occurred_at, record_id, leg`. A file row's `occurred_at` is None (csv.rs:732) and two file rows matching the same broker fill share account and trade day (csv_import.rs:370), so their order is by record id, a UUID v7 of the store's `at` (lib.rs:134-138): across imports, the earlier import's row comes first, takes the one free broker row, and `used` (line 342) keeps the later one live. The scenario is reachable: the csv record key is account, layout, cells and occurrence (csv.rs:644-645), so two files stating different price or fee cells for the same fill are two live records, and a pull then runs `link` over all of them (broker_reads.rs:422). The row left live carries its own price and fee into the holding's cost, so which one gives way is a figure on the page. The plan (lines 113-115) replaces the file-side walk with a lookup from each stored broker row to "live file rows of the same movement" and says only that "a broker row taking one file row only" is unchanged; it names no order among the file rows found, while line 36 claims nothing on screen changes. No acceptance criterion holds the linking outcome equal to master's (criterion at line 132 counts rows compared only; the fresh-build property test at line 128 covers the engine, not which record `link` supersedes), and the existing test `a_broker_row_takes_the_place_of_one_file_row_only` (csv_import.rs:790-798) imports two identical rows in one file, so which gives way is unobservable there (and within one import the v7 ids share `at`, so that order is random bits today anyway). Two caveats that keep it low: SPEC trade-42/43 does not define which of two file rows gives way, so either outcome is spec-conformant, only different from master; and a BTreeSet<RecordId> lookup would happen to reproduce master's order for fills (same account and day, no occurred_at). It would not for dividends or cash moved, where two file rows can match one broker row on different trade days (csv_import.rs:396, 412) and ledger order is then by trade date, not record id, so the order does need stating.

verdicts.why: The finding holds. On master, which of several live file rows a broker row takes is fixed by the ledger's order: csv_import.rs:363/:386/:411 walk `ledger.transactions` for the file rows, and link (csv_import.rs:335-343) gives the broker row to the first file row met, `used` keeping later ones off; that order is `ORDER BY account_id, trade_date, occurred_at, record_id, leg` (records.rs:617), a CSV row's occurred_at is None (csv.rs:732) and a record id is a v7 UUID of the import's `now` (records.rs:158, lib.rs:134-137), so for two rows on one account and day the earlier import's row gives way. The scenario is reachable: a row's key is (account, layout, cells, occurrence) (csv.rs:644-645), so two files stating different price places or fees for one fill are two live records, and both match one broker row since a fill compares only account, day, instrument, kind, quantity and the broker price rounded to the file's places (csv_import.rs:370-371), never fee or cash. The row left live carries its own price and fee into the holding's cost, so the choice changes average cost and realised P/L on the page. The plan's part D (lines 111-115) looks up from the broker row's side and says "a broker row taking one file row only" is unchanged but names no order; SPEC.md :78 states the rule from the file row's side only, and neither statement-gaps.md nor stage-money.md fixes it. No test catches a change: `a_broker_row_takes_the_place_of_one_file_row_only` (csv_import.rs:790-798) uses two identical rows so the survivor is unobservable, the pull-side test (csv_import.rs:958-968) has one file row, and the plan's "equal to a fresh build" criterion compares the engine with whatever state the book holds, which is consistent either way. Partial mitigation only: if the build's index keeps records in a BTreeSet<RecordId>, fills on one account and day would come out as today, but the plan does not say so, and for movements and cash rows that match by settle day (csv_import.rs:396, :412) ledger order is by trade day first, so even a record-id set diverges there. Severity low is right: it needs two differing unlinked file rows for one movement, and both outcomes are already a double count.
