findings.title: No test in the plan holds linking's outcome equal to today's; the count criterion as worded would forbid the fix
findings.where: plan line 128 (equality is Engine::differences against Engine::build, which reads the supersede links as the book holds them and never runs `link`), line 132 ("an import of N rows into a book of any size compares N rows ... a pull that stored nothing compares none"); rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354 (link is a book write, outside the engine)
findings.claim: The fresh-build property test cannot catch a file row left live that today's whole-ledger pass would have superseded: the engine agrees with the book either way, and the book is what is wrong. The count criterion asserts exactly the behaviour of findings 1-3 (only stored rows examined), so a build meeting it reproduces them, and a build that re-examines the touched keys' other file rows fails it.
findings.failing_scenario: Finding 1's sequence (B1, B2; F1 ambiguous; F2 takes B2; a pull storing nothing): both acceptance tests pass, F1 stays counted, the holding reads 15 units where today it reads 10.
findings.required_change: Add an equivalence test with today's whole-ledger `link` kept as the oracle (as compare.rs keeps whole builds): over random sequences of imports (rows stating prices at various places, duplicates across files) and pulls (feed and statement rows stored, revised, removed, superseded), after each step the set of supersede links from file rows and the set of ambiguous rows equals what the whole pass produces on the same book. Re-word the count criterion to "reads only the live file rows and free broker rows under the keys the operation touched".

verdicts.why: The finding stands. (1) The plan's equality test (line 128) and the existing `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` both use `Engine::build` from the book as the oracle (`same_as_fresh`, figures.rs:589-595: `build(&book, ...)` then `e.differences(&fresh)`). `link` is a book write outside the engine: csv_import.rs:341 calls `book.supersede`, which deletes the superseded record's transactions (records.rs:502-505 via links.rs:93) and sets it Superseded (links.rs:94). The engine reads the book as it stands (engine_inputs.rs:53 `book.transactions()`), so a file row wrongly left live is in both the incremental engine and the fresh build: the test passes on a wrong book. (2) Today's `link` examines every live file row on every pass (csv_import.rs:325 `live_records(&csv::source())`), with `taken` = every broker row already superseding one (331), and runs on every pull whether or not it stored anything (broker_reads.rs:422). The plan's D (lines 111-115) examines only the rows the operation stored and says "A pull that stored nothing links nothing", while claiming only "which rows are compared changes" and (line 36) "Nothing on screen changes". The count criterion at line 132 ("an import of N rows ... compares N rows"; "a pull that stored nothing compares none") asserts exactly that narrowing, so a build that re-examined the other live file rows whose candidates the operation took would fail it. (3) The scenario produces a different figure. Two broker fills B1, B2 of the same instrument, account, day, side and quantity (5 each) at prices 10.001 and 10.002. File row F1 states 10.00: candidates (371, rounded to the file's places) are [B1, B2] → ambiguous (345-347). A later file row F2 states 10.002: candidates [B2] → takes B2 (340-343). Ledger order is account, trade_date, occurred_at, record_id, leg (records.rs:617), so F1 (stored earlier) is examined before F2 in the same pass and stays ambiguous there; today the next pull's whole pass (422) sees B2 in `taken` (331), leaves F1 with free=[B1] (337) and links it: live rows B1+B2 = 10 units. Under the plan, F2's import looks up only F2 and a pull storing nothing looks up nothing, so F1 stays live: B1+B2+F1 = 15 units, and the holding, its cost and the cash row all differ from today's; both acceptance tests at 128 and 132 pass. The plan nowhere compares the post-link book (supersede links and ambiguous set) against today's whole pass; the right-to-refuse clause (148) covers only match couplings inside the engine. No test today pins a later pass resolving an earlier ambiguity either (csv_import.rs tests at 711, 786, 843, 953 check single passes), so nothing in the suite would catch it. Medium is right: the wrong figure is real and silent but needs a specific shape (two same-size same-day broker fills, two file rows at different precision, or a feed/statement pair for a movement).
verdicts.evidence: csv_import.rs:323-354 — `link` reads `book.live_records(&csv::source())` (325), `book.superseding(&csv::source())` as `taken` (331), picks the first tier with free candidates (337), supersedes on exactly one (340-343), records ambiguity on more (345-347); it is a book write, not an engine change. csv_import.rs:363-377 — fill candidates filtered by `!taken.contains` (369) and the price rounded to the file's places (371), so a row stating fewer places matches more broker rows. links.rs:93-94 — `clear_derived` then `set_state(Superseded)`; records.rs:502-505 — the superseded record's `transactions` rows are deleted. records.rs:617 — ledger order `account_id, trade_date, occurred_at, record_id, leg`. engine_inputs.rs:53 — the engine's transactions are `book.transactions()`, i.e. the book as linked. broker_reads.rs:422 — `link` runs on every pull, stored rows or not. figures.rs:589-595 — `same_as_fresh` compares the engine with `build(&book, ...)`: the book is the oracle. Plan line 36 ("Nothing on screen changes"), 111-115 (link takes only the rows the operation stored; "A pull that stored nothing links nothing"; "only which rows are compared changes"), 128 (equality = `Engine::differences` vs `Engine::build`, writers listed without import or link), 132 ("an import of N rows ... compares N rows"; "a pull that stored nothing compares none"), 148 (refusal clause limited to match couplings).

verdicts.why: The finding stands on all three points. (1) The plan's equality criteria cannot see a wrong supersede state: plan line 128 holds `Engine::differences` against `Engine::build` "from the book", and the existing `same_as_fresh` (figures.rs:589-595) is exactly that form — both sides read the same book, so a file row left live that today's pass would have superseded is in both engines and the test passes. Line 129 (Moved equals the difference of two fresh builds) has the same blind spot. Lines 130-131 are about the log and whole reads. No criterion in the plan compares link outcomes against the whole-ledger `link`, and the "also held with the existing" test at figures.rs:612 never calls `link` (the pull-side test at csv_import.rs:958 covers a row linked when the broker row is stored, not a row left ambiguous and resolved later). (2) The count criterion at line 132 asserts the divergent behaviour: "a pull that stored nothing compares none" forbids re-examining an earlier file row on a pull, and "an import of N rows compares N rows" forbids re-examining other file rows whose candidate set the import's own links just shrank; plan line 115 states "A pull that stored nothing links nothing" as design, so the plan does not handle the gap, it codifies it. (3) The failing scenario is real on master: `link` reads every live file row on every pass (csv_import.rs:325) and seeds `used` from `book.superseding` (:331, :334, :337), and a pull calls `link` unconditionally (broker_reads.rs:422), so a row ambiguous on one pass is linked on the next once another row has taken one of its candidates; ambiguity is persisted nowhere (grep of the crates finds it only in the import report and the pull's log line). The fill tier matches on the price rounded to the places the file states (csv_import.rs:371), so F1 at "20.00" sees B1 and B2 (ambiguous, :345-347) while F2 at "20.001" sees B2 alone and takes it (:340-343); today the next pull links F1 to B1 and the holding reads 10 units, under the plan F1 stays live and it reads 15. SPEC.md:78 ("is linked to the broker's row and not counted twice, when there is exactly one such row") describes F1's state after F2's import, so the plan's outcome also breaks the rule it says at line 115 is unchanged. Severity medium is right: the finding is about the test gap and the criterion wording; the wrong figure itself is findings 1-3's.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354 — `link` reads `book.live_records(&csv::source())` (every live file row, :325), seeds `used` with `book.superseding` (:331, :334), and for each row takes the first tier's free candidates (:337): one → `book.supersede` (:340-343), more → `out.ambiguous` (:345-347), nothing persisted. csv_import.rs:358-379 — the fill tier compares `price(b).round(p.places(), HalfEven) == p` (:371), so two file rows stating the same fill to different places see different candidate sets. rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:421-425 — every pull calls `crate::csv_import::link(f, now)` whatever it stored. rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:726-743 — `live_records` and `superseding` are book queries; a supersede is a book write. rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:589-595 — `same_as_fresh` builds `fresh` from `f.book()` and asserts `e.differences(&fresh)` empty: engine against the same book, link never run; figures.rs:612-666 — `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` never calls `link`. csv_import.rs:945-968 — the existing ambiguity test asserts only the ambiguous report; the pull-side test links a row when its broker row is stored, not a row ambiguous earlier. Plan lines 115 ("A pull that stored nothing links nothing"), 128 (equality is against `Engine::build` from the book), 129, 132 ("an import of N rows ... compares N rows ...; a pull that stored nothing compares none"). SPEC.md:78 — a file fill "is linked to the broker's row and not counted twice, when there is exactly one such row; with more than one, nothing is linked".

findings.title: Engine::differences never compares Matched or Identity, so the equality property test cannot see the collections part B re-keys per family
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:609-652 (compare/differences), engine.rs:240-255 and 322-359 of ledger.rs (what is held but not compared); readers: rust/crates/server/src/status.rs:206-215 (matched.beyond), status.rs:743 (matched.units_on), rust/crates/server/src/wire/build.rs:748 (matched.roles), rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:78-110 (identity.needs_trade/moved/joined/unclaimed), rust/crates/engine/src/equity.rs:121,164-166 (matched.cash, matched.units into broker checks). Plan lines 99-101, 107, 128.
findings.claim: `Engine::differences` is `compare(&other.snapshot(Parts::ALL))` plus quotes: it compares trades, positions, cash rows, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, the brokers' statements and `BookFig` (accounts, instruments, waiting, activity, today). It does not compare `Matched` (trips, books, units, roles, beyond, dust, arrived, last_price, cash, disagreements, unit_disagreements, unapplied, stock_dividends) nor `Identity`. Part B makes exactly these the things a family rematch replaces by key (`Matched` lists become maps with per-family key ownership; `Matched.cash` becomes per (account, family) shares; `Identity` is updated for recomputed families only). The acceptance criterion 'Equal to a fresh build … holds Engine::differences against Engine::build' therefore cannot catch a stale or lost entry in any of them unless it happens to change a derived figure, and several are read by the page or the server directly.
findings.failing_scenario: A book with no broker statement (the generator lists accounts, instruments, events, links and trades but no `BrokerAccount`): `broker_checks` is empty, so `matched.cash` is invisible. A transfer link between accounts A and B is removed, splitting one family into two; the keyed engine fails to drop the old family's (A, F) cash share and keeps summing it. `differences` is empty, the test passes, and the next pull that stores A's cash statement shows a CAD cash difference the fresh build does not. Likewise: a revision moves transaction t from instrument X's family to Y's; the old family's `roles[t]` or `beyond` entry keyed by t is not removed; `differences` is empty, yet the status page prints 'A sale of X … took N more than the book held' for a row that no longer takes anything (status.rs:210-215) and the fill words on the detail page read the stale role (build.rs:748).
findings.required_change: Make the equality test compare the whole engine state the plan re-keys: extend `Engine::differences` (or the property test) to compare `Matched` and `Identity` whole (both derive PartialEq), and have the generator produce broker statements with stated cash and units so `checks` is non-empty. State in the acceptance criterion that `matched` and `identity` are part of the equality, not only the figures `Figures` exposes.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it. `Engine::differences` (rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:644-652) is `compare(&other.snapshot(Parts::ALL))` plus quotes; `snapshot` (589-601) and `compare` (609-640) cover only trades, positions, cash rows, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, the brokers' statements and `BookFig` (accounts, instruments, `matched.waiting`, activity, today). `Matched` (ledger.rs:322-359) and `Identity` (identity.rs:27-45) are never compared, though both derive PartialEq. Several `Matched` fields have no reader in the engine's derivation at all: every engine-side use of `beyond`, `dust`, `arrived`, `disagreements`, `unit_disagreements`, `unapplied` and `roles` is a push/insert in ledger.rs (e.g. 1204, 1483, 1504, 1157, 1373, 1520); their only consumers are the server's status.rs:206-215 (`matched.beyond`, printed in the header) and wire/build.rs:748 (`matched.roles` into fill words), plus the `compare.rs` tool. So a stale or lost entry in them changes no figure `differences` sees, yet the page prints them directly. `matched.cash` is read only by `broker_checks` (equity.rs:121) inside a loop over `inputs.market.brokers` (equity.rs:115-119); with no `BrokerAccount` the loop runs zero times, `checks` is empty, and `matched.cash` is invisible. The plan's generator (line 128) lists accounts, instruments, transfers, events, a multi-leg order and the record/link/adjustment/trade/journal writers, but no broker statement, so the generated books take exactly that path. `Identity.needs_trade/moved/joined/unclaimed` are consumed by `settle_trades` (figures.rs:78-110) as book writes; only `trade_of` reaches `build_trades`. The plan's acceptance criterion (line 128) names only `Engine::differences` against `Engine::build`, and the existing `same_as_fresh` (figures.rs:589-595) asserts the same thing; line 129's `Moved` comes from the same `compare`. Nothing in the plan says `matched` or `identity` are part of the equality, while lines 99, 101 and 107 make precisely those collections the ones replaced per family, and line 148's right-to-refuse relies on this property test to expose a missing coupling. The failing scenarios are therefore real blind spots: a lost (account, family) cash share with no statement in the book, or a `roles`/`beyond` entry left under a transaction that moved family, passes the test and reaches the status header, the fill words, or the next broker cash check. Severity high stands: this is the plan's sole correctness guard for the riskiest part (B), and it cannot see the collections B re-keys unless they happen to alter a derived figure.
verdicts.evidence: engine.rs:644-652 `pub fn differences(&self, other: &Engine) -> Moved { ... self.compare(&other.snapshot(Parts::ALL), &mut m); ... quote_moved ... }`; engine.rs:589-601 Snapshot fields: trades, positions, cash, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, brokers, book; engine.rs:604-607 `BookFig { accounts, instruments, waiting: self.matched.waiting.clone(), activity, today }`; engine.rs:240-255 Engine holds `matched: Matched, identity: Identity` not in any snapshot. ledger.rs:322-359 `pub struct Matched { trips, books, beyond: Vec<Beyond>, dust, arrived, last_price, stock_dividends, disagreements, unit_disagreements, unapplied, units, roles: BTreeMap<TransactionId, FillRole>, waiting, cash: BTreeMap<AccountId, BTreeMap<Currency, Fig<Dec>>> }` with `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]`. Readers outside the engine: status.rs:206 `let beyond = &figures.matched.beyond;` ... :214 `"{what} of {} in {}{day} took {} more than the book held."`; wire/build.rs:748 `fill_words(tx, option, figs.matched.roles.get(&tx.id).copied())`; equity.rs:115-121 `let brokers = match only { Some(a) => inputs.market.brokers.get_key_value(&a)..., None => inputs.market.brokers.iter().collect() }; for (account, b) in brokers { ... let own_cash = matched.cash.get(account).unwrap_or(&no_cash);` (no brokers → no checks → matched.cash unseen). Grep over crates (non-test) for `.beyond|.roles|.dust|.arrived|.disagreements|.unapplied|.unit_disagreements`: all engine hits are pushes/inserts in ledger.rs (818, 1157, 1202, 1204, 1373, 1433, 1483, 1504, 1520, 1965); no derivation reads them. identity.rs:27-45 `Identity { trade_of, needs_trade, joined, moved, unclaimed }`; figures.rs:78-110 settle_trades reads needs_trade/moved/joined/unclaimed and writes the book. figures.rs:589-595 `same_as_fresh`: `let held = f.read(|e| e.differences(&fresh)); assert!(held.is_empty())`. Plan line 128: "holds `Engine::differences` against `Engine::build` from the book empty after every step" with a generator of "accounts of several kinds; shares, coins, contracts on underlyings; transfers between accounts; corporate events with their adjustments; a multi-leg order naming no instrument" and writers "insert, revise and remove a record...; add and remove a transfer link; set and clear an adjustment; open, move and orphan a trade; a journal entry" — no broker statement. Plan line 99: Matched lists become maps "the engine keeps, per family, the keys it produced... `Matched.cash` kept per (account, family) and summed per account"; line 107: "`Identity` is updated for the recomputed families only"; line 148: "the property test would show it".

verdicts.why:
The finding holds on the code and on the plan's words. `Engine::differences` (engine.rs:644-652) is `compare(&other.snapshot(Parts::ALL))` plus quotes, and `snapshot` (engine.rs:589-601) clones only trades, positions, cash rows, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, brokers and `book_fig()`; `book_fig` (engine.rs:604-607) takes only `matched.waiting` from `Matched`. Nothing in `compare` (engine.rs:609-640) touches the other fourteen fields of `Matched` (ledger.rs:322-359) or any field of `Identity` (identity.rs:26-45), though both derive `PartialEq` and could be compared whole. The plan's part B (lines 99, 101, 107) makes exactly these the collections that a family rematch replaces by key, its acceptance criterion (line 128) holds only `Engine::differences`, its "right to refuse" (line 148) says a missing coupling is what "the property test would show", and the build order (line 167) puts B "behind the equality property test". Both existing tests the plan leans on use only `differences` too (engine/tests/changes.rs:187, server/src/figures.rs:593); no test in the tree compares `matched` or `identity`.

The failing scenarios are real paths to a wrong screen with the test green. `beyond` entries are pushed without tainting the holding (ledger.rs:1200-1205, 1496, 1965), so a stale one moves no position or trade figure, yet `broker_failures` (status.rs:206-215) prints "… took N more than the book held" for each, and it is wired into the header's failure line (status.rs:118). `roles` (ledger.rs:1483, 1504) is read by nothing in the snapshot and only by `fill_words` on the detail page (wire/build.rs:748). `matched.cash` (ledger.rs:2244-2251) is read only inside `broker_checks` (equity.rs:121), which iterates `inputs.market.brokers` (equity.rs:115-118); the plan's generator (line 128) lists accounts, instruments, events, links and trades but no broker statement, so with `brokers` empty a lost or doubled per-(account, family) cash share produces no check, no difference, and a green test, until a later statement makes the check exist. `Identity.needs_trade/moved/joined/unclaimed` are read only by `settle_trades` (figures.rs:79-110), which writes trades to the book from them; a stale entry there is a wrong book write the figure comparison does not see until after it has happened.

Nothing in the plan handles it: no line says `Matched` or `Identity` are compared, and no line says the generator produces broker statements. The severity stands: the plan's only guard for the correctness of B, and the mechanism it names for discovering a missed coupling, is blind to the very state B re-keys.

findings.title: A saved group spans families; a ledger change to one member's trip leaves the group's trade stale, and the generator never saves a group
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:296-341 (build_trades: groups first, `trip_of_trade`, `used`, first group takes a shared trade), rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:612-666 (no group in the existing writer test). Plan lines 88, 101, 128.
findings.claim: `build_trades` builds a `TradeKey::Group` from the trips of every member trade whatever instrument or account each is in, then suppresses those trips as trades of their own (`used`), in group order (a trade in two groups goes to the first). Part B says `build_trades` takes 'the families (or their trips…)' to build; a group whose trips lie in two families is rebuilt correctly only if the keyed rebuild maps trip → group and re-applies the `used` rule, which the plan does not state. The property test's writes (insert/revise/remove a record, links, adjustments, open/move/orphan a trade, a journal entry) never save a group, and `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` has none either, so the omission would not be caught.
findings.failing_scenario: Group G = {trade on trip X of instrument X, trade on trip Y of unrelated instrument Y}. A sale of X is added. Fresh build: G's slices, qty, pnl, pnl_cad, last_on and status change, and X's trip is still absent from the list (used by G). Keyed rebuild of family {X} alone: G keeps its old figures, and X's trip is emitted as a trade of its own beside G (the `used` set was not consulted), so the Trades list shows X twice: once inside G's stale figure and once alone.
findings.required_change: Keep an index trip → group in the engine; a change reaching a trip rebuilds every group holding it and re-applies the `used` rule over all groups in book order; add 'save a group of two trades on unrelated instruments, and remove it' to the generator's writes and to the existing writer test.

verdicts.why: The plan does not handle this and the tests it proposes cannot catch it. On master, build_trades (rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:305-338) builds each saved group from the trips of all its members whatever instrument or account they are in (trade→trip via identity.trade_of, line 305), takes the group's slices directly from matched.trips[k].slices (line 320), marks those trips `used` (line 323) and suppresses them as trades of their own (line 329). A group spanning two instruments is legal record state: Book::add_group validates nothing about members (rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408-429); its only caller is the legacy import (rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:262-281), whose own test fixture saves a group with members on two different symbols (rust/crates/server/src/legacy_import.rs:773); the reference model collapses a saved group from any member slices (rust/crates/model/src/trades.rs:189-199); SPEC trade-15 says a group joins "any trades". Today the engine is correct only because Change::Ledger/Trades/Groups/Journal all call build_trades over everything (rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:448-468). The plan replaces that with keyed rebuilds by family (lines 88, 101) and lists five match-level couplings (lines 90-97); none joins a group's member trips across families, and the plan never states a trip→group index or re-applying the `used` rule. A record change to instrument X therefore reaches family {X} only: the group's figure (slices, qty, pnl, pnl_cad, last_on, status) stays stale, and X's trip is rebuilt as TradeKey::Trip(X) without the `used` check, so it appears twice. The acceptance tests would not see it: the existing writer test (rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:612-666) runs on pulled_book (tests_common.rs:68-77), a replay pull with no legacy import and so no group; the plan's generated books and write list (line 128) contain no group, so the "right to refuse" clause (line 148, "the property test would show it") cannot fire for this coupling. Severity medium is right: groups exist only on books that came through the legacy import, but on those the Trades list would show a wrong group P&L and a duplicate trade after an ordinary sale.
verdicts.evidence: trades.rs:305 `let trip_of_trade: BTreeMap<TradeId, &TripKey> = identity.trade_of.iter().map(|(k, t)| (*t, k)).collect();` trades.rs:308-325 groups built first from members' trips, `used.extend(trips)`; trades.rs:329 `if used.contains(key) || managed(...) { continue; }`; trades.rs:320 group slices from `matched.trips.get(k)...t.slices`. book/src/trades.rs:421-426 inserts members with no check. legacy_import.rs:773 fixture `"members": ["b1|s1|10.00000000", "gone|x|1.00000000"]` (two symbols in one group). engine.rs:456-461 Change::Groups rebuilds all trades today. Plan line 97 families joined by the five couplings only; line 101 build_trades takes "the families (or their trips...)"; line 128 generator writes: record insert/revise/remove, transfer link, adjustment, open/move/orphan a trade, journal entry — no group; line 148 relies on the property test to reveal a missing coupling. tests_common.rs:68-77 pulled_book is a replay pull, no legacy import.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not cover it. build_trades (rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:296-341) builds TradeKey::Group from trip_of_trade over every member whatever its instrument or account, then suppresses those trips from the per-trip pass through `used`, first group winning. Groups with members on unrelated instruments are reachable: Book::add_group (rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408-429) places no constraint on members, its only caller is the legacy import (rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:277) which brings the old app's groups over, and SPEC.md:51 says a saved group joins "any trades". The plan's families are defined only by the five match couplings (plan lines 90-95); groups are not a match coupling and line 152's self-check ("no family the engine keeps that the match does not use") steers away from adding one. Line 101 has build_trades take "the families (or their trips…)" and compares only recomputed entries, with no trip→group mapping and no re-application of the `used` rule, so a literal build rebuilds TradeKey::Trip(X) for the reached family, leaves TradeKey::Group(G) at its old figure, and emits X's trip as its own trade beside G (the fresh build would have suppressed it). The right-to-refuse clause (line 148) relies on the property test surfacing a missed coupling, but line 128's generated books and writes name no group at all. The existing tests also cannot catch it: each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would (figures.rs:612-666) and the pulled_book fixture (tests_common.rs) carry no group; the engine's changes.rs test does hold a two-instrument group (line 128) but applies every change independently to `base` (lines 181-187) built from tests/fixtures/book.json, which has zero groups, so its ledger change (the late sale of X) never runs with a group present. Severity stays medium: a visible wrong Trades list (a stale group figure and a trade shown twice) but only for books holding legacy groups across instruments, after a ledger change reaching one member.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:305 `let trip_of_trade: BTreeMap<TradeId, &TripKey> = identity.trade_of.iter().map(|(k, t)| (*t, k)).collect();` :306 `let mut used: BTreeSet<TripKey>`; :308-325 groups loop over `inputs.ledger.groups` with `!used.contains(*k)` and `used.extend(trips)`; :327-331 per-trip pass skips `used.contains(key)`. rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408 `pub fn add_group(&self, members: &[TradeId], locked: bool, legacy_key: Option<&str>, at)` inserts members with no instrument/account check; sole caller rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:277. SPEC.md:51 "a saved group joins them, as it does any trades." Plan line 90-95 lists five match couplings only; line 101 "`build_trades` ... take the families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts) to build ... only the recomputed entries are compared"; line 128 property test writes: "insert, revise and remove a record ...; add and remove a transfer link; set and clear an adjustment; open, move and orphan a trade; a journal entry" (no group); line 152 "no family the engine keeps that the match does not use". rust/crates/engine/tests/changes.rs:181-187 applies each change to `base.clone()` independently; `grep -c '"groups"' tests/fixtures/book.json` = 0. rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:612-666 writes: quote, ex-dividend, declared, rates, mark_removed, cash/buying power, clock — no group; tests_common.rs has no match for "group".

findings.title: An `account` change is logged but reaches no family, while `managed`, `coin_minimum` and the account type feed the match, identity, trades and the broker check
findings.where: Plan line 74 (`account` kind from `accounts`, `broker_connections`) against plan lines 97 and 101 (a change reaches the families of the transactions, instruments and adjustments it names; `Entity::Book` updated by key). Code: rust/crates/engine/src/identity.rs:61-63,69-71 (managed skips trips), rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:329 (managed skips trades), rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:19-21,30 (coin_minimum from the connection's broker), rust/crates/engine/src/dust.rs:20,32 and ledger.rs:1201,1427 (dust decided in the match), rust/crates/engine/src/equity.rs:214 (margin decides held()).
findings.claim: The log records writes to `accounts` and `broker_connections`, but 'what a change can reach' never names an account, and part B rebuilds only `Entity::Book`'s accounts for it. A revision of an account row that changes `managed` or its kind alters identity and the trades (every trip of the account) and, through `coin_minimum`, the match of every coin holding in it; a fresh build reflects that, a keyed apply that only updates `BookFig.accounts` does not. The generator's writes never touch an account, so neither property test would see it.
findings.failing_scenario: Account A's row is revised so that `account_type` becomes `Known { managed: true, .. }` (the `accounts` trigger writes `account A`). Fresh build: `identify` and `build_trades` skip every trip in A, so A has no trades and `needs_trade` lists none of them. Keyed engine: `BookFig.accounts` moves, the trades of A stay listed with their ids, `settle_trades` keeps them; `differences` against a fresh build would report them, but the property test as written never makes this write, so the gap ships.
findings.required_change: Define what an `account` change reaches: every family with a holding or cash in the account (rematch for `coin_minimum`/kind, re-identify and rebuild trades for `managed`, recheck for the margin flag), or show which `AccountInfo` fields can change after creation and that each is inert; add account revisions (status, kind, managed) to the generator's writes.

verdicts.why: The failing scenario requires an `accounts` row to be revised after creation (account_type becoming managed, a kind change, a connection change). No writer on master can make that write. The book crate's only statement touching `accounts` is the INSERT in `Book::add_account` (rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:85-89); there is no `UPDATE accounts` or `UPDATE broker_connections` anywhere under rust/ (grepped case-insensitively, including `accounts SET`/`ON CONFLICT`). `add_account_ref` writes only `account_refs` (identity.rs:106-109), a table `engine_inputs::ledger` does not read. The pull adds an account only when its ref is unknown and never revises an existing one's status or type (rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:121-128); the old-store import does the same (rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:235-256). The only DELETE of `accounts` is `Book::clear` (rust/crates/book/src/clear.rs:257-269), which removes only accounts with no transactions, holds, statements, links or backing, and the server follows every clear with a full `f.rebuild(now)` (rust/crates/server/src/clear.rs:155,177), which the plan keeps (line 139, and the full build at a start/rebuild is in "What stays the same"). A migration runs at open, before the start's whole build. So the fields the finding names (`managed`, kind via `is_margin` at scope.rs:732-734, `coin_minimum` derived at engine_inputs.rs:19-21,30 from the connection's never-updated `broker` column) are immutable for the life of an account row; an `account` log entry can only be a fresh insert, which holds no transactions yet and reaches no family, and the plan's `Entity::Book` update by key (line 101) is exactly what that needs. The alternative the finding offers ("show which AccountInfo fields can change after creation and that each is inert") is already true of the code: none can change. The property test's generator omitting account revisions therefore misses nothing a writer can do; the acceptance criterion at line 128 is scoped to "the book's own writers", and the book has no account-revising writer. At most the plan could state this immutability in one sentence so a future account-revising writer knows it must widen the reach; that is a note, not a wrong figure.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:63-98 (`add_account`: INSERT only), :101-113 (`add_account_ref`: INSERT INTO account_refs only); grep for `UPDATE accounts|UPDATE broker_connections|accounts SET|broker_connections SET` over rust/: no matches; grep for `INSERT ... accounts` in book/src: only identity.rs:86; rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:119-130 (existing account found by ref is reused untouched); rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:223-256 (existing account gains refs only; new one inserted); rust/crates/book/src/clear.rs:257-269 (deletes only accounts naming no transactions/holds/statements/links/backing) and rust/crates/server/src/clear.rs:155-177 (`book.clear` then `f.rebuild(now)`); rust/crates/engine/src/scope.rs:732-734 (`is_margin` reads account_type only); rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:19-21,26-31 (`coin_minimum` from `broker_connections.broker`, never updated); plan lines 74, 97, 101, 128, 139.

verdicts.why: The failing scenario ("Account A's row is revised so that account_type becomes Known { managed: true, .. }") cannot be produced by any writer the book has on master. The `accounts` table is written by exactly two statements: the INSERT in `Book::add_account` (rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:85-89) and the DELETE in `clear.rs:257-269`, which removes only accounts with no transactions, record holds, statements, buying power, days, links, activity reads or margin backing. There is no `UPDATE accounts` or `UPDATE broker_connections` anywhere under rust/crates (case-insensitive, multiline grep found none); `broker_connections` has only the INSERT at identity.rs:36 and the DELETE at clear.rs:271-274 (only a connection no account or record names). The pull, the one path that re-reads accounts from the broker, looks the account up by ref and, when found, uses it as is (rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:121-128): a changed `account_type`, `open` or nickname at the broker is not written. The old-app import (book/src/import/mod.rs:224-255) adds accounts or refs, never revises one. So every field of `AccountInfo` the finding names (`managed`, kind for `is_margin`, status, `coin_minimum` which is fixed by the connection's broker since neither `connection_id` nor `broker` is ever updated, `broker_label`) is immutable after creation. The only `account` log entries the book can produce today are an insert of an account that has no transactions yet (hence no family, no trips, no trades, no dust decision) and a delete of an account that clear.rs has already proved has none; both are what plan line 101 handles (`Entity::Book`'s accounts updated by key, read at scope.rs:729 and :861 straight from `ledger.accounts`). The property test's generator "writes through the book's own writers" therefore cannot miss an account revision: there is no such writer, and no figure can come out different from a fresh build through this path. The finding does not cite a writer that revises an account, and the "required change" offers as its alternative exactly the demonstration above. At most this is a latent coupling for a future writer (a pull that one day stores a changed status or type), worth a one-line note in the plan's "What a change can reach", not a correctness gap in what ships.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:33-40 (add_connection: the only INSERT into broker_connections; no update function exists); identity.rs:63-98 (add_account: INSERT INTO accounts, the only write of kind/registration/managed/joint/status/nickname); identity.rs:101-113 (add_account_ref writes account_refs only); rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:121-128 (`match book.account_by_ref(&r)? { Some(id) => id, None => { ... book.add_account(...) } }`: an existing account is not revised, its stated type and open flag unused); rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:224-255 (old-app import adds accounts or refs only); rust/crates/book/src/clear.rs:257-269 (DELETE FROM accounts only for ids in no transactions, record_holds, statements, buying_power, account_days, account_links, activity_reads, margin_backing) and :271-274 (DELETE FROM broker_connections only when no account, record or broker_read names it); grep for `UPDATE\s+accounts|accounts\s+SET|UPDATE\s+broker_connections|broker_connections\s+SET` over rust/crates: no matches. rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:26-32: coin_minimum derives from the connection's broker, which is never updated. Engine readers of ledger.accounts: identity.rs:62, equity.rs:214, dust.rs:20,32, scope.rs:729,861, engine.rs:307 — all keyed by an account whose row cannot change after insert. Plan lines 88 (delta per keyed collection, accounts included), 101 (Entity::Book by key), 139 (Book::clear empties the log with the record).

findings.title: Turning `beyond`, `unit_disagreements`, `unapplied` and `stock_dividends` into maps 'by the transaction' loses entries, since one transaction can produce several
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1965 (Beyond per cash leg of an event, keyed by the anchor), 1202-1204 and 1590 (per transaction), 1520 via 1822/1844/1874 (UnitsDisagree for `from` and for `to` under one anchor), 1156-1158 and 1792-1799 (unapplied pushed once per failing leg of one event), 1832 (StockDividend per `from` leg under one anchor); readers: rust/crates/server/src/status.rs:206-215 (one line per Beyond), rust/crates/engine/src/cashflow.rs:83-97 (one CashRow per StockDividend, `id: s.transaction`), rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:617 (Entity::CashRow keyed by that id). Plan line 99.
findings.claim: None of these lists is positional in meaning, but several are not unique per transaction: an event anchor appears once per leg in `beyond`, `unit_disagreements`, `unapplied` and `stock_dividends`. A map keyed by the transaction alone keeps one of them. Because `differences` does not compare `Matched`, and `diff` collapses CashRow entities sharing an id into one map entry (engine.rs:212-213), the loss is invisible to the equality test.
findings.failing_scenario: A merger-for-cash adjustment with two `from` legs (the holder receives cash for units of P and of Q under one anchor row), each closing more units than the book held: today `beyond` holds two rows {anchor, P, left_p} and {anchor, Q, left_q} and the status page prints two sentences. A map by transaction keeps the last; one sentence disappears; `differences` is empty. The same anchor with two stock-dividend legs produces two cash rows with one id today (already colliding in `diff`); a cash map by id keeps one, and the Cashflow total drops a payment with nothing reported.
findings.required_change: Key each by what makes it unique in the match: (transaction, instrument) for beyond, unit_disagreements and stock_dividends, a Vec or merged Gaps per transaction for unapplied; give stock-dividend cash rows an id that includes the instrument (or keep a Vec keyed per family); and include these collections in the equality comparison.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's words do not handle it. On master every collection named is a Vec (ledger.rs:326-344) and several are pushed more than once under one transaction id: `Beyond` per `from` leg of one adjustment anchor (ledger.rs:1965, inside `apply_leg`, which the leg loop at 1792 calls per leg), `UnitsDisagree` per leg at 1520 (from 1822, 1844 for `from`, 1874 for `to`), `unapplied` per failing leg at 1797 via 1157, `StockDividend` per qualifying leg at 1832. The book's writer accepts any number of legs naming any instruments (facts.rs:429-455), and the engine builds `before` per `from` (1787) and `event_groups` over every named instrument (2185), so a multi-instrument adjustment is a supported shape, not a malformed one. Plan line 99 says these become "a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about" — an alternative, not a composite; neither key alone is unique (by holding alone, two sales each beyond on one holding also collapse). The acceptance test at plan line 128 relies on `Engine::differences` (engine.rs:644 → `compare`, 608-640), which compares trades, positions, cash, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, brokers and the book figure and never reads `matched.beyond`, `unit_disagreements` or `unapplied`; stock dividends reach it only as cash rows keyed `Entity::CashRow(r.id)` with `id = s.transaction` (cashflow.rs:84, engine.rs:617) and `diff` collects into a `BTreeMap<Entity,_>` (engine.rs:212-213), so duplicates collapse before comparison. The page effect is real: status.rs:206-215 prints one sentence per `Beyond` row, so a merger-for-cash adjustment with two `from` legs each closing beyond the book would show one sentence instead of two after a change, differing from master's full build, with the property test green. Severity lowered to low rather than medium because: `unit_disagreements` and `unapplied` have no server reader but the `compare` tool (grep over crates excluding tests), so their loss is not page-visible and the shared test harness already collapses `unapplied` by id (cases.rs:819); `disagreements` is already unique per transaction; the stock-dividend half is already a latent duplicate-id defect on master (views.rs:814 drains rows into a HashMap by id and build.rs:1082 asserts cash ids unique) and needs two stock-dividend legs with a stated cost under one anchor; and the reachable `beyond` scenario needs a hand-entered multi-instrument event, rare in practice. What stands is the plan's gap: the key named is not unique for `beyond` and `stock_dividends`, and the equality criterion cannot detect the loss, so the plan should name the key as (transaction, account, instrument) and add these `Matched` collections to the comparison.
verdicts.evidence: Checked: ledger.rs:323-344 (Matched Vec fields); 1156-1158 and 1792-1799 (unapplied pushed once per failing leg of one anchor); 1202-1204, 1384, 1398, 1407, 1496, 1590, 1688, 1749 (beyond per transaction/instrument) and 1965 (`self.out.beyond.push(Beyond { transaction: anchor.clone(), account, instrument: from, qty: left })` per cash leg); 1510-1521 check_units pushing `UnitsDisagree { transaction: anchor.clone(), account, instrument, .. }` from 1822, 1844, 1874; 1832 StockDividend per `to == from && cost` leg; 1780-1799 leg loop and 1787 `before` keyed by each leg's `from`; 2185 `named` over every leg's from/to. facts.rs:425-455 write_adjustments: legs validated only for naming some instrument. engine.rs:208-224 `diff` collects `BTreeMap<Entity,&T>`; 608-640 `compare` lists the collections compared (no Matched lists); 617 CashRow keyed by `r.id`; 644-652 `differences` = compare + quotes. cashflow.rs:83-97 one CashRow per StockDividend with `id: s.transaction.clone()`. status.rs:206-215 one sentence per Beyond. scope.rs:928-931 cashflow totals over the row Vec. views.rs:811-816 rows drained into `HashMap<String, CashflowRow>` by id; wire/build.rs:1082 asserts cash row ids unique. Server readers of unit_disagreements/unapplied/disagreements outside tests: only compare.rs:497-503. Existing multi-leg adjustment cases: event_units.json:55, review_fixes.json:110 (both legs from X). Plan lines 99 ("a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about"), 101 (collections "held by key", recomputed entries compared), 128 (equality held through `Engine::differences`).

verdicts.why: The code facts hold and the plan does not cover them, but the shapes that produce the loss are not reachable from any writer the product has today, so the visible consequence is latent rather than medium. findings.title: `Matched.cash` per (account, family) summed is not the running sum the fresh build makes: the two differ when a partial sum overflows
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2244-2251 (one running checked_add in ledger order, Err sticky), rust/crates/engine/src/equity.rs:121,140,153-155 (the account's own cash compared with the broker's); plan line 99.
findings.claim: Today each account's cash in a currency is one running `checked_add` over every transaction in ledger order, and once it fails it stays Err. Summing per family and then across families changes the grouping; exact decimal addition is associative only while every partial fits, so a grouping that overflows in one path and not in the other gives Err in one engine and a value in the other.
findings.failing_scenario: Account A, CAD rows in ledger order: +7e28, +7e28, −7e28 (the first two on instrument X, the third on Y). Fresh build: Err(arithmetic) after the second row, sticky, so the broker check says 'cannot sum it'. Keyed engine: family {X} share = Err, family {Y} share = −7e28 → the account total is Err too in this order, but with rows +7e28 (X), −7e28 (Y), +7e28 (X): fresh build: 7e28 − 7e28 + 7e28 = Ok(7e28); keyed: family {X} = 7e28 + 7e28 = Err → Err. The broker check for A differs from a fresh build; the property test sees it only if a broker statement exists for A.
findings.required_change: Make the total order-free in both paths (sum each family exactly, then the families, in the full build too), or keep one running sum keyed by transaction recomputed for the account on any change to it; and generate broker statements so the check is compared.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it. On master, `match_lots` ends with one running `checked_add` per (account, currency) over `ledger.transactions` in ledger order, and an Err is sticky (`if let Ok(total) = e` skips every later row). `Dec::checked_add` refuses an overflow of rust_decimal's 96-bit mantissa (max ≈ 7.92e28) and also an `Inexact` sum, so checked addition is not associative: whether a partial sum fails depends on the grouping. Plan line 99 says `Matched.cash` becomes per-(account, family) shares "summed per account", and line 99 also says `match_lots` runs "exactly as today over their transactions only", so a family's share is a running sum over only its rows. The finding's second scenario checks out numerically: rows +7e28 (X), −7e28 (Y), +7e28 (X) give Ok(7e28) in the fresh build but family X = 7e28 + 7e28 = 1.4e29 → Overflow → Err in the keyed engine, so the account's `own` cash in `broker_checks` (equity.rs:140-154) differs from a fresh build, contradicting plan line 36 ("exactly those of a fresh build"). Nothing bounds a transaction's cash at write (`records.rs:400-434` stores the Dec's text as given), and 7e28 is exactly the `HUGE` amount the engine's own tests use for this failure path (scope.rs:1124, 1135-1138, 1142-1149), where the codebase deliberately specifies the sticky-Err behaviour. The claim that the plan's property test would miss it is also right: `matched.cash` is read by nothing but `broker_checks` (equity.rs:121; cashflow.rs does not read it), `Engine::differences` compares only the snapshot parts (trades, positions, cash rows, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, brokers, book), and a check exists only for an account in `inputs.market.brokers`; the plan's property test (line 128) lists no broker statements among its generated inputs or writes. Low severity is right: the amounts are unreal for any brokerage book, and the visible effect is one broker check reading "cannot sum" instead of a value (or vice versa).
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2244-2251 — `for t in &ledger.transactions { if let Some(c) = t.cash { let e = m.out.cash.entry(t.account).or_default().entry(c.currency).or_insert(Ok(Dec::ZERO)); if let Ok(total) = e { *e = total.checked_add(c.amount).map_err(Gaps::from); } } }` (one running sum in ledger order, Err sticky). rust/crates/core/src/dec.rs:204-214 — `checked_add` returns `Overflow` when rust_decimal's `checked_add` fails and `Inexact` when the scale drops; dec.rs:6-7 states an overflowing addition "is an error rather than a rounded value". rust/crates/engine/src/scope.rs:1124 `const HUGE: &str = "70000000000000000000000000000";` and :1135-1138, :1142-1149 — the suite asserts that HUGE + HUGE is an arithmetic gap and that the gap is sticky from that day on. rust/crates/engine/src/equity.rs:121 `let own_cash = matched.cash.get(account)...` and :140-154 — the only reader of `matched.cash`; the difference is pushed when `o != Ok(br)` with `own: o` carrying Ok or Err. rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:589-634, 644-652 — `differences` compares `snapshot(Parts::ALL)`: trades, positions, cash rows, payers, equity, checks, benchmarks, brokers, book; `matched.cash` is not among them except through `checks`, built from `inputs.market.brokers` (equity.rs:115-118). rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:400-434 — `insert_transaction` stores `m.amount.to_text()` with no bound. Plan lines 36 ("the engine's figures after any change stay exactly those of a fresh build"), 99 ("`match_lots` ... runs exactly as today over their transactions only ... Each account's cash totals (`Matched.cash`) are kept per (account, family) and summed per account"), 128 (property test inputs and writes name no broker statements), 148 (right to refuse covers only a missing coupling, which the property test would have to show).

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says on master: ledger.rs:2244-2251 keeps one running Dec::checked_add per (account, currency) in ledger order with Err sticky, and Dec::checked_add (core/src/dec.rs:207-214) fails on Overflow (the 96-bit mantissa, ~7.9e28) or Inexact (a lost scale), so Err-ness is grouping-dependent. But the finding's failing scenario compares the keyed engine against a fresh build that keeps master's single running sum, and that is not the plan's design. Plan line 99 makes Matched.cash a map per (account, family) summed per account; a full build under the plan is match_lots over every family (line 82 "built whole, as now", line 99 "takes the set of families"), and a per-(account, family) map can only be produced by summing each family on its own, so the fresh build and the incremental engine compute the same family shares (each a running sum over that family's transactions in ledger order, a function of the ledger state) and sum them the same way. The property test at line 128 compares against Engine::build under the plan, not master, so the scenario the finding builds (fresh Ok(7e28) vs keyed Err) does not arise between the two paths the plan promises equal. What remains is at most a nit the finding does not argue: the cross-family sum should be in a deterministic family order, and that only matters when partial sums of Ok shares themselves overflow 96 bits or need 29 significant digits. Reaching any of this needs a cash amount of ~7e28 (29 digits) or a fiat cash amount with 28 decimal places in one account's record; the broker's amounts are 2-place fiat, so only a hand-written CSV can place one (csv.rs:458 keeps the parsed Dec unbounded, dec.rs:101-119 accepts up to 28 places and the 96-bit max). On such a book the broker check already reports a difference either way (the broker never states 7e28), so neither Err nor Ok(7e28) is a figure the plan can make wrong in a way a person could act on. Versus master, a book holding ±7e28 rows would flip Ok to Err under the per-family grouping, but line 36's "every figure keeps its definition" is about SPEC.md's definitions, and the sum is still the same exact sum where it fits. Given the plan's grouping is the same in both paths and the amounts needed are not ones a broker produces, the finding is refuted at the plan-review level; the only follow-up worth a line in the build is to sum families in a stable key order.

findings.title: A record's legs are applied as one unit at the first leg's position; the family builder must keep a record's legs in one family, and the plan's coupling list and generator do not say so
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2137-2143 (`record_rank` over all a record's legs), 2197-2242 (`one_day`: every leg of the record applied where its first leg falls, each next the first that meets an opposite), 690-700; producers: rust/crates/wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:498-562 (multi-leg order legs, one per `securityId`), 743,769 (conversion legs, cash only). Plan lines 90-97, 99, 128, 148.
findings.claim: The order a transaction is applied in depends on the other legs of its record: its record's rank at the instant, and, for a same-day multi-leg record, the position of the record's first leg and the meets-opposite rule among the legs. Matching 'exactly as today over their transactions only' holds only if every leg of a record is in the family being matched. Today's producers keep legs on contracts of one underlying (joined by coupling 2, assumed, not enforced in `multi_leg`) or on cash; the plan's list does not name the record itself as a coupling, so a future or unexpected record whose legs name unrelated instruments is split, and the generator would not produce one to show it.
findings.failing_scenario: Record R, one day: leg1 buy X stating no time (bucket 0), leg2 sell 10 Y at 15:00. Record S: buy 10 Y at 10:00. Full match: `t` = leg1, `one_day` applies leg1 and leg2 before S, so the Y sale finds nothing and is `beyond`, S then opens a lot. Family-only match of {Y}: S at 10:00 then leg2 at 15:00 closes the lot with a realized slice. Y's trade, position and P&L differ.
findings.required_change: Add 'the legs of one record' to the couplings (join every instrument a record's legs name), or assert in the family builder that a record's legs fall in one family and refuse otherwise; add a record whose legs name two unrelated instruments to the generator so the right-to-refuse clause can fire.

verdicts.why: The mechanism the finding describes is real on master: a record's legs are a coupling in the match (ledger.rs:2137-2143 sorts each leg by `record_rank` over all the record's legs; 2225-2240 applies a same-day record's legs as one unit where its first leg sorts, each next the first that meets an opposite; 2214 treats a record differently when it has one leg), and the plan's coupling list (lines 90-97) does not name it, nor does the generator (line 128) make a record whose legs name unrelated instruments. But the failing scenario cannot occur with any writer in the codebase, so no figure comes out different from a fresh build. The scenario needs one record with legs at different instants (leg1 stating no time, leg2 at 15:00) or with heterogeneous effects on independent instruments. Every multi-leg producer drafts all legs from one `Base`, so they share `occurred_at` and `trade_date` (mapping.rs:355-360); `multi_leg` (498-562) draws legs from one Wealthsimple order, which is an options strategy on one underlying (joined by coupling 2); `conversion` (743, 769) is cash only (one cash family per account); CSV rows and manual entries are single-leg (`row_leg`). The finding's own premise is also incomplete: `moves` (mapping.rs:961-995) and `institutional` (1195-1200) do write one record with legs on many unrelated instruments plus cash, so today's book already has records split across the plan's families, and I traced those: all legs are the same kind at one instant, `record_rank` is the same for any subset (every leg is effect None with the same `acquires` sign, 690-700), `meets_opposite` is false for `Move::Transfer` (1527), `apply_transfer` ignores `record_legs`, `record_units` overwrites per day (1246-1262), and legs sharing (date, bucket, occurred_at, rank, source_key) are contiguous in `txs`, so applying them as a unit equals applying each at its own position: the split changes nothing. A corporate event record with an adjustment is consumed as one group (1755-1760) and joined by coupling 3; one without an adjustment has each leg applied independently (1731-1753), and its subset rank differs only on an exact `occurred_at` tie with another record on the same instrument, which is a separate and negligible corner, not the finding's scenario. The plan's right-to-refuse clause (148) already commits to adding any coupling that breaks equality. What remains is a defensive note (the generator would not show a record shape no producer writes), which is not a wrong figure or behaviour; under the default-to-refuted rule this does not stand as a finding.

findings.title: The plan says no-instrument transactions reach only the cash family, but a multi-leg order naming no instrument taints every holding of the account
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1283-1318 (the leg-unstated branch runs before `let Some(instrument) = t.instrument else { return }`; `None` names `account_taint` and every book of the account), 840-849 (`book()` merges `account_taint` into every holding touched afterwards). Plan line 97 ('Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only') against line 95 (coupling 5).
findings.claim: A transaction with no instrument whose record carries the `leg-unstated` problem does not touch cash only: it taints every holding the account has at that point and every holding touched later, so its family is the whole account. The sentence at line 97, built literally, would reach the cash family alone for an insert, revision or removal of such a row, leaving the account's holdings' taints as they were.
findings.failing_scenario: Account A holds X and Y. A pull stores a multi-leg row with no instrument and `leg-unstated` dated before both. Fresh build: every X and Y figure in A waits on `leg-unstated` (gaps on positions, slices' taint on trades). Keyed apply per line 97: the row joins A's cash family, cash totals move, X and Y keep their stated figures. Removing the row later leaves the taint in place the same way.
findings.required_change: State that a no-instrument transaction's family is decided by its record's problems: with `leg-unstated` it is the whole account (coupling 5), otherwise the cash family; the generator's 'a multi-leg order naming no instrument' must be inserted, revised and removed both before and after holdings exist so both directions are held.

verdicts.why: The code is as the finding says, but the plan already handles the case; the finding rests on reading one sentence of line 97 in isolation from the sentence before it and from the acceptance test. Line 95 lists coupling 5 explicitly: "every holding of an account, where a multi-leg order names no instrument (`account_taint`)". Line 97's first sentence then says the engine keeps "a disjoint-set over instruments, plus the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint". On master the only writer of `account_taint` is ledger.rs:1310, the `None` branch for a no-instrument `leg-unstated` row, so "accounts made whole by an account-wide taint" can only mean that such a row reaches the whole account; the later parenthetical "(cash moved)" distinguishes ordinary cash movements from that row, it does not reassign the multi-leg row to the cash family. The acceptance criterion at line 128 generates books containing "a multi-leg order naming no instrument", applies "insert, revise and remove a record, back-dated and today" through the book's writers, and holds `Engine::differences` against a fresh `Engine::build` after every step, so an implementation that put the row in the cash family alone would fail the test on exactly the finding's scenario (back-dated insert taints X and Y in a fresh build, not in the keyed apply; removal the reverse). Line 148 commits to adding any coupling the test shows missing rather than working around it. The finding's "required change" is a wording clarification plus a test case the property test already generates, not a figure the plan as written would get wrong.
