findings.title: Collections held by key change the order the page's tie-breaks and index-based views rely on, and the key-based comparison cannot see it
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:339 (trades sorted last_on desc), rust/crates/engine/src/cashflow.rs:98 (cash rows newest first), rust/crates/engine/src/scope.rs:475-481,600-602,739 (indexes into the slices, 'in the engine's order'), rust/crates/server/src/views.rs:640-650,811-815 (column sorts whose ties fall to input order), rust/crates/server/src/wire/build.rs:603,633,652-655 (positions and cash rows by index). Plan line 101.
findings.claim: `Engine::differences` compares by entity key (engine.rs:211-230), so the order of `trades`, `positions` and `cash` is outside the equality test. The views re-sort by the chosen column, but equal keys keep the engine's order, and `Portfolio.positions`, `Cashflow.rows` and `IncomeHolding.position` are indexes into the slices. Holding the collections 'by key' (BTreeMap by TradeKey / TransactionId) presents them in key order unless a sorted view is kept.
findings.failing_scenario: Two trades closed on the same day: today the list shows them by closed_at then key (trades.rs:339); keyed by TradeKey they come in opening-transaction order; the Trades table sorted by Activity shows the pair swapped after a change compared with a restart, and nothing reports it.
findings.required_change: Keep the engine's sorted Vecs as the presented order (a keyed map behind them for replacement), or specify the order each keyed collection presents and make the views break ties themselves; the comparison stays key-based either way, so say which.

verdicts.why: The plan holds trades, positions and cash "by key" (line 101) and fixes an iteration order only for ledger.transactions (line 88); it names no presented order for the three collections while claiming nothing on screen changes (lines 36, 123). Its equality test is Engine::differences (line 128), which on master compares by Entity key through BTreeMaps (engine.rs:211-230, :609-653), so order is outside it; same_as_fresh (figures.rs:589-595) uses the same call. On master the Trades view under the default `activity` sort sorts on a single day-only value with a stable sort (views.rs:635-655, :670) over the engine's order (scope.rs:600-602), and the page shows the server's order verbatim (Trades.svelte:13); the engine's order is (last_on, closed_at, key) descending with closed_at a Timestamp (trades.rs:339, :69), which is how SPEC trades-8 ("a closed one by its close") is met for two trades closed the same day. Keyed by TradeKey, two same-day closes at 10:00 and 15:00 would show by opening transaction rather than by moment of close, a visible departure from SPEC and from master that the acceptance test cannot report. The one imprecision is that with a BTreeMap the order after a change equals the order after a restart (both key order), so the departure is from master/SPEC rather than between a change and a restart; with a Vec replaced in place the finding's own reading also holds. Cash rows are weaker (views.rs:811 and SPEC cashflow-37 break ties by symbol then account). Severity stays low: no figure's value is wrong, only the order of ties on the default sort, and the fix is to specify the presented order and have the comparison or the views cover it.
verdicts.evidence: engine.rs:211-230 `fn diff` builds `BTreeMap<Entity, &T>` for before and after and compares per key; engine.rs:644-653 `differences` calls `compare(&other.snapshot(Parts::ALL))`. figures.rs:589-595 `same_as_fresh` asserts `e.differences(&fresh)` is empty, nothing on order. trades.rs:339 `out.sort_by(|a, b| (b.last_on, b.closed_at, &b.key).cmp(&(a.last_on, a.closed_at, &a.key)))`; trades.rs:67-69 `last_on: Date`, `closed_at: Option<Timestamp>`. cashflow.rs:98 `rows.sort_by(|a, b| (b.day, b.at, &b.id).cmp(...))`. scope.rs:600-602 `trades_in_scope` "in the engine's order"; scope.rs:475-481 `rows: Vec<usize>` "indexes into the cashflow rows"; scope.rs:739 `idx: Vec<usize>` into positions; build.rs:603, 633 `&figs.positions[h.position]`, :652 `&figs.cash[*i]`. views.rs:640-655 `sorted_then` stable `sort_by` on the sort value, further values then input order; :635-637 `sorted` passes one value; :670 `"activity" => SortValue::Text(t.last_date.clone())`; :709-726 rows pushed in `trades_in_scope` order then `sorted`. web/src/lib/Trades.svelte:13 "the trades in scope, sorted by the server as the header says". SPEC.md:479 trades-8 "Newest activity first by default (an open trade by its latest fill, a closed one by its close)"; SPEC.md:801 cashflow-37 ties "by symbol and then account". Plan line 88 (transactions "read ... through an iterator in the record's order"), line 101 ("the engine's collections (`trades`, `positions`, `cash`) are held by key, and only the recomputed entries are compared"), lines 36 and 123 (nothing on screen changes; the match order kept), line 128 (`Engine::differences` against `Engine::build`).

verdicts.why: The mechanism is real and the plan does not handle it, but the failing scenario is misstated. Under the plan both a restart and an incremental apply would present the same keyed map, so "after a change compared with a restart" would not differ. What differs is master versus the plan: the engine's Vecs carry a total order (trades by (last_on, closed_at, key) desc, cash by (day, at, id) desc) that the views' stable single-column sorts fall back to on ties; a BTreeMap by TradeKey/TransactionId presents key-ascending order instead. Concrete case: two open trades each with a fill today (equal last_on, closed_at None) are listed today key-descending under the default Activity order and would be listed key-ascending after the plan, a visible swap. This contradicts plan line 36 ("Nothing on screen changes") and no acceptance criterion can see it: Engine::differences collects into BTreeMap<Entity> (order-blind) and the determinism digest in capacity.rs sorts its lines. Severity stays low: SPEC.md:479 fixes only "newest activity first" and does not define the tie, so no specified figure is wrong; the plan just needs to state the presented order of each keyed collection (keep the sorted Vec, or have the views break ties themselves).
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:211-230 — `diff` builds `BTreeMap<Entity, &T>` for before and after; order of the input iterators is lost. engine.rs:644-652 `differences` uses it. rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:339 — `out.sort_by(|a, b| (b.last_on, b.closed_at, &b.key).cmp(&(a.last_on, a.closed_at, &a.key)))`. rust/crates/engine/src/cashflow.rs:98 — `rows.sort_by(|a, b| (b.day, b.at, &b.id).cmp(&(a.day, a.at, &a.id)))`. rust/crates/engine/src/scope.rs:599-602 — `trades_in_scope` "in the engine's order". rust/crates/server/src/views.rs:706-726 — Trades::refresh takes that order and calls `sorted(&listed, dir)`; views.rs:631-654 — `sorted_then` is a stable `sort_by`, "a tie in all of them keeps the rows' own order"; views.rs:669 — `activity` sorts on `last_date` only. views.rs:811-815 — CashflowView adds symbol, account, then input order. scope.rs:476 `rows: Vec<usize>`; build.rs:603, 633, 655 index `figs.positions`/`figs.cash`; scope.rs:739 `idx` into positions. Plan line 101: "the engine's collections (trades, positions, cash) are held by key"; line 36: "Nothing on screen changes." Acceptance line 134's digest is capacity.rs:815-827 `figures_digest`, which ends with `out.sort()`, so it is order-insensitive too. SPEC.md:479 — "Newest activity first by default (an open trade by its latest fill, a closed one by its close)", no tie rule.

findings.title: The ×4 book grows breadth only; the growth rule cannot see the family's depth, and the 100 ms budget is measured on a ~15-row family while the owner's worst is 349
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:243-245 (sized: accounts, instruments, trades each ×times, months fixed); rust/crates/wealthsimple/src/generated.rs:365-374 (each trade picks an account and a share uniformly); capacity.rs:508-531, :585 (the probed instrument chosen by closes then name, and no closes are stored by the build: facts() at :457-460 stores quotes only); capacity.rs:688-705 (judge: GROWTH_LIMIT on ×1 vs ×4); rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1304, :1311 (books.keys().filter per multi-leg row), :2180-2191 (transactions scanned per adjustment), :2211-2216; plan lines 61, 133, 134
findings.claim: Under the plan an added trade's work is proportional to its instrument's family. In the ×4 preset trades per instrument stay at 646/157 ≈ 4 round trips (the generator draws the account and the listing uniformly, and all three counts scale together), so the probed family has the same ~10-25 transactions at both sizes. The judge's ratio then reads ≈1.0 whether the family match is O(depth) or O(depth²), and the 100 ms Pi budget is held on a family a twentieth of the owner's deepest (349 live transactions on one instrument, plan line 61). The Verification table and the acceptance criterion on the Capacity workflow would both pass without ever measuring the case the plan is for. Nor does the owner's-copy criterion (line 134) say which instrument the added trade is on.
findings.failing_scenario: Build the plan so that match_lots over a family does something quadratic in its rows (for example the event_groups scan at ledger.rs:2187 run per adjustment, or books.keys().filter at :1304 per multi-leg row, both now family-local but still a scan per row). Run `capacity run`: add-trade at ×1 and ×4 both match a ~15-row family, steps 25k → 26k, allocations 1.04×, Pi time 20 ms: within budget, off OVER_BUDGET, #420 closed. On the owner's book an added trade on the 349-row instrument then re-matches 349 rows with a 349-row scan each (120k scans), and a coin with weekly staking rows walks its hundreds of lots per sale; the 100 ms claim was never tested at that depth.
findings.required_change: Add a depth pair to the Capacity workflow beside the breadth pair: a preset whose accounts and instruments are the owner's but whose probed listing carries the owner's deepest count of rows (the generator takes a `deep` share of trades for one named listing, or a per-listing depth), and its ×4 (that listing four times deeper). The add-trade and import probes target the deepest family (most live transactions on the instrument), not the first by name. Judge the depth pair separately: the plan's own design is linear in the family, so GROWTH_LIMIT = 2 cannot apply to it; hold instead (a) the wall-time budget at depth ×4 of the owner's deepest, and (b) a sub-quadratic limit on steps and allocations (×4 depth: linear grows 4×, quadratic 16×; a limit near 6 tells them apart). Criterion 134 names the deepest instrument on the owner's copy. Answer to the CTO: nothing in match_lots needs an algorithmic change at 349 rows today, but the gate must measure depth now or the 100 ms criterion says nothing about the owner's worst add-trade.

verdicts.why: The finding's reading of the code is accurate (the ×4 preset grows breadth only; the probe picks the alphabetically first held share since no closes are stored; the judge's ×4/×1 ratio cannot see family depth; plan line 134 does not name the instrument), but its failing scenario produces no wrong figure and no wrong behaviour. The finding itself concedes nothing in match_lots needs an algorithmic change at 349 rows; the cited scans (ledger.rs:2187 per adjustment, :1304 per multi-leg row, :2211-2216 same-instant take_while) become family-bounded under the plan, and even a fully quadratic pass over the owner's deepest family (349 rows, ~120k cheap comparisons) is far under the 100 ms budget. The plan already reasons about depth at line 61 (the deepest instrument is about a twentieth of the book; a full rebuild at ×1 is ~180 ms Pi-equivalent, so a linear family match on the deepest is bounded near ~10 ms) and line 99 keeps the match as today, in the same order, over the family only, which is linear in practice. The Capacity gate catches what it claims (work not growing with the book); it never claimed to reproduce the owner's per-instrument distribution. Criterion 134 does time an added trade on the owner's real copy; the only real gap is that it does not pin the instrument to the deepest one, which is a one-line sharpening of a criterion, not a missed change, a doubled change, or a wrong state the page could show. A separate depth preset is a reasonable future improvement, not a defect in this plan.
verdicts.evidence: capacity.rs:243-245 `Size { accounts: OWNER.accounts * times, instruments: OWNER.instruments * times, trades: OWNER.trades * times, ..OWNER }` (months fixed). generated.rs:373-374 `let account = invest[r.below(invest.len())]; let under = shares[r.below(shares.len())];` (uniform draws, so ~646*0.9/157 ≈ 3.7 round trips per listing at every size). capacity.rs:457-460 stores quotes only; grep for `store_closes` in server/src hits only clear.rs:352 and read_sources.rs:436, so `closes` at :522 is 0 for every instrument and the sort at :526 falls through to name; :585 and :593 use `held.first()`. capacity.rs:49 `GROWTH_LIMIT: f64 = 2.0`; :688-705 judge compares four/one steps and allocs, and four.wall_ns × PI_SLOWDOWN (2.1) against budget_ms. Plan line 61: "the largest single instrument has 349 … about a twentieth of the book at worst"; line 99: "`match_lots` takes the set of families to match and runs exactly as today over their transactions only, in the same order"; line 134: "an added trade and a 20-row import on the copy, timed and counted, pasted in the PR" (instrument unnamed). Plan Verification table: add-trade 729 ms Pi at ×4 (so ~180 ms at ×1); a twentieth of that is ~10 ms, inside the 100 ms budget. ledger.rs:2180-2191 adjustment scan is over `ledger.transactions` per adjustment (family-local after the plan: 349 × adjustments on that instrument); :1304/:1311 `books.keys().filter` per multi-leg row over a family's few books; :2211-2216 take_while over same-instant rows only. The finding's own text: "nothing in match_lots needs an algorithmic change at 349 rows today".

verdicts.why: Every factual claim in the finding checks out on master, and the plan does not handle the gap. `sized()` (capacity.rs:243-245) multiplies accounts, instruments and trades by the same factor with months fixed, and the generator draws each trade's account and listing uniformly (generated.rs:373-374), so trades per instrument (646/157 ≈ 4) and rows per family are the same at ×1 and ×4. The probe's instrument is the held Security with the most closes then first by symbol (capacity.rs:508-528); the build stores only quotes (:457-460) and benchmark closes (:473-474), never instrument closes, so it is simply the first symbol by name, a family of roughly 15 rows at either size. `judge` (:688-705) holds the wall budget at ×4 and the ×1→×4 ratio under GROWTH_LIMIT. Once the plan makes an added trade's work proportional to its family (plan line 97-99, "runs exactly as today over their transactions only"), that ratio reads ≈1 whether the family match is linear or quadratic in its depth, and the 100 ms criterion (line 133) is held on a family a twentieth of the owner's deepest (349 live rows, line 61). The scans the finding names exist on master and would stay family-local but still per-row: the event_groups scan over every transaction per adjustment (ledger.rs:2180-2191) and `books.keys().filter` per unstated multi-leg row (:1304, :1311). Criterion 134 (the owner's copy) does not name the instrument, and if the same probe code is reused it picks by closes history, not by depth, so it does not cover the deepest family either. So criterion 133 is a test that cannot catch the thing the plan changes the cost driver to. Severity lowered to medium rather than high: the plan's design is linear in the family, the quadratic pieces on master only fire where a family has adjustments or unstated multi-leg rows, and a linear extrapolation of today's 730 ms over 7,151 rows gives ~36 ms for 349 rows, within budget; the harm is a blind verification gate under a careless implementation, not a wrong figure or a known-failing owner's case.
verdicts.evidence: capacity.rs:243-245 `Size { accounts: OWNER.accounts * times, instruments: OWNER.instruments * times, trades: OWNER.trades * times, seed, ..OWNER }` (months fixed at 36). generated.rs:373-374 `let account = invest[r.below(invest.len() as u64) as usize]; let under = shares[r.below(shares.len() as u64) as usize];`. capacity.rs:522-527 sorts held by `market.closes.get(&p.instrument).map_or(0, |c| c.len())` then symbol; the only closes the build stores are `cache.store_benchmark_closes` at :473-474 and quotes at :457-460, so every instrument has 0 closes and `held.first()` (:585 add-trade, :593 import) is the first symbol by name. capacity.rs:688-705: `pi_ms = four.wall_ns * PI_SLOWDOWN` against budget, and `r = four/one >= GROWTH_LIMIT` on steps, allocs, bytes read. ledger.rs:2180-2191: `for (applies_to, adj) in inputs.facts.adjustments.iter() { ... for t in &ledger.transactions { if t.kind == Kind::CorporateEvent && ... } }`; ledger.rs:1304 and :1311: `self.out.books.keys().filter(...)` per multi-leg row. Plan line 61: "the largest single instrument has 349"; line 97-99: families matched "exactly as today over their transactions only"; line 133: "add-trade and import meet the growth rule, then their budgets (100 ms answered; 1 s for a small import, on a Pi)"; line 134: "an added trade and a 20-row import on the copy, timed and counted, pasted in the PR" with no instrument named and no pass/fail. The plan's own Verification table (lines 158-161) reports only the breadth pair.

findings.title: settle_trades' `seen` map and identify's `anchors` stay O(trades) with a clone per trade: allocations that grow with the book after the book reads are keyed
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:82-91 (seen: every trade's Opening cloned into a BTreeMap on each loop pass), :92, :111 (book.trades() before and after); rust/crates/engine/src/identity.rs:48-56 (anchors: every trade's TransactionId cloned), :89-108 (every trade scanned, and :95 every trip per unclaimed trade); plan lines 31, 107
findings.claim: Plan C replaces the book reads in settle_trades with keyed ones but says nothing of the in-memory `seen` map, built from every trade the engine holds on every pass, nor of identify's `anchors`, which the plan says is updated per family but which is built from ledger.trades whole. An added trade always opens a round trip (needs_trade non-empty), so both run on every add-trade; their allocations are one or two per trade and the judge counts allocations.
findings.failing_scenario: At the owner's size the engine holds ~700 trades (646 round trips plus contracts); at ×4 ~2,800. `seen` and `anchors` each allocate a node and a cloned id per trade: roughly 2,000 allocations at ×1, 8,000 at ×4. If the keyed path's own cost is a few thousand allocations (a family match plus a handful of indexed reads), the allocation ratio lands between 2 and 3 and add-trade stays over the growth rule on allocations after everything the plan names is done; or, if a large constant hides it, the growth of this part is invisible and returns when the constant is cut.
findings.required_change: Hold `seen` and `anchors` by key: the engine keeps the trade-by-opening index as part of Identity and updates it from the trades delta; settle_trades reads only the trades its identity names (identity.moved, joined, unclaimed give the ids). Add these to the anti-stub self-check: no pass over ledger.trades on a change.

verdicts.why: The code reads as the finding says on master, but the plan already replaces those passes and its acceptance criteria mechanically catch any that survive. identity.rs:48-56 (anchors) and :89-91 clone a TransactionId per trade, figures.rs:82-91 (seen) clones an Opening per trade, and Leg is a String (ids.rs:122-123, :175-179) so each clone allocates; the probe's trade goes to the empty Manual account (capacity.rs:586, entries.rs:24/:142/:252) so it does open a round trip and the seen branch runs; the judge applies the growth rule to allocations for add-trade (capacity.rs:695-704). However: plan line 101 has identify take the families and line 107 updates Identity "for the recomputed families only", so the anchors scan is master's code the plan proposes to replace, not a pass the plan keeps; line 88 keys the ledger's collections with trades part of the same delta (entries put, keys removed), which turns seen.get(trade) into a keyed lookup of ledger.trades, and line 107 names settle_trades reading by key. The plan does not spell out a trade-by-opening index, but that is an implementation detail below the plan's level, and the plan's done-contract covers the outcome: criterion line 133 requires add-trade to meet the growth rule, which judges allocations ×4/×1 under 2.0 (GROWTH_LIMIT, capacity.rs:49), and ×4 scales accounts, instruments and trades together (capacity.rs:243-245), so a surviving O(trades) pass would grow 4× against constant per-family work and fail the build's own gate. The finding's failing scenario is therefore the plan's own acceptance criterion firing, not a wrong figure, a change missed or applied twice, or a wrong page state; the "a large constant hides it" branch is a hypothetical about later work. It is a cost finding outside the brief's behaviour-or-correctness scope. One claim is also overstated: a buy on an instrument held open joins the current round trip (ledger.rs:858-865), so an added trade does not always make needs_trade non-empty, though it does in the probe.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:82-91 (seen built from every engine trade, o.clone() per Opening), :92 and :111 (book.trades() whole before and after); rust/crates/engine/src/identity.rs:48-56 (anchors: o.transaction.clone() per trade), :89-91 (second pass, TripKey clone per trade), :95 (trips scanned per unclaimed candidate); rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:290-294 (rematch calls identify), :451 (identify again on Change::Trades); rust/crates/core/src/ids.rs:122-123 (Leg(String)), :175-179 (TransactionId holds a Leg, so clone allocates); rust/crates/server/src/entries.rs:24, :142, :252 (empty account = Manual account, made first time); rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:858-865 (a buy joins the holding's open round trip; a new opening only when none is open); rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:49 (GROWTH_LIMIT 2.0), :243-245 (sized ×4 multiplies accounts, instruments and trades), :584-589 (add-trade probe), :695-704 (growth rule judged on steps, allocations, bytes read for per-change ops); plan lines 31 (settle_trades by key), 88 (keyed delta including trades), 101 (identify takes families), 107 (Identity updated for recomputed families only), 133 (add-trade must meet the growth rule and leave OVER_BUDGET).

verdicts.why:
The code does what the finding says, but the failing scenario produces no wrong figure, no missed or doubled change and no wrong page state; it is a performance-completeness note about allocations the plan's own acceptance criterion already measures, and the brief limits findings to behaviour or correctness. Where the plan is silent (`seen`), its design makes the map a lookup; where it speaks (`identify`, plan 101/107), it already says the work is per family. The finding also overstates the trigger: an added trade does not "always" open a round trip.

What holds in the finding: `Leg` is a `String` (`core/src/ids.rs:123`, `:176-179`), so every `o.clone()` in `settle_trades` (`figures.rs:82-91`) and every `o.transaction.clone()` in `anchors` (`identity.rs:48-56`) allocates once per trade, and `engine.identity().clone()` (`figures.rs:78`) clones a `TripKey` per round trip too. `identity.rs:89-108` scans every trade; `:95` scans every trip per unclaimed trade. None of this is named in the Scope table row for `settle_trades` (plan line 31), which speaks only of `book.trades()`.

Why it is refuted:
1. No behaviour or figure is wrong in either branch of the scenario. Branch (a): the residual O(trades) allocations push the ×4/×1 ratio to ≥2.0 — then `judge` (`capacity.rs:695-704`, `GROWTH_LIMIT` 2.0 at `:49`) fails the job, the plan's criterion at line 133 ("`add-trade` and `import` meet the growth rule") is unmet, and the work is not done until the index is added. The plan's done-contract catches exactly this; the finding's "Required change" is what a builder would then do, not something the plan prevents. Branch (b): a large keyed-path constant K hides it — by arithmetic the rule passes only when K exceeds about twice the residual (ratio (K+4R)/(K+R) < 2 iff K > 2R), i.e. when the residual is a minority of the operation's own allocations; at ×4 that residual is on the order of 10–17k allocations, well under a millisecond against the 100 ms budget. Nothing the page shows differs.
2. `seen` under the plan: `settle_trades` only ever calls `seen.get(id)` for ids in `identity.moved/joined/unclaimed` (`figures.rs:94`, `:102`, `:107`). Plan line 88 makes `Change::Trades` part of a keyed delta ("for each keyed collection of the ledger, the entries put and the keys removed") applied by key, which makes `ledger.trades` (today a `Vec<Trade>`, `engine/src/input.rs:79`) keyed by trade id; `seen` then collapses to a lookup on the engine's own trades with no build. The finding's required change ("settle_trades reads only the trades its identity names") is what the plan's keyed design yields.
3. `anchors` under the plan: line 101 lists `identify` among the functions that "take the families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts) to build", and line 107 says "`Identity` is updated for the recomputed families only". The plan does not leave `identify` whole; it leaves the index by which a per-family `identify` finds its anchored trades unnamed, which is an implementation detail the growth-rule criterion governs.
4. "An added trade always opens a round trip (needs_trade non-empty)" is false in general: `ledger.rs:856-865` ("what is bought later joins the round trip already open") adds a later buy as another opening of the open trip, so a buy into a held position leaves `needs_trade`, `moved`, `joined` and `unclaimed` empty and `settle_trades` returns at `figures.rs:79-80` before `seen` is built. It does hold for the capacity probe (`capacity.rs:586`: `account: String::new()` → the Manual account, `entries.rs:24`, `:142-155`, a new holding and so a new trip), so the probe exercises the path twice per pass (`seen` on pass 1 and the no-write pass 2) — but only the probe-sized case, not the owner's ordinary add-to-holding.

Default-to-refuted applies: the magnitude claim ("ratio between 2 and 3") rests on a guessed constant ("if the keyed path's own cost is a few thousand allocations") that the finding does not measure, and the only consequence of its being right is that the plan's own test fails and the builder fixes it before the work is done.

findings.title: The names cache is dropped on every record change and reloaded with one query per instrument and per account: O(book) per change, and no probe measures it
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:458 (*self.names = None in pulled), :313-321 (names()); rust/crates/server/src/wire/build.rs:30-46 (Names::load: instrument_refs per instrument, account_refs per account); rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:584-590 (the add-trade measurement ends at enter's return), :570-583 (feed-step follows a price change, which keeps the cache); plan lines 26, 123
findings.claim: The plan keeps Figures::pulled's shape and says it reads the log instead of the whole record, but the cache reset at :458 stays: after any added trade, pull, import or removed row, the next page build runs instruments+accounts queries. On the owner's book that is ~210 instrument_refs reads and 29 account_refs reads per change; at ×4, four times that. The work is per change and proportional to the book, which is the rule the plan claims to establish, and it falls outside every probe's window (add-trade stops before a page reads; feed-step's change is a quote).
findings.failing_scenario: Owner's book, a pull every few minutes that stores one new row: each pull drops the cache; the next feed step or status read runs ~240 indexed queries (~5-10k VM steps) before it can serialise a view. At ×4 that is ~960 queries per change. `capacity run` reports add-trade and feed-step within the growth rule because neither window contains the reload.
findings.required_change: Maintain Names from the same delta: an `instrument`-kind log entry reloads that instrument's refs, an `account`-kind entry that account's, nothing else is touched; or at least have the feed-step probe follow a record change (enter a trade, then feed.step) so the gate sees the reload. State which in the plan's Scope table.

verdicts.why: The facts hold: Figures::pulled (figures.rs:458) drops the names cache unconditionally after every record change, and every pull calls pulled whether or not it stored a row (broker_reads.rs:409), so the next names() (figures.rs:313-321) runs Names::load (wire/build.rs:30-46), which is one instrument_refs per ledger instrument and one account_refs per account. instrument_refs is three statements (identity.rs:269 canonical, :304 instrument_refs with an EXISTS-ordered subquery, :308 instrument_routes), so on the owner's 191 instruments plus 29 accounts the reload is ~600 statements at x1 and ~2,400 at x4: proportional to the book, triggered by a change. The plan never mentions Names, instrument_refs or account_refs; line 123 keeps pulled's shape; lines 22-34 claim the Scope table lists every place the §13 rule applies 'all fixed here'; line 115 lets a pull that stored nothing link nothing, yet that same pull still drops the cache. No probe window contains the reload: add-trade ends at enter's return (capacity.rs:587-589; enter does not call names() outside tests), feed-step follows a price change which does not reset the cache (resets only at figures.rs:201 and :458), import never calls names(). The boundary test (plan line 131) guards ledger/transactions/trades whole readers, not per-instrument refs reads, so it cannot see this either. Severity is lowered to low rather than medium: no figure comes out different, no change is missed or applied twice, no page state is wrong; the reload is pre-existing on master and correct; the growth rule as architecture.md:240 defines it names 'an added trade's write' and 'an import's linking', not the read that follows, so the plan's acceptance criteria hold as written; and ~600 indexed point queries is single-digit milliseconds on a Pi against the 1 s stream budget. It is a gap in the plan's inventory of per-change O(book) work (and the largest such term the plan would leave, likely comparable to the keyed add-trade's own work once the 900k-step rebuild is gone), worth a Scope-table line or a probe that steps the feed after a record change, not a blocker.
verdicts.evidence: figures.rs:456-461: `drop(guard); // the broker's names for what the record holds are read again\n *self.names.write()... = None; self.wake(); Ok(self.moved(moved))` — unconditional, in pulled; record_changed (figures.rs:411-413) is pulled(now, &BTreeSet::new()). broker_reads.rs:409: `let applied = f.pulled(now, &report.stated_for);` on every pull. figures.rs:313-321 names(): loads `Names::load(&book, e.inputs())` when the cache is None. wire/build.rs:32-43: `for id in inputs.ledger.instruments.keys() { let refs = book.instrument_refs(*id)...}` and `for (id, info) in &inputs.ledger.accounts { let refs = book.account_refs(*id)...}`. identity.rs:296-318 instrument_refs: `let head = self.canonical(id)?;` (query_row on instrument_joins, :272) then a loop over two prepared statements (instrument_refs with `ORDER BY EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM security_standings ...)`, instrument_routes). identity.rs:167-168 account_refs: one SELECT per account. capacity.rs:584-590 AddTrade: `let m = mark(); crate::entries::enter(f, &req, ...)?; Ok(since(&m, 1))` — no names() in enter (grep: the only entries.rs names() call is in a #[test] at :334). capacity.rs:576-582 FeedStep: quote_moved + price_changed then feed.step; price_changed does not touch self.names (grep: only figures.rs:201 rebuild and :458 pulled set it to None). events.rs:483 `let names = match f.names()` in the feed step; events.rs:358 in status_for. Plan: grep for Names/instrument_refs/account_refs finds nothing; line 123 'Figures::pulled keeps its shape: it reads the log instead of the whole record'; line 22 'The places it applies, by reading the code, and all fixed here'; line 115 'A pull that stored nothing links nothing'; line 131 boundary test lists only ledger, transactions, trades. docs/architecture.md:240: growth rule operations are 'brokers, price_changed, Feed::step, an added trade's write, an import's linking'. findings.title: engine_inputs::facts is still read whole on every record change; declared rows grow with the book, and the boundary criterion does not name `facts`
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:423 (engine_inputs::facts(&book)?.adjustments); rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:73-90 (facts: rates(), rate_series(), bank_holidays(), rate_reads(), declared(), frequencies(), adjustments() all whole); rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:462-471 (the build stores a declared record for every dividend-paying listing, so declared rows scale with instruments); plan lines 26, 80, 131
findings.claim: The plan's Scope table keys the ledger and the adjustments but Figures::pulled on master reads the whole Facts to take `.adjustments`. Line 80 names only `facts().adjustments`' tables for triggers, and criterion 131 adds `ledger`, `transactions`, `trades` to the whole-readers list but not `facts`. A build that keys the ledger and leaves :423 passes every stated test while reading every Bank rate, every declared distribution and every frequency on each added trade; the declared part is 4× larger at ×4.
findings.failing_scenario: ×1 build: ~137 payers with ~12 declared rows each (quarterly over 36 months) ≈ 1,600 declared rows plus ~2,000 rate rows read per add-trade; ×4: ~6,500 declared rows. Steps for this part grow ~3× (rates fixed, declared ×4). The property test (criterion 128) and the boundary test (131) are green; `capacity run` shows add-trade's steps and bytes read growing with the book from a read the plan's table says is gone.
findings.required_change: Read adjustments by key from the log's `adjustment` kind (Book::adjustments_for(&[TransactionId])) and drop the facts() call from pulled; add `facts` to WHOLE_READS with only the start's build and the comparison tool allowed.

verdicts.why: The code reads as the finding says: on master `Figures::pulled` (figures.rs:423) calls `engine_inputs::facts(&book)?.adjustments`, and `facts` (engine_inputs.rs:73-90) reads rates, series, holidays, rate reads, every declared record, every frequency and every adjustment whole; the capacity build stores a declared record per dividend-paying listing (capacity.rs:461-471) and `sized()` scales instruments and trades ×4 with months fixed (capacity.rs:243-245), so that read would grow with the book. But the finding is refuted on the rubric's three grounds. (1) The plan already handles it: the log carries an `adjustment` kind keyed by the transaction it applies to (plan line 78), and the change handler "reads each named thing by its key through indexed readers" (line 82; line 26: `pulled` "reads what the book's change log names ... by key"); line 103 has `Change::Adjustments` reach "the families of the transactions the changed adjustments apply to", which requires a keyed read of the changed adjustments, and the anti-stub self-check (line 152, "no trigger whose kind nobody reads") forbids exactly the build the finding posits, where the `adjustment` kind's triggers exist but nobody reads their keys and `facts()` is read whole instead. A build that leaves :423 does not implement the plan's Approach A. (2) The failing scenario produces no wrong figure or behaviour: reading the adjustments whole and comparing with `!=` (figures.rs:447) yields the same engine input as a keyed read; nothing is missed, applied twice, or shown wrong. The task's own scope is behaviour and correctness, and this is a residual cost. (3) The finding's claim that such a build "passes every stated test" ignores criterion 133: `add-trade` must meet the growth rule (under 2× steps, allocations and bytes read ×1→×4, capacity.rs:688-707, `GROWTH_LIMIT` = 2.0) and come off `OVER_BUDGET`, after which `listed_disagree` fails the job on any growth. The finding's own estimate (the facts part grows ~3×, declared rows ×4) is the kind of proportional read the growth rule exists to catch; the only way it slips under 2× is if the keyed work dwarfs it, in which case it is a small residual inside the plan's budget, not a defect. The finding even concedes "`capacity run` shows add-trade's steps and bytes read growing with the book". What remains is a wording nit: criterion 131's whole-readers list (`ledger`, `transactions`, `trades`) could also name `facts`, and line 82's "…" could name the adjustment reader explicitly, so the mechanical boundary test rather than the capacity job pins the read in place. That is a completeness nit on a test list for a performance property, not a correctness finding; if kept at all, low.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:420-450 — `pulled` reads `engine_inputs::ledger(&book)?` and `engine_inputs::facts(&book)?.adjustments`, then applies `Change::Adjustments(adjustments)` only when `e.inputs().facts.adjustments != adjustments`; a whole read here is slower, not wrong. rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:73-90 — `facts` reads `book.rates()`, `rate_series()`, `bank_holidays()`, `rate_reads()`, `declared()`, `frequencies()`, `adjustments()` whole. rust/crates/book/src/facts.rs:335-368 and :539-580 — `declared()` runs a correlated-subquery scan over `declared_reads` plus `declared_rows(id)` per payer; `adjustments()` reads every live record's adjustments. rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:243-245 — `sized(times)` multiplies accounts, instruments and trades, keeps `months: 36`, so rate rows are fixed and declared rows scale; :461-471 — a declared row per dividend transaction, a frequency per payer; :688-707 — `judge` fails a per-change op whose steps, allocations or bytes read grow ≥ `GROWTH_LIMIT` (2.0); :711-719 — `listed_disagree` fails the job for an op off `OVER_BUDGET` that is over. rust/crates/server/src/tests_boundary.rs:192-252 — `WHOLE_READS` currently lists only `market`, `market_from_cache`, `brokers`; the plan's criterion 131 adds `ledger`, `transactions`, `trades`, not `facts` (the nit). rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:428-431 — `Change::Adjustments(a)` replaces `inputs.facts.adjustments` whole and rematches (the plan's line 28/103 keys this). No `Book::adjustments_for` exists on master (grep over rust/crates), so the finding's reader is new, as the plan's line 82 "…" allows. Plan lines: 26 (`pulled` reads what the log names, by key), 78 (`adjustment` kind keyed by the transaction it applies to, from `adjustments` and `adjustment_legs`), 80 (trigger test covers `facts().adjustments`' tables), 82 (each named thing read by key), 103 (`Change::Adjustments` reaches the families of the transactions the changed adjustments apply to), 131 (boundary test list omits `facts`), 133 (add-trade must meet the growth rule and leave `OVER_BUDGET`), 152 (anti-stub: no trigger whose kind nobody reads).

verdicts.why: The code reads as the finding says (figures.rs:423 takes `.adjustments` from a whole `engine_inputs::facts` read; engine_inputs.rs:73-90 reads rates, series, holidays, rate reads, declared, frequencies and adjustments whole; capacity.rs:461-471 stores a declared read and frequency per payer so those scale ×4), and criterion 131 indeed lists `ledger`, `transactions`, `trades` without `facts`. But the finding is not a behaviour or correctness defect and the plan already catches it: criterion 133 requires `add-trade` to meet the growth rule, which `judge()` (capacity.rs:688-707) applies to the whole operation on steps, allocations and bytes read with GROWTH_LIMIT 2.0 from ×1 to ×4, plus the 100 ms Pi budget, and to be removed from OVER_BUDGET. A build that leaves :423 and keys everything else has a fixed part (rates ~800 rows per non-CAD currency, the write, a handful of keyed reads) against a declared/frequency part scaling ×4; by the finding's own numbers (~1,600→6,500 declared rows) the whole-operation ratio lands near 3×, failing 133 — the finding itself concedes "capacity run shows add-trade's steps and bytes read growing with the book". If the ratio stayed under 2×, the plan's objective is met and nothing is wrong. Criterion 131's claim is "no change handler reads the record whole", and the plan uses "the record" for the ledger tables (lines 11-13, 68-78), not facts; the Scope table (line 26) and section A (lines 78-80, the `adjustment` log kind with triggers on the adjustment tables) state adjustments are read by key. No figure differs from a fresh build, no change is missed or doubled, and no wrong page state follows from the whole facts read (`Change::Adjustments` with whole adjustments is master's behaviour and equals the fresh build). At most a wording note for criterion 131.

findings.title: The boundary test cannot see the whole readers the plan must remove: its scanner matches free-function calls only, and book.trades()/book.transactions()/live_records/superseding are method calls
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/tests_boundary.rs:213 (regex requires a non-`.` character before the name), :258 (asserts a method call is not found), :201-208 (WHOLE_READS); the method calls: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:92, :111, :130 (book.trades()), rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:325, :329, :331 (live_records, superseding), rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:434, :450; plan line 131
findings.claim: Criterion 131 says the boundary test gains `ledger`, `transactions`, `trades` 'with only the start's build and the comparison tool allowed to call them'. `ledger` is a free function (engine_inputs::ledger) and would be found; `transactions` and `trades` are Book methods, which whole_reads excludes by design, so adding those names finds nothing and the criterion 'no change handler reads the record whole' is held by no test. The same holds for live_records and superseding in link.
findings.failing_scenario: A build keeps `book.trades()` in settle_trades (figures.rs:92, :111). The extended test's `found` list has no entry for figures.rs/trades because `.trades(` never matches the regex; WHOLE_READS lists none either; the assertion passes. The handler reads every trade on every added trade, which is the behaviour criterion 131 says is gone.
findings.required_change: Extend whole_reads to the method form (`\.(trades|transactions|live_records|superseding|instruments|accounts)\(` with the receiver named `book`), with the allowlist by file and name as now, and add the scanner's own unit test for a method call found; or hold the criterion by work counted instead (a test that `record_changed`'s steps on a one-row change do not grow between SMALL and SMALL×4, as test_every_operation_is_measured_and_the_growth_rule_judged does for the probes).

verdicts.why: The finding's mechanics are correct on master: whole_reads (rust/crates/server/src/tests_boundary.rs:213) requires a non-`.` character before the name, and :258 asserts a method call is not found by design. `ledger` is a free function (engine_inputs.rs:25, called `engine_inputs::ledger(` at figures.rs:61/:422, read_sources.rs:188, compare.rs:255) and would be found, but `trades` and `transactions` exist only as Book methods (book/src/trades.rs:280, book/src/records.rs:581) and are called only as `book.trades()` (figures.rs:92, :111, :130; engine_inputs.rs:57; compare.rs:278) and `book.transactions()` (engine_inputs.rs:53; capacity.rs:434; read_sources.rs:124; demo_facts.rs:67/:99/:152); `live_records` and `superseding` (records.rs:726/:734) are methods called at csv_import.rs:325/:329/:331. Adding the three names as plan line 131 describes finds nothing for `trades`/`transactions`, so a build that leaves `book.trades()` in settle_trades (which runs whenever identity has a round trip to settle, figures.rs:79-92, as an added opening fill does) passes criterion 131 unchanged. The plan says nothing about extending the scanner to the method form. Criterion 133's growth rule (GROWTH_LIMIT 2.0, capacity.rs:49, judged at SMALL vs SMALL×4 by test_every_operation_is_measured_and_the_growth_rule_judged, :949-960, once add-trade/import leave OVER_BUDGET) is only a loose secondary guard: a residual whole read of 40→160 trade rows, or a few hundred source_records ids in link, does not push an otherwise proportional operation past 2×, so it does not hold line 131's claim either. Severity corrected to low: no figure differs from a fresh build and the practical cost of the residual read is small; the defect is an acceptance criterion that can be satisfied trivially.

findings.title: link still reads every csv row, every person row and every superseding link whole; in the capacity book these are most of the record, so import can still fail the growth rule after the N×M compare is gone

findings.claim: Plan D replaces candidates' product with an index lookup per stored row, but the three exclusion sets link builds first are whole reads whose size is the book's: in the capacity build ~6,100 csv ids and ~6,100 superseding links at ×1, ~24,500 each at ×4. The plan does not say these go. Once the product is gone they are the import's largest remaining read and grow 4×. Criterion 132 counts rows `link` compares, not rows it reads, so it passes.
findings.failing_scenario: Import probe after the plan: 20 stores (~20k steps) + record_changed (keyed) + link: live_records(csv) 6,100 rows, live_records(person) ~0, superseding 6,100 rows, ~20k steps and ~12k allocations at ×1; at ×4 ~80k steps and ~50k allocations. steps ratio ≈ 2.5, allocations ≈ 3: import stays over the growth rule and #419 cannot be closed, while criterion 132's test is green.
findings.required_change: Make the index carry what the sets carry: an entry is kept only for broker rows (source not csv, not person) and is removed when the row is superseded (its source_records state change is already logged), so link needs no exclusion set; the import passes the ids it stored and the pull the ids it stored. Amend criterion 132 to count rows read by link, not only rows compared, against a book of any size.

verdicts.why: The finding's scenario rests on three whole reads staying in `link` after the plan, and its numbers are wrong on the code it cites. (1) `Book::supersede` sets the csv row (the `from` side) to `Superseded` (links.rs:94), so after the capacity build's linking `live_records(csv)` returns only the rows that did not link, and the build's own test holds that those are only the ASSET_MOVEMENT rows (capacity.rs:852–868); the finding's "live_records(csv) 6,100 rows" contradicts its own premise that nearly every csv row has a superseding link. `live_records(person)` is ~0 as the finding says. Only `superseding(csv)` (records.rs:734–743) is about one row per linked csv row. (2) The plan does say the `csv_rows` read goes: line 32 and lines 111–113 replace "every file row ever imported" with "the records the operation stored", looked up "in the index for broker rows of the same movement", so the index carries the source and the `not_broker` set has no role either. The one set the plan does not spell out is `taken`, and a keyed reader for it already exists on master, `Book::has_superseded(record)` (links.rs:139–146, through the `link_records_record` index at migrations/001-the-book.sql:186), so "a broker row taking one file row only" (plan line 115) can be kept per candidate with no whole read; the plan does not prescribe the whole read the finding assumes. (3) Even if a builder kept `superseding(csv)` whole, the plan's own criterion at line 133 (import meets the growth rule, then its budget, and is removed from OVER_BUDGET; #419 closed) is measured by the capacity job over the whole import operation (plan line 143; capacity.rs:591–599 measures `import_from`, which calls `link` at csv_import.rs:274), with GROWTH_LIMIT 2.0 (capacity.rs:49) judged at :696–700 and OVER_BUDGET at :128 refusing a listed operation that still fails. The finding says import "stays over the growth rule ... while criterion 132's test is green", but criterion 133 would be red and the PR could not close #419, so the plan already catches exactly this. (4) No figure differs from a fresh build, no change is missed or applied twice, no wrong page state: this is a performance concern, outside the finding brief. What is left is a wording gap: criterion 132 is titled "reads only what was stored" but its test counts rows compared, and approach D should name how `taken` is found by key. That is a note, not a defect.

AND state = 'live'`). rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:861–868: after `build(SMALL, 1)` the live csv rows are asserted to be only ASSET_MOVEMENT. links.rs:139–146 `has_superseded(record)`: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM link_records WHERE record_id = ? AND side = 'to'`, indexed by migrations/001-the-book.sql:186 `CREATE INDEX link_records_record ON link_records (record_id)`. Plan lines 32, 111–115: "each row the import stored, looked up by its movement in an index"; "looked up in the index for broker rows of the same movement". AND state = 'live' ORDER BY first_received_at, rowid`, and the only index on source_records is `source_records_key (COALESCE(connection_id,''), source, source_key)` whose leading column is an expression, so EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN gives `SCAN source_records` + `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY`: a full table scan however few rows come back. `superseding` (records.rs:734-743) plans as `SCAN t USING INDEX link_records_record` with two indexed searches per row: a scan of every link row in the book. The capacity book (capacity.rs:353-356, EXPORTED_SHARE :362) imports 6,156 of 7,994 feed rows as csv and links them, so link_records holds ~12k rows at ×1 and ~49k at ×4, and source_records ~14k → ~56k. findings.title: Criterion 130's test is specified through `work::statements_naming`, which does not exist on master
findings.where: rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs:1-42 (the only counter: VM steps per thread; no statement or table naming); no `statements_naming` or `brief 25` anywhere under rust/ or docs/; plan lines 80, 130
findings.claim: The plan's guard that every table the ledger reads has a trigger ('listed by the test, not by hand') rests on a counter it says was built for brief 25. Nothing of that name is in the repository, so the test as described cannot be written in this plan without building that counter, which the Scope does not include. Without it the trigger list is by hand (line 72-78), and a table the ledger reads through a join (for example the instrument_joins COALESCE in trades.rs:287 and whatever transactions() joins) can be left without a trigger with nothing to show it.
findings.failing_scenario: A writer merges one instrument into another (instrument_joins), which the plan lists, but a later change adds a join on a new table to Book::transactions() with no trigger; the hand list is stale; an added row on that table changes what the ledger reads and the engine never hears of it; the figures differ from a fresh build until the next start. The property test (128) drives only the writers it knows, so it does not see it either.
findings.required_change: Build the table-naming guard in this plan: rusqlite's Connection::authorizer reports SQLITE_READ with the table name for every statement prepared, so a test can open the book with an authorizer, run engine_inputs::ledger and facts().adjustments, collect the tables read, and assert each has an AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE trigger in sqlite_master; name it in Scope and in the anti-stub check.

verdicts.why: The facts hold. `work::statements_naming` and "brief 25" appear nowhere in the repository (grep over rust/, docs/ and the plan's own branch, which is a single plan-only commit b3c3bc87 adding docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md). The only facility in `rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs` (lines 1-42) is a per-thread VM-step counter via `progress_handler`; it names no statement or table. The plan's line 80 and criterion 130 (line 130) both say the trigger-coverage test reads the tables "through `work::statements_naming`, the counter built for brief 25" (past tense, as if existing), and neither Scope (lines 7-38) nor the anti-stub check (line 152) lists building it. So the test as specified cannot be written without unplanned work, and until it exists the trigger table list at lines 72-78 is a hand list. rusqlite 0.32.1 with the `hooks` feature the sqlite crate already enables (crates/sqlite/Cargo.toml:12) does expose `Connection::authorizer` (hooks/mod.rs:405), so the required change is buildable with no new dependency. Severity lowered to low rather than medium: I checked every table the whole readers in `engine_inputs::ledger` (engine_inputs.rs:25-61) and `facts().adjustments` touch on master, and the hand list at lines 72-78 covers all of them today (broker_connections, accounts, instruments, instrument_joins, instrument_sightings+source_records, option_terms, transactions+source_records+instrument_joins, record_problems, transfer_links, trades+instrument_joins, trade_groups, trade_group_members, journal, adjustments, adjustment_legs). No figure comes out wrong on the plan as written; the failing scenario is a future join on a new table left without a trigger, which is a guard gap in the plan's own "a trigger cannot be forgotten" argument (line 84), not a present defect. A builder would also hit a compile error on the nonexistent function immediately, so the risk is that the test is quietly replaced by a hand-maintained list, which is what the finding warns of.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs:1-42 on master d6824aa7: `start_counting`, `steps`, `watch` using `conn.progress_handler(1, ...)` incrementing a thread-local u64; nothing names tables or statements. `grep -rn "statements_naming|brief 25|brief-25"` over the cm checkout and the p506 branch: no matches. `git show --stat b3c3bc87`: one file, docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md, no code. Plan line 80: "The tables are listed by the test, not by hand: a test reads every table `engine_inputs::ledger` and `facts().adjustments` read (through `work::statements_naming`, the counter built for brief 25)"; line 130 repeats it as the acceptance criterion; lines 72-78 are the hand list; line 152's anti-stub check does not name the counter. Whole readers and their tables: identity.rs:42 (broker_connections), :129-134 (accounts), :238-239 (instruments, instrument_joins), :222 instrument() (instruments), :378-383 names() (instrument_sightings JOIN source_records, group_sql over instrument_joins at :875), :423-425 (option_terms), records.rs:581/608-617 transactions() (transactions JOIN source_records LEFT JOIN instrument_joins), :659-662 problems() (record_problems JOIN source_records), :677-678 live_record_facts() (source_records), statements.rs:549-550 (transfer_links), trades.rs:280/286-288 (trades LEFT JOIN instrument_joins), :371-372 (journal), :431-437 (trade_groups, trade_group_members), facts.rs:539-553 adjustments() (adjustments JOIN source_records, adjustment_legs). rusqlite: crates/sqlite/Cargo.toml:12 `rusqlite = { version = "0.32", features = ["bundled", "hooks"] }`; ~/.cargo/registry/src/.../rusqlite-0.32.1/src/hooks/mod.rs:405 `pub fn authorizer<'c, F>(&self, hook: Option<F>)`.

verdicts.why: The finding holds. `rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs` (lines 1-42 on master d6824aa7) is the whole `work` module: a `COUNTING` flag, a thread-local step `Cell`, `start_counting`, `steps` and `watch` (a progress handler counting VM instructions). Nothing in it names a statement or a table. A repository-wide grep for `statements_naming`, `statements naming`, `brief 25` and `brief-25` returns nothing under `rust/`, `docs/` or anywhere else; the briefs the repository cites stop at brief 22 (`docs/plans/stage-3-the-brokers-statements.md:99`), and `work::steps` is the only `work::` symbol any crate uses (`server/src/capacity.rs:216, 222, 498`). So the plan's line 80 ("listed by the test, not by hand ... through `work::statements_naming`, the counter built for brief 25") and criterion 130 rest on a facility that does not exist, and neither Scope nor the anti-stub check (line 152) names building it. The plan does not handle it elsewhere: the property test at 128 drives only the writers it lists, so it cannot notice a table the ledger reads through a join whose writer is not in that list. The gap is already real on master, not just hypothetical: `engine_inputs::ledger` (`server/src/engine_inputs.rs:35`) calls `Book::names`, which reads `listings_named` (`book/src/identity.rs:404` -> `book/src/watched.rs:117-126`) and `instruments_described` (`identity.rs:404-416`); neither appears in the plan's hand list at lines 72-78. `instruments_described` is upserted for an already-existing instrument by `Book::instrument_stated` (`identity.rs:473-490`), on a units pull that states a holding no record brought, without touching `instruments`, `instrument_sightings` or `option_terms`. Concrete failing scenario: a stated-only holding whose broker description changes symbol; the pull upserts `instruments_described` only; with the plan's hand list no `ledger_changes` row is written, the engine's `InstrumentInfo.names` keeps the old symbol until restart, while `Engine::build` from the book would show the new one. That is exactly the class of omission criterion 130's test claims to catch, and as specified it cannot be written. rusqlite 0.32.1 with the `hooks` feature (already enabled in `crates/sqlite/Cargo.toml:12` and `crates/book/Cargo.toml:16`) does expose `Connection::authorizer` reporting `SQLITE_READ` with the table name (`rusqlite-0.32.1/src/hooks/mod.rs:258, 405`), so the required change is buildable without a new dependency, but it must be named in Scope. Severity stays medium: the guard's absence yields a wrong name on the page for a stated-only holding and leaves every future table unguarded, but does not corrupt cost, quantity or cash figures on master's tables once the two missed tables are added.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/sqlite/src/work.rs:1-42 (only `start_counting`, `steps`, `watch` via `progress_handler`; no statement or table naming); grep for `statements_naming|brief 25|brief-25` across the checkout: no matches; `work::` uses: server/src/capacity.rs:216,222,498 (`steps`, `start_counting` only); plan lines 72-78 (hand list), 80 and 130 (`work::statements_naming`), 128 (property test over listed writers only), 152 (anti-stub check without the counter); server/src/engine_inputs.rs:34-37 (`book.names(i.id)`, `book.option_terms(i.id)`); book/src/identity.rs:378-419 (`names` reads `instrument_sightings JOIN source_records`, then `listing_named`, then `instruments_described`); book/src/watched.rs:117-126 (`listing_named` reads `listings_named`); book/src/identity.rs:473-490 (`instrument_stated` upserts `instruments_described` for an existing instrument); book/src/records.rs:616 and book/src/trades.rs:287-288 (`LEFT JOIN instrument_joins`, the joins the finding cites); rusqlite 0.32.1 src/hooks/mod.rs:258 (`SQLITE_READ` -> `AuthAction::Read { table_name, column_name }`) and :405 (`pub fn authorizer`), with `hooks` enabled in crates/sqlite/Cargo.toml:12 and crates/book/Cargo.toml:16.

findings.title: The add-trade probe measures the first trade into a Manual account created on the spot, not an add-trade into an account that holds the instrument
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/capacity.rs:586 (account: String::new()); rust/crates/server/src/entries.rs:202-215 (empty account → Prepared::Manual), :142-156 (manual_account: add_connection and add_account on a copy that has none); plan line 143
findings.claim: Every measured add-trade runs on a fresh copy of the built book, which has no Manual account, so each run creates a connection and an account inside the measurement window and the trade lands in an account holding nothing else. Under the plan that exercises the `account` kind and the new-account paths (equity, checks, Book figure) on every run and never the case the families exist for: a trade in an account that already holds the instrument, coupled to the other accounts' holdings of it through last_price/places. The plan says the probes are unchanged.
findings.failing_scenario: The family-match replacement for a holding that already has lots (the common add-trade) regresses to re-matching every account's holdings of every instrument the account holds; the probe's trade is the only row in its account, so the regression does not show in `capacity run`, and the owner, whose trades go into existing accounts, meets it.
findings.required_change: Probe the trade into the account of the position chosen (the entries tests do this: `held()` returns the account), keeping the Manual-account case as a one-off test rather than the measured operation; say so in Surfaces to check.

verdicts.why:
The code facts hold: capacity.rs:586 sends `account: String::new()`, entries.rs:202-215 turns that into `Prepared::Manual`, entries.rs:252 calls `manual_account` inside `enter`, i.e. after `mark()` at capacity.rs:587, and the built book has no Manual account (build at capacity.rs:248-358 pulls into a Wealthsimple connection and imports with `Some(first_account)`, so csv_import.rs:168's Manual path is never taken; no "manual" appears in capacity.rs). So each measured add-trade does create a connection and an account in the window and lands in an account holding nothing else.

The conclusion does not follow from the plan's own rule. Plan lines 90-97 define a family per instrument, joined across accounts by the first coupling ("every account's holdings of one instrument share its coin places and its last stated price"), extended to a whole account only by `account_taint`. The probe trades a held instrument (`held.first()`, capacity.rs:585), so under the plan the change reaches that instrument's family, which contains every other account's holdings of it with their existing lots, re-matched in the record's order with the new row. The probe therefore does exercise exactly the case the finding says it never does: a holding that already has lots, coupled through last_price/places across accounts. Which account the single new row sits in changes the family only when that account carries an account-wide taint, and that needs a `leg-unstated` problem (ledger.rs:1289-1311), which only the old app's rows carry (book/src/import/mapping.rs:355); the generated book has none (no multi-leg rows in wealthsimple/src/generated.rs). In the capacity book a trade into the held account would reach the same family as a trade into the Manual account, so the proposed change would measure nothing the current probe does not, and the per-account holding count does not grow with ×4 either, so the growth rule would not separate the two.

The failing scenario is a hypothetical implementation bug (a family widened to everything the account holds) that the plan does not propose, and it is a cost, not a figure: the figures would still equal a fresh build, which the plan's property test holds. The probe measuring the Manual-account path is, if anything, heavier (two extra writes and an `account` entry in the log), not a case that hides work. Not a wrong figure, a missed or doubled change, a wrong page state, or a test that cannot catch what it claims.
verdicts.evidence: capacity.rs:584-590 (`account: String::new()`, `mark()` before `enter`); entries.rs:202-215, :249-253 (`Prepared::Manual` → `manual_account` inside `enter`); entries.rs:142-156 (`add_connection`/`add_account` when absent); capacity.rs:252-258, :353-356 (build: Wealthsimple connection only; import with `Some(first_account)`); csv_import.rs:166-169 (Manual only when account is None); plan lines 90-97 (family per instrument across accounts; account-wide only via `account_taint`), line 143 (probes unchanged), line 128 (equality property test); ledger.rs:1289-1311 (`account_taint` only for a record with problem `leg-unstated` and `instrument: None`); book/src/import/mapping.rs:355 (`leg-unstated` comes from the earlier app's rows); wealthsimple/src/generated.rs has no multi-leg or leg rows.

verdicts.why: The factual premise holds on master: `capacity.rs:586` sends `account: String::new()`, `entries.rs:202-215` turns that into `Prepared::Manual`, and `manual_account` (`entries.rs:142-156`) adds a connection and an account inside the `mark()` window, since the capacity book is built by a Wealthsimple pull only (`capacity.rs:248-260`) and has no Manual account. But the conclusion does not follow from the plan. The plan's families are keyed by instrument, not by account: coupling 1 (plan line 91) is "every account's holdings of one instrument share its coin places and its last stated price", and the code bears that out — `Matcher.last_price` is `BTreeMap<InstrumentId, Dec>` (`ledger.rs:334`) written by `price_of` for any account's fill (`ledger.rs:1191`), and `places` is keyed by `(InstrumentId, SourceName)` (`ledger.rs:2164-2175`). So a buy of X in the fresh Manual account reaches X's family, which is every account's holdings of X including the existing account's lots, and the match re-run is the same set of transactions (plus one) as a buy of X into the account that already holds it. The probe therefore does exercise the cross-account coupling the finding says it never reaches, and the growth-rule comparison (×1 vs ×4 steps) measures the same family either way. The failing scenario depends on an implementation that scopes the rematch to the account's holdings, which is not what the plan proposes (account-wide reach exists only for `account_taint`, a multi-leg order naming no instrument, line 95); a hypothetical mis-implementation the plan does not describe is not a defect in the plan, and the plan's equality property test (line 128) would still hold the figures for either account. The extra work the probe does carry (a connection, an account, the Book figure) is a small constant that makes the probe measure more than the common case, not less. The existing-account path is already covered for correctness by `entries.rs` tests (`held()` returns the account, `a_trade_by_hand_is_of_the_instrument_the_book_holds_by_that_symbol_and_reaches_the_figures`).
