findings.title: A succession join changes every transaction's and trade's instrument without touching their rows; an `instrument` key does not reach them
findings.where: rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:608-617 (`COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)` on every transaction read); rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:288 (trade anchors read through `instrument_joins`); rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:640-729, esp. :707-713 (`settle_successions` rewrites `instrument_joins` whole, run inside every pull: broker/src/pull.rs:383, book/src/records.rs:123,147,463,495, links.rs:110); plan lines 70-82 (the `instrument_joins` trigger writes kind `instrument`), line 88 (transactions held by record, put by `record` key), line 128 (generator has no succession)
findings.claim: The plan's delta re-reads a thing only under the key its trigger writes. A join inserts rows in `instrument_joins` only; no `transactions` or `trades` row changes, so the log carries `instrument` keys for the two ids and no `record` or `trade` key. The engine re-reads the two InstrumentInfos and rematches their families with the transactions it still holds under the old id, while a fresh build reads every fill and anchor on the old id as the new instrument. The property test cannot see it: its generator (line 128) makes no retired-by-event standing, and the trigger-coverage test (line 130) passes because the table has a trigger.
findings.failing_scenario: Book holds 100 shares bought under Wealthsimple id O. A pull brings a `retired-by-event` standing for O with successor N (a symbol/CUSIP change) and a sale of 100 under N. `settle_successions` joins O→N (identity.rs:711-713). Fresh build (`Book::transactions`, records.rs:610): one holding N, buy and sale matched, trade closed, P&L realized. Incremental: log = {instrument O, instrument N, record of the sale}; the engine keeps the buy on O, puts the sale on N; match: O still long 100, N short 100 (sale beyond held → listed by the broker check, SPEC §4 pages-13), the trade anchored on (buy, O) → `identify` finds no trip for its anchor → `unclaimed` → `settle_trades` tries to orphan it. Differs from a full rebuild and shows a false disagreement in the header.
findings.required_change: Make the `instrument_joins` trigger (or the reader of an `instrument` key) name every live record with a transaction on the joined or parted instrument and every trade anchored on it, so the delta re-reads them (`Book::record_transactions`, `trades_by_id`); put both ids in one family after a join; and add a succession (a standing arriving after fills under the old id, and one parting them again) to the property test's generator.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it. On master the engine never sees joins: `engine_inputs::ledger` (server/src/engine_inputs.rs:53,57) fills `Ledger.transactions` from `book.transactions()` and `Ledger.trades` from `book.trades()`, both of which resolve the instrument at read time through `LEFT JOIN instrument_joins` (`COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)`, book/src/records.rs:610,616; `COALESCE(j.into_id, anchor_instrument)`, book/src/trades.rs:287-288). `settle_successions` (identity.rs:640-729) writes only `instrument_joins` (DELETE at :711, INSERT at :713); it touches no `transactions` or `trades` row on a join (the only record write, :720-726, is on a parting and only for option contracts on the underlying). Its `Successions` return value is discarded everywhere it is called (pull.rs:383, records.rs:123,147,463,495, links.rs:110, identity.rs:487,840, clear.rs:209) and nothing in server/src reads it, so today the engine only learns of a join because `Figures::pulled` re-reads and compares the whole ledger. The plan removes exactly that: its `instrument_joins` trigger writes kind `instrument` (line 73), the delta "reads each named thing by its key" (line 82), transactions are held and put by `record` key (line 88), and the rematch runs over "their transactions" as held (line 99). No `record` or `trade` key is written by a join, so the engine keeps every fill on the old id while a fresh build reads them on the new one. It is in fact worse than the finding states: `Book::instruments()` lists only instruments not in `instrument_joins` (identity.rs:238-239), so the `instrument O` key would remove O from the engine's instruments while the engine's transactions still name O. The failing scenario produces a wrong figure: fresh build has one holding on N with the buy and sale matched (closed trip, realized P&L); the incremental engine has O long 100 and N sold 100 beyond held, listed by the broker check. The finding's tail about the trade being orphaned is secondary and may not play out exactly that way under the plan's keyed `settle_trades` (C reads only the trips the change produced, so T1 would not be re-read), but the holdings and P&L divergence stands on its own. The plan's property-test generator (line 128) makes no `security_standings`/succession, so the equality criterion cannot catch it, and the trigger-coverage test (line 130) passes because the table has a trigger. Severity stays high: `settle_successions` runs inside every pull and every record store, successions are a real, tested feature (book/tests/successions.rs), and the wrong holdings and false disagreement persist until a restart.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:53 `transactions: book.transactions().map_err(err)?` and :57 `trades: book.trades().map_err(err)?` — the engine's ledger holds the resolved instrument, no join map. rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:608-617 `transactions_where`: `Read::AsBook => "COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)"` ... `LEFT JOIN instrument_joins j ON j.instrument_id = t.instrument_id`. rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:286-288 `SELECT id, anchor_record, anchor_leg, COALESCE(j.into_id, anchor_instrument) ... FROM trades LEFT JOIN instrument_joins j ON j.instrument_id = trades.anchor_instrument`. rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:707-716: `let held = self.joined()?; if wanted == held { return Ok(Successions::default()); } self.conn().execute("DELETE FROM instrument_joins", [])?; for (m, head) in &wanted { ... INSERT INTO instrument_joins ... }` — the only tables written on a join. identity.rs:720-726 writes `source_records.derived_version = 0` only `for (h, m) in &parted` and only for option contracts on the underlying. identity.rs:238-239 `instruments()`: `SELECT id FROM instruments WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT instrument_id FROM instrument_joins)`. Call sites discarding the result: broker/src/pull.rs:383 `book.settle_successions()?;`, book/src/records.rs:123,147,463,495, links.rs:110, identity.rs:487,840, clear.rs:209; grep of server/src for `Successions|settle_successions` finds no reader. Plan: line 73 (`instrument_joins` → kind `instrument`, key "the instrument's id"), line 82 ("reads each named thing by its key ... `Book::record_transactions(&[RecordId])`, `Book::instruments_by_id`, `Book::trades_by_id`"), line 88 (transactions "held by record (`BTreeMap<RecordId, Vec<Transaction>>`) ... a delta is applied by key"), line 99 ("`match_lots` takes the set of families to match and runs exactly as today over their transactions only"), line 128 (generator: accounts, shares/coins/contracts, transfers, corporate events with adjustments, multi-leg order — no standing/succession), line 131 (no change handler may call the whole `transactions`/`trades` readers). engine/src/identity.rs:65-110 `identify` keys trips and anchors by `(opening, instrument)`, so a buy held on O and a trade read as anchored on N cannot meet.

verdicts.why: The plan's delta re-reads only what a key names, and the only key a succession writes is `instrument`. The engine's held `Ledger` (engine/src/input.rs:68-82) carries transactions and trades whose instrument ids were canonicalized in SQL at read time and holds no join map, so re-reading two `InstrumentInfo`s cannot move the held fills and anchors from the old id to the new one. A fresh build reads every one of them as the successor; the incremental engine keeps them on the retired id. The plan does not handle it: line 73 maps `instrument_joins` to kind `instrument` with "the instrument's id"; line 82 reads an instrument key through `Book::instruments_by_id`; line 88 puts transactions by `record` key only; none of the five couplings at lines 91-95 is a succession; and the property test's generator at line 128 lists no standing or succession, while the existing `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` runs on a pulled fixture with no `retired-by-event` standing (no server or broker test mentions one), so neither test can show the divergence. One detail of the finding's scenario is overstated: in the stale engine the buy stays on O, so the trip keyed (buy, O) still exists and `identify` (engine/src/identity.rs:65-95) still finds the trade's anchor; it does not go unclaimed. But the figures still differ from a fresh build: O long 100 under an instrument the delta has removed from `instruments` (since `Book::instruments()` at identity.rs:239 excludes joined ids), N short 100 or listed beyond held, no realized P&L, versus one closed round trip on N. That is a wrong position and a false broker disagreement shown until restart, triggered by any symbol or CUSIP change the broker reports, so high stands.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:608-617: `transactions_where` selects `COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)` via `LEFT JOIN instrument_joins j ON j.instrument_id = t.instrument_id`; `Book::transactions()` (:581-583) uses `Read::AsBook`, and `engine_inputs::ledger` (rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:51) calls `book.transactions()`. rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:285-288: `trades_where` likewise reads `COALESCE(j.into_id, anchor_instrument)`; `engine_inputs::ledger` (:55) calls `book.trades()`. rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:239: `instruments()` is `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT instrument_id FROM instrument_joins)`, so a joined id drops out of the engine's `instruments` map. rust/crates/book/src/identity.rs:640-729: `settle_successions` reads `security_standings` (:644-668), computes `wanted`, and at :707-713 does `DELETE FROM instrument_joins` then inserts the new rows; it writes no `transactions`, `trades` or `source_records` row for the join (only :720-725 resets `derived_version` on contracts for a *parted* underlying). It runs inside `Book::store` (records.rs:123), `store_superseding` (:147), :463, :495, links.rs:110, clear.rs:209, identity.rs:487 and :840, and in every pull after standings are stored (rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:383). rust/crates/engine/src/input.rs:68-82: `Ledger` holds `instruments`, `transactions: Vec<Transaction>`, `trades: Vec<Trade>` and no join map; grep of `crates/engine/src` for `joins|joined|canonical|succession` finds only trip/roll joins, nothing about instrument successions. rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:420-446: `pulled` today compares the whole ledger, which is what catches this on master. Plan lines 70-82 (trigger table, `instrument` key read "through indexed readers ... `Book::instruments_by_id`"), 88 (transactions held by record), 90-97 (the five couplings, none a succession), 128 (generator contents: no standing), 130 (trigger-coverage test passes since `instrument_joins` has a trigger). grep for `retired-by-event` across `rust/crates/server/src`, `rust/crates/broker/src` and `tests/fixtures` hits only `clear.rs`, so the existing fresh-build test's fixture has no succession.

findings.title: The legs of one record are a coupling the five do not cover; an event without an adjustment moves two instruments as one order
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2193-2241 (a record whose legs share a day is applied as one order at the first leg's position in `txs`), :680-687 and :636-642 (bucket 0 for an untimed leg bringing units in, 2 for one taking them out), :1728-1754 (`apply_event` with no anchor applies each leg on its own instrument); rust/crates/wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:685-716 (a corporate action record carries a leg on the old security and a leg per security received) and :717-729 (an adjustment is drafted only for the `continues` kinds); plan lines 90-97 (the five couplings), line 128 (generator: events "with their adjustments" only), line 148
findings.claim: A family-only match applies a record's leg at its own sorted position; the whole match applies every leg of the record at the position of the leg that sorts first. When an adjustment exists the legs' instruments are one family (coupling 3). A spin-off or merger has no adjustment until the person enters one (SPEC §2, What you enter), so its parent and child are two families, and the parent's leg lands at a different point in the parent's order than today. The right to refuse says the property test would show it, but its generator never makes an event without an adjustment or any other record with legs on two uncoupled instruments.
findings.failing_scenario: TFSA holds 100 P. On the event day the person sold 40 P at 10:00 (timed row). A spin-off record with no `occurred_at` states −100 P given and +50 C received (two legs, no adjustment). Whole match: the received leg sorts in bucket 0 (before the day's timed rows), so the record is applied there: −100 P takes all 100 lots with no P&L (`moved_out`), the 10:00 sale then finds nothing and is `beyond` 40 — header: "A sale of P in the TFSA on <day> took 40 more than the book held.", the trade's P&L for the sale 0. Family-only match of P: the given leg sits in bucket 2, the sale applies first and realizes P&L on 40, the event takes 60 and 40 is beyond. Different P&L, different broker-check sentence.
findings.required_change: Add a sixth coupling: every instrument the legs of one record name are one family (by record, before and after the change), and make the property test generate events without adjustments and records with legs on different instruments, so the equality test can fail on it.

verdicts.why: The failing scenario needs a record with legs on two uncoupled instruments and no `occurred_at`, so that the received leg sorts in bucket 0 and drags the given leg ahead of the day's timed rows. No writer on master produces such a record. Wealthsimple drafts every leg of a corporate action from `base.draft`, which sets `occurred_at: Some(row.occurred_at)` (mapping.rs:355-360), and the given and received legs are clones of that one `event` draft (mapping.rs:685-706); `read_row` requires `occurredAt` (mapping.rs:238-239). The CSV/statement import makes exactly one single-leg record per row (`row_leg`, book/src/import/mod.rs:32-34; STKDIS BUY/SELL are two separate rows, book/src/import/mapping.rs:148, 369-386), so a file row's `None` instant (mapping.rs:229-230) never sits in a multi-leg record. Manual entries (`EntryRequest`: Trade, CostOfArrival, SpinOff, ReturnOfCapital, entries.rs:23-35) write adjustments or a single trade, not multi-leg records. The only `occurred_at = None` the Wealthsimple mapping sets is on a single cash leg (mapping.rs:926-933). With a shared instant, the two legs tie on (trade_date, bucket 1, occurred_at, record_rank, source_key) in `order_key` (ledger.rs:660-676) and are adjacent in `txs` (source_key unique per source, migrations/001:115), so applying the record "at the first leg's position" (ledger.rs:2225-2241) puts each leg exactly where its own sorted position is relative to every other record; `meets_opposite` is false for a CorporateEvent (read_move gives Move::Event, ledger.rs:1525-1528), so there is no intra-record reordering; `apply_event` with no anchor acts on each leg's own instrument only (ledger.rs:1731-1753); `record_units` is per day and idempotent (ledger.rs:1246-1262). A family-only match of P therefore yields the same lots, P&L, `beyond` entries and broker-check sentence as the whole match for every record a writer can store. The plan's coupling 3 indeed does not join an un-adjusted event's instruments, but that gap produces no different figure. Residual, outside this finding: `record_rank` (ledger.rs:690-700) is computed from all of a record's legs, so a family-only match must compute order keys from the whole record, not the family's subset, to keep ties at one instant identical; the plan's "in the same order" should be read that way, but no writer today produces a multi-instrument record whose rank could tie with another record at an untimed instant.
verdicts.evidence: mapping.rs:355-360 `fn draft(&self, leg: Leg, kind: Kind) -> Draft { Draft { leg, account: self.account.clone(), occurred_at: Some(self.occurred_at), trade_date: self.day, ...` — every Wealthsimple leg carries the row's instant. mapping.rs:685-706: `let event = base.draft(row_leg(), Kind::CorporateEvent);` then `let mut d = event.clone(); d.instrument = Some(instrument(root, old, base.day)?); d.quantity = Some(given.abs().neg());` and for each received `let mut d = event.clone(); d.leg = nth_leg("receive", i); ...` — given and received legs share one `occurred_at`. mapping.rs:238-239 `let at_text = n.text("occurredAt")?;` — required. book/src/import/mod.rs:32-34 `/// The one leg an imported row becomes: each old row was one transaction. pub fn row_leg() -> Leg { Leg::named("row") }`; book/src/import/mapping.rs:386 `Ok(Mapped { legs: vec![leg], problems, ..Mapped::default() })` — one leg per imported row. book/src/import/mapping.rs:148 `("STKDIS", "BUY" | "SELL") => r(Kind::CorporateEvent, ...)` — each side its own row/record. entries.rs:23-35 EntryRequest variants Trade/CostOfArrival/SpinOff/ReturnOfCapital. ledger.rs:660-676 order_key = (trade_date, bucket, occurred_at, record_rank, source_key, leg_rank, content) — same-record timed legs tie through source_key and are adjacent. ledger.rs:1525-1528 `fn meets_opposite ... if !matches!(read_move(t), Move::Trade(None | Some(Effect::Close))) || q.is_zero() { return false; }` with ledger.rs:629 `Kind::CorporateEvent => Move::Event` — no intra-record reordering for event legs. ledger.rs:2225-2241 one-day record applied at first leg's position, legs in sorted order when none meets an opposite. ledger.rs:1731-1753 `apply_event` without anchor: `let Some(instrument) = t.instrument else { return }; ... self.open_lot(account, instrument, ...)` / `self.take(account, instrument, q.abs())` — per leg, own instrument. ledger.rs:1246-1262 `record_units` writes only when the net changed. mapping.rs:717-734: adjustment drafted only for `continues` kinds — confirms a spin-off has no adjustment, but that alone changes no figure. Plan lines 90-97 (five couplings), 128 (generator), 148 (right to refuse).

verdicts.why: The failing scenario cannot be produced by any writer on master. It needs a corporate-event record with legs on two instruments and no `occurred_at`, so that the received leg sorts in bucket 0 and the given leg in bucket 2 around a timed sale. The only writer that drafts a multi-leg event record is the Wealthsimple mapping (`corporate_action`, mapping.rs:685-716), and every leg it drafts comes from `Base::draft`, which stamps `occurred_at: Some(self.occurred_at)` from the row's `occurredAt` (mapping.rs:348-359; the lone `occurred_at = None` at :929 is a single cash leg with no instrument). The CSV import, the only source of untimed rows (`Origin::File` → `(None, stated_day())`, import/mapping.rs:229-230), maps `STKDIS` to one single-leg record per row (`Mapped { legs: vec![leg] }`, :280 and :386), so its event legs on different instruments are different records and never share `by_record`. `statements.rs` creates no transaction legs, and `entries::enter` writes a person's trade, not an event. With both legs timed, both sit in bucket 1 at the same instant (`instant`, ledger.rs:680-687), so a P-only match places the P leg at the same (day, bucket, timestamp) slot as the whole match; the only residual difference is `record_rank` (1 with the acquiring C leg present, 2 without; ledger.rs:690-700) and it can reorder the leg only against another transaction of the same account at the identical timestamp, which no real broker data gives and which is not the scenario claimed. The P leg's application itself is independent of the C leg (`apply_event` with no anchor touches only its own instrument, ledger.rs:1731-1753), so no P&L, `moved_out` or `beyond` figure differs. The finding's claim that the property test can never reach an event without an adjustment is also wrong as stated: plan line 128 lists "set and clear an adjustment" among the generated writes, and the equality is held after every step, so a cleared adjustment followed by a write on one side is within the generator's reach (not targeted, but reachable), and line 148 commits to adding any coupling the test exposes. What survives is a low-severity note: a record's legs are a real coupling the five do not name, and listing it (or generating the clear-then-write sequence deliberately) costs nothing; it does not change a figure on master's data.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:348-359 — `struct Base { occurred_at: jiff::Timestamp, .. }`, `fn draft(..) -> Draft { .., occurred_at: Some(self.occurred_at), ..}`; :685-716 every event leg is `event.clone()` of `base.draft(row_leg(), Kind::CorporateEvent)`, so both the given and the received legs are timed; :929 the only `d.occurred_at = None` is a cash move with no instrument. rust/crates/book/src/import/mapping.rs:229-240 — `Origin::File => (None, stated_day()?)` is the only untimed path; :148 `("STKDIS", "BUY" | "SELL") => r(Kind::CorporateEvent, ..)`; :280 and :386 `Ok(Mapped { legs: vec![leg], .. })` one leg per row. rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:680-687 bucket 1 for any timed leg; :690-700 `record_rank` differs by the legs seen; :2225-2241 a one-day multi-leg record is applied at its first leg's position; :1728-1753 `apply_event` without an anchor moves only `t.instrument`. Plan line 128: "set and clear an adjustment" among the writes, "holds `Engine::differences` against `Engine::build` ... after every step"; line 148: a coupling the test shows "is added to the families".

findings.title: Reads before the lock with a consumed log make a stale apply permanent; the record and its trades are not read as one snapshot
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:420-427 (the ledger read before the engine lock at :428), :431-436 (the one-state rule), :92-118 (`settle_trades` writes trades under the lock), engine_inputs.rs:53 and :57 (transactions and trades read in separate statements); broker_reads.rs:427-429 (`fills_give_way` then `record_changed`) and orders/readback.rs:177 (`record_changed` on the read-back thread); app.rs:323-326 (`store_signal` only signals the bus; nothing re-applies); plan line 82 (read the log, "and then" read each key), line 123 (`pulled` "keeps its shape"), line 107
findings.claim: Today a stale read is overwritten at the next write, because every write re-reads the whole record. With a watermark, a reader that read its keys at an older state but takes the lock later overwrites a newer apply, and no later change names those keys again, so the engine stays wrong until a restart. Separately, reading the log and then each key in separate statements can hand the engine a record at one state and the trades on it at a newer one, which is what the :431-436 rule forbids, and `settle_trades` then writes on it. The plan does not say the log and the keys are read in one read transaction, nor under the lock, nor how the watermark moves (including for the trades `settle_trades` itself writes while holding the lock).
findings.failing_scenario: Order read-back stores fill F (seq 8) and calls `record_changed`: it reads the log >7 → {8}, reads F live. Meanwhile the pull's `fills_give_way` supersedes F with the broker's row B (seq 9) and its `record_changed` reads >7 → {8, 9}, reads F as gone and B live, takes the lock first, applies, watermark 9. Read-back then takes the lock and applies its read: F live again beside B. The fill is on the book twice; position qty and cash off by one fill; no later write names F. Second: a reader reads record R's transactions, a pull supersedes R by R2 and moves trade T to R2 in one write, the reader then reads T (now anchored on R2) — the engine holds T on a record it does not hold, `identify` lists T `unclaimed`, `orphan_unclaimed(T, seen)` passes the book's check because `seen` is already R2, and T is orphaned with its note cut loose (the case of figures.rs:675-710) for good.
findings.required_change: Read the log and every keyed thing in one read transaction and apply only under the engine lock, with the watermark monotonic and the read's snapshot seq compared against it (a read older than the watermark is re-read, never applied); state what happens to the entries the engine's own writes under the lock append (settle_trades, fills_give_way), so they are neither re-applied as a change nor skipped past a concurrent writer's seq. Add a test with two writers racing on one record.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it. On master, `Figures::pulled` opens a fresh connection (`Figures::book`, figures.rs:208-209) and reads the ledger before taking the engine write lock (figures.rs:421-427, lock at :428); `engine_inputs::ledger` reads `book.transactions()` (:53) and `book.trades()` (:57) as separate autocommit statements on a WAL connection (`transactions_where`/`trades_where` each `prepare_cached` on `Book::conn()`, no transaction wrapper), so the "one state" the comment at :431-436 relies on is already one snapshot per statement, not one per read. Two callers of `record_changed` run on different threads: the orders read-back (`gate::record` -> `readback::followed` -> `f.record_changed`, readback.rs:177, on `bagholder-orders-loop`, main.rs:244) and the pull (`broker_reads.rs:409` `f.pulled`, then `fills_give_way` at :427 superseding the read-back's fill records with the broker's row, then `record_changed` at :429, on `bagholder-broker`, main.rs:239). Today a stale apply is healed by any later write because every write re-reads and compares the whole ledger (:444). The plan keeps that shape explicitly (line 123: "`Figures::pulled` keeps its shape: it reads the log instead of the whole record"), reads the log "and then" each key (line 82), and defines the watermark only as "the highest seq it has applied" (line 82), i.e. monotonic; it says nothing about a read transaction, reading under the lock, comparing a read's snapshot against the watermark, or what the engine's own `settle_trades` writes under the lock (figures.rs:92-118, called at :450 inside the guard) do to the watermark. Under those words, the finding's first scenario (read-back reads {F} live, pull supersedes F with B and applies first, read-back applies its stale put of F, watermark stays at the higher seq, no later change names F) leaves F and B both live in the engine - position quantity and cash off by one fill - with nothing to re-read F until a restart, whereas on master the next write would overwrite it. The property test in acceptance criterion 2 (line 128) applies writes sequentially and reads the log after each, so it cannot exercise two writers racing one key. The second scenario (a torn read between a record and the trades on it, then `orphan_unclaimed` passing `anchored_as` because `seen` is already the new anchor, trades.rs:131-139, with `identify` listing the trade `unclaimed`, identity.rs:89-107) is real but pre-exists on master in the same :53/:57 gap; the plan carries it over rather than introducing it. I lower the severity to medium: both races need a narrow window (the read-back stalled on a contended engine lock between its keyed read and the lock, or a commit landing between two keyed reads), but the consequence is a figure that stays different from a fresh build until restart, which the plan's own acceptance criterion promises against and its test cannot catch.
verdicts.evidence: figures.rs:208-209 `Book::open_in(&self.home, ...)` per `book()` call; figures.rs:420-428 reads `engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` and `facts` before `self.engine.write()`; figures.rs:431-446 the one-state comment and the Trades/Ledger applies; figures.rs:450 `settle_trades(&book, e, now)` under the guard, which writes `move_trade`/`open_trade`/`orphan_joined`/`orphan_unclaimed` (:93-110) and re-reads `book.trades()` (:92, :111). engine_inputs.rs:53 `transactions: book.transactions()` and :57 `trades: book.trades()` - records.rs:581-583 and trades.rs:280-294 each a single `prepare_cached` statement on `self.conn()` (lib.rs:107-109, a plain `Connection`); sqlite/src/lib.rs:118-128 `atomically` is the only transaction wrapper and is used for writes. broker_reads.rs:409 `f.pulled`, :427 `book.fills_give_way(now)` (fills.rs:198-216 supersedes the fill-source live records of an order with the broker's row), :429 `f.record_changed(now)`, on the `bagholder-broker` thread (main.rs:239). readback.rs:173-183 `followed` calls `f.record_changed` and sets `pull_asked`, reached from gate.rs:183-193 `record` on the `bagholder-orders-loop` thread (main.rs:244). trades.rs:131-139 `orphan_unclaimed` orphans whenever `anchored_as(trade, seen)` holds; identity.rs:89-107 a trade whose opening key is in no matched trip and not among `openings` is pushed to `unclaimed`. app.rs:323-326 `hear_book(self.store_signal)` only signals the bus. Plan line 82 ("keeps the highest `seq` it has applied", "reads `SELECT kind, key FROM ledger_changes WHERE seq > ?` ... and then reads each named thing by its key"), line 123 ("`Figures::pulled` keeps its shape"), line 128 (sequential property test, "applies random sequences of writes ... reads the change log after each"); no mention of a read transaction, the lock, snapshot-vs-watermark comparison, or the engine's own writes' seqs anywhere in lines 66-135.

verdicts.why:
The first scenario holds against the code and the plan's own words; the second is a pre-existing weakness the plan carries forward rather than introduces, which weakens that half but does not refute the finding.

Scenario 1 (stale apply made permanent) is reachable and the plan does not handle it. On master, `Figures::pulled` reads the record (figures.rs:421-427) before taking the engine write lock (:428); `record_changed` is `pulled` with no accounts (:411-413). The plan keeps exactly that shape (plan line 123: "`Figures::pulled` keeps its shape: it reads the log instead of the whole record"; line 82: reads `seq > ?` "and then reads each named thing by its key") and keeps "the highest `seq` it has applied" (line 82), i.e. a monotonic watermark. Nothing in the plan puts the log read, the keyed reads and the apply under one lock or one read transaction, and the acceptance tests (lines 128-130) apply writes sequentially, so they cannot see the race. The two writers are on different threads with their own connections: the orders loop (`main.rs:244` → `readback.rs:432` → `gate::read_back` → `record` → `readback::followed` → `f.record_changed`, readback.rs:176-177) and the broker thread (`main.rs:239` → `broker_reads::pull_now`, which calls `book.fills_give_way` then `f.record_changed`, broker_reads.rs:427-429); `Figures::book()` opens a fresh connection per call (figures.rs:208-209). `fills_give_way` (book/src/fills.rs:198-216) supersedes the fill record F by the broker's row B in one `atomically` write (links.rs:33-112, `set_state(Superseded)` at :94), so under the plan's triggers it logs F and B after F's own `book_fill` entry. With a third thread holding the write lock (the figures thread's market/clock applies, figures.rs:324-340, :362), both readers queue on it after reading; std RwLock gives no order. If the pull's apply lands first (F gone, B live, watermark past both), the orders thread's apply then puts F back live: the engine holds F and B, and no later write names F (`fills_give_way` iterates live records only, fills.rs:200, and F is no longer live). On master the same interleaving is healed by the next `pulled`/`record_changed`, which re-reads the whole ledger and compares (:422, :444); under the plan nothing re-reads F until a restart. The plan's own claim "the engine's figures after any change stay exactly those of a fresh build" (line 36) is false under this interleaving.

Scenario 2 (record and trades from different states) is real but pre-existing: `engine_inputs::ledger` already reads `transactions` (:53) and `trades` (:57) in separate autocommit statements on one connection, so a supersede-and-move between them can already hand the engine T anchored on R2 with R live, and `settle_trades` (:106-110) then calls `orphan_unclaimed(T, seen=R2)` whose `anchored_as` check (trades.rs:131-139) passes against the book's R2. The plan preserves this; it does not create it. The "watermark and settle_trades' own entries" point is a genuine gap in the plan's text (line 107 says only that trades are read by key) but is speculative as to outcome.

Severity: kept at high rather than lowered, because the outcome is a doubled fill in position quantity and cash on the path where the person is acting (their own order's fill), with no indicator, lasting until restart, and the plan's tests cannot catch it. The window is a lock race, so it is not frequent; a reviewer could argue medium on probability alone, but the plan's correctness contract (line 36, criterion line 128) is what it breaks.
verdicts.evidence:
Checked and found as the finding says:
- figures.rs:420-429: `pulled` reads `engine_inputs::ledger(&book)` and `facts` before `self.engine.write()`; :411-413 `record_changed` delegates to it; :444 the whole-ledger compare that heals a stale apply today.
- figures.rs:74-120 `settle_trades`: reads `book.trades()` (:92, :111) and writes `move_trade`/`open_trade`/`orphan_*` under the caller's lock (:450 inside the guard).
- figures.rs:208-216 `book()`: `Book::open_in` per call, a connection per thread, no shared snapshot.
- engine_inputs.rs:53 and :57: `book.transactions()` and `book.trades()` are separate statements, no enclosing read transaction.
- broker_reads.rs:385-431: `pull_now` runs `f.pulled` (:409), then `csv_import::link` (:422), then `book.fills_give_way(now)` (:427) and `f.record_changed(now)` (:429), on the "bagholder-broker" thread (main.rs:239).
- orders/readback.rs:173-183 `followed` calls `f.record_changed(Timestamp::now())` after a fill; reached from `gate::record` (gate.rs:183-193) ← `read_back` (gate.rs:161-179) ← readback.rs:432 on the "bagholder-orders-loop" thread (main.rs:244). `book_fill` is written in `order_event` (book/src/orders.rs:167).
- book/src/fills.rs:198-216 `fills_give_way`: for each live own-fill record with a live broker row, `supersede(&fills, &[row], ...)`; links.rs:33-112 does it in one IMMEDIATE transaction (lib.rs:122-128), setting the from-records Superseded (:94) and inserting `links`/`link_records` (:97-108).
- records.rs:677-678 `live_record_facts` selects `WHERE state = 'live'`, so a keyed read of F after supersede returns it gone.
- trades.rs:131-139 `orphan_unclaimed` checks `anchored_as(trade, seen)` against the book's current anchor, so a `seen` already equal to the newer anchor passes.
- figures.rs:668-710: the test guarding the journal-cut-loose case is sequential (`store_superseding` then `record_changed` on one thread).
- app.rs:323-326 `set_figures`: `hear_book(store_signal)` only signals the bus; no re-apply.
- Plan: line 36 (figures equal a fresh build after any change), line 82 (highest seq applied; read log, "and then" each key), line 107 (settle_trades by key, nothing on its own log entries), line 123 (`pulled` keeps its shape), lines 128-130 (sequential property and writer tests, no concurrent writers).
Sound: the plan's trigger-based log does capture every writer in the same transaction (lib.rs:122-128 `atomically`, so a rollback leaves no entry); the keyed-read design itself is not the problem — only the absence of a snapshot/lock-ordering rule and of a stated watermark rule for the engine's own writes under the lock.

findings.title: A group's figure spans families; recomputing one family's trips without rebuilding the group leaves the group's P&L stale
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:296-341, esp. :308-326 (a group collapses the trips of its members) and :329 (a trip in a group is not listed on its own); plan line 101 (derive "the families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts)"; groups not named)
findings.claim: `build_trades` keyed by trip rebuilds `TradeKey::Trip` entries of the recomputed families; a `TradeKey::Group` entry collapses trips from several families and must be rebuilt whenever any member's trip was recomputed (and a recomputed trip whose trade is a group member must leave the trip list, not join it). The plan does not say which group figures a family's change reaches.
findings.failing_scenario: Saved group G = {trade on AAPL in the TFSA, trade on MSFT in the TFSA}. The person adds a sale of AAPL. AAPL's family is rematched; the AAPL trip's figure is rebuilt but, under the plan's wording, G's figure is not: the Trades page row for G keeps its old P&L and Close, while a fresh build shows the realized sale in G. If the rebuilt AAPL trip is also emitted as a `TradeKey::Trip`, the trade appears twice (in G and alone).
findings.required_change: When trips are recomputed, rebuild every group any of their trades belongs to from the recomputed trips and the held trips of its other members, and exclude member trips from the trip list as :329 does; include a group spanning two instruments in the property test.

verdicts.why: The plan does not handle the coupling the finding names, and its tests cannot catch it. (1) Groups span families: `Book::add_group(&self, members: &[TradeId], ...)` (rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408-428) takes any trade ids with no instrument or account constraint, and SPEC.md:51 (trade-15) says "a saved group joins them, as it does any trades". The plan's families (line 90-97) join instruments only through the match's five couplings; two instruments with no contract/event/transfer link are separate families, so a group over AAPL and MSFT trades straddles two. (2) On master a group's figure is derived from the slices of every member trip and the member trips are excluded from the trip list: trades.rs:308-326 collects `trips` across members via `identity.trade_of`, collapses their slices into `TradeKey::Group(g.id)`, and marks them `used`; trades.rs:327-331 skips any `used` trip. So a group figure (realized, pnl, closed_on, status) depends on trips from every family it spans. (3) The plan's derivation (line 101) says `build_trades` takes "the families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts) to build" and "only the recomputed entries are compared"; nothing names a group reached by a recomputed member trip, and "What a change can reach" (line 90-95) lists only match couplings, with the right-to-refuse (line 148) scoped to the match. Line 88's keyed `Groups` delta covers a change *to* a group, not a record change reaching a group through a member. Built as written, a sale added to AAPL rematches AAPL's family and rebuilds `TradeKey::Trip(aapl)` but leaves `TradeKey::Group(G)` held stale, and emits the AAPL trip alongside G, where a fresh build would fold it into G (trades.rs:329). (4) The tests cannot catch it: the property test (line 128) generates "open, move and orphan a trade; a journal entry" but no group; the existing `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` (figures.rs:612-666) runs on `pulled_book`, which creates no groups (no "group" in tests_common.rs), and never writes one. Severity stays medium: the Trades page shows a wrong P&L/Close/status for a saved group, and a trade twice, until the next full build (start or day turn), but no data is lost.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:308-326 — `for g in &inputs.ledger.groups { ... trip_of_trade.get(m) ... collapse(inputs, matched, TradeKey::Group(g.id), None, trips.clone(), slices, ...) ... used.extend(trips)` — a group's slices are gathered from every member trip, whatever its instrument. trades.rs:329 — `if used.contains(key) || managed(...) { continue; }` — a member trip is not listed on its own. rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:408 — `pub fn add_group(&self, members: &[TradeId], locked: bool, legacy_key: Option<&str>, at)` — no instrument constraint on members. SPEC.md:51 — "a saved group joins them, as it does any trades". Plan line 101 — "`build_trades`, ... take the families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts) to build; the engine's collections (`trades`, `positions`, `cash`) are held by key, and only the recomputed entries are compared"; plan lines 90-95 list five match couplings and none for groups; plan line 128's generated writes: "insert, revise and remove a record ...; add and remove a transfer link; set and clear an adjustment; open, move and orphan a trade; a journal entry" — no group. rust/crates/server/src/figures.rs:612-666 writes no group; tests_common.rs has no group. Failing scenario: G = {trade on AAPL, trade on MSFT} in one TFSA; a sale of AAPL is written; AAPL's family rematches; under the plan's words only AAPL's trip entry is rebuilt, G's entry keeps its pre-sale realized/pnl/closed_on while a fresh `Engine::build` (master trades.rs:296-341) folds the sale into G, and the AAPL trip appears both inside G and as its own row.

verdicts.why: The finding holds. On master a saved group is one TradeFig whose figures (pnl, pnl_cad, realized, exit, closed_on, status) are summed over the slices and lots of every member trip (trades.rs:308-326 collects the trips of all members, :320 flattens their slices, collapse at :213-215 sums pnl across them), and the member trips are then excluded from the per-trip list (:323 `used.extend`, :329 `used.contains(key)`). Members are arbitrary TradeIds: Book::add_group (crates/book/src/trades.rs:406-429) imposes no shared-instrument rule, and the legacy journal import creates groups this way (crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:277), so a group spanning two instruments, hence two families under the plan's definition, is a real state of the owner's book. The plan's five couplings (lines 90-97) are match-time couplings only; its derivation sentence (line 101) names "families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts)" and never groups; Change::Groups is folded into the delta (line 88) as a thing rebuilt "when named" (line 30), not when a member's family is rematched. Implemented as written, a sale of AAPL rematches AAPL's family and rebuilds TradeKey::Trip(AAPL trip), while TradeKey::Group(G) either keeps its old P&L and Close (stale) or, if the group loop is run over only the family's trips, is collapsed from the AAPL trip alone (missing MSFT's slices); and the rebuilt AAPL trip is emitted as its own trade unless the group's membership is consulted, so the Trades page shows it twice. Either way differs from Engine::build. The plan claims equality with a fresh build "for every kind of change" (line 128), but the property test's generated books and write list (accounts, shares, coins, contracts, transfers, corporate events, a multi-leg order; insert/revise/remove a record, transfer links, adjustments, open/move/orphan a trade, a journal entry) contain no groups, and the existing each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would (figures.rs:612) runs on a pulled fixture with no legacy import and so no groups. The right to refuse (line 148) fires only on what the property test shows, so this gap is not caught. Severity medium is right: a wrong displayed figure on a Trades page row, but only for owners with cross-instrument groups carried from the old app, and no new-group writer exists in the Rust server's HTTP routes.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/trades.rs:296-341 build_trades: :308 `for g in &inputs.ledger.groups`, :310-316 gathers every member's TripKey via identity.trade_of regardless of instrument, :320 `slices` = flattened slices of all member trips, :322 collapse(TradeKey::Group(g.id), trips, slices, lots_of(&trips)), :323 `used.extend(trips)`, :329 `if used.contains(key) ... continue` so a member trip is never listed alone. trades.rs:213 `let pnl = sum_money(currency, slices.iter().map(Slice::pnl))`, :214-215 realized/pnl_cad over the same slices, :219-227 closed_on/closed_at from all slices: the group's figures depend on every member's trip. rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:100-103 TripKey { opening, instrument }: trips of different instruments are distinct keys, hence distinct families. rust/crates/book/src/trades.rs:406-429 add_group(members: &[TradeId], ...) inserts whatever ids are given, no instrument check; rust/crates/book/src/import/mod.rs:277 the legacy import calls it. rust/crates/engine/src/engine.rs:421-426 Change::Ledger rematches and compares everything today (groups rebuilt for free); :453-458 Change::Groups rebuilds trades only when the groups themselves change. Plan: line 30 "Change::Trades / Groups / Journal ... rebuilds the ones the change names"; lines 90-97 the five couplings, none a group; line 101 derivation keyed by "families (or their trips, holdings, transactions and accounts)", groups absent; line 128 property test's books and writes list no group; figures.rs:612-668 the cited existing test exercises no group; line 148 refusal conditioned on "the property test would show it".

findings.title: A pull that removes a broker row stores nothing, so a file row it leaves with exactly one candidate is never linked
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354 (`link` runs over every live file row, :345-347 ambiguity links nothing), broker_reads.rs:422 (`link` after every pull); plan lines 111-115 ("each broker row the pull stored"; "a pull that stored nothing links nothing"), line 132
findings.claim: Today every pull re-runs `link` over all file rows, so an ambiguity resolved by a removal is linked at that pull. The plan looks up only the rows the pull stored, so a removal (or a supersede by `fills_give_way`) that leaves one candidate links nothing, and the file row's fill stays counted twice.
findings.failing_scenario: A file row (buy 100 X at 10.00 on day D) has two broker candidates (a duplicate the feed later withdraws). Master: `link` reports it ambiguous; the next pull removes the duplicate (`report.removed`), `link` finds one free candidate and supersedes the file row — the position holds 100. Plan: the pull stored nothing for X on D, `link` looks up nothing, the file row and the broker row both stay live — the position holds 200 and the broker check says the broker states 100.
findings.required_change: A pull's linking takes the movement keys of every broker row it stored, revised or removed (and every row `fills_give_way` superseded), and the linking-count test includes a removal that resolves an ambiguity.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan does not handle it; the plan's own words codify the regression. On master, `csv_import::link` (rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354) runs over every live file row (`book.live_records(&csv::source())`, :325) and is called after every pull (rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:422) regardless of what the pull stored. A pull removes broker rows it no longer lists through `unlisted` → `book.mark_removed` (rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:247-250; a final row gone within the span is removed when few, pull.rs:490-503), and the statements step withdraws booked rows the same way (rust/crates/broker/src/statements.rs:308-309). `mark_removed` calls `clear_derived`, which deletes the record's rows from `transactions` (rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:486, :502-505), and `engine_inputs::ledger` reads `book.transactions()` (rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:53), so after the removal the withdrawn duplicate is no longer a candidate in `candidates` (csv_import.rs:358-379, one tier for fills) and `link` finds exactly one free candidate and supersedes the file row (:340-343). A pull that only removes stores nothing (`records_new`/`records_revised` both zero; only `report.removed` grows). The plan, line 113-115, says a pull's link takes "each broker row the pull stored" and states outright "A pull that stored nothing links nothing"; acceptance criterion line 132 tests exactly that ("a pull that stored nothing compares none"). Nothing in part D or the delta description says a removed (or revised-away) key is looked up for file rows it leaves with one candidate. The "equal to a fresh build" property test (line 128) cannot catch this: linking is a book write, and both the incremental engine and a fresh build read the same unlinked book. So the failing scenario stands: file row F (buy 100 X on D) with two live broker candidates A and B → ambiguous on both master and plan; a later pull withdraws A and stores nothing → master links F to B (position 100, broker check agrees); plan links nothing (position 200, broker check says the broker states 100) and no later operation revisits F unless an unrelated row with the same movement key is stored. The `fills_give_way` half of the claim is weaker (that supersede runs after `link` on both master and plan, and in the common orderings the file row is linked to the fill row at import or to the broker row at the pull, so no ambiguity arises), but the removal half is a real divergence from master that the plan's own criterion locks in. Severity kept at medium: it needs a feed duplicate first (which the pull code explicitly anticipates by removing unlisted final rows), but once it occurs the position and broker check stay wrong indefinitely.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354 — `link` reads every live csv record (:325) and supersedes on exactly one free candidate (:340-343), ambiguity links nothing (:345-347); `candidates` (:358-379) matches fills in one tier against `e.inputs().ledger.transactions`. rust/crates/server/src/broker_reads.rs:409-427 — `f.pulled` then `link` on every pull, then `fills_give_way`. rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:247-250 and :462-503 — unlisted rows are `mark_removed`, pushed to `report.removed`, never "stored"; rust/crates/broker/src/statements.rs:308-309 — withdrawn booked rows also `mark_removed`. rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:471-497 and :502-505 — `mark_removed` → `clear_derived` deletes the record's `transactions` rows. rust/crates/server/src/engine_inputs.rs:53 — the ledger's transactions are `book.transactions()`. Plan lines 111-115 ("each broker row the pull stored is looked up"; "A pull that stored nothing links nothing"), line 132 ("a pull that stored nothing compares none"), line 128 (equality test compares engine to book, not linking).

verdicts.why: The finding holds. On master `csv_import::link` (rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:323-354) runs after every pull (broker_reads.rs:422) over every live file row (`book.live_records(&csv::source())`, :325), so an ambiguity (:345-347, nothing linked) is re-examined on the next pull and linked once exactly one candidate remains. A pull does remove broker rows: `unlisted` (broker/src/pull.rs:462-503) returns feed rows no longer listed within the span read (a non-final row gone is "posted again or withdrawn", :474-475) and `mark_removed` (book/src/records.rs:471-498) deletes their transactions via `clear_derived` (:486, :503-504), so they leave `book.transactions()` (engine_inputs.rs:53) and stop being candidates (csv_import.rs:363-373 filter on `ledger.transactions`). Likewise `fills_give_way` (book/src/fills.rs:198-216), run after `link` in the same pull (broker_reads.rs:427), supersedes a `bagholder-fill` row (source "bagholder-fill", fills.rs:25-27, which is not in `not_broker` = person + csv, csv_import.rs:329-330) and `supersede_counting` deletes its transactions (links.rs:92-94); so a file row ambiguous between the order's own fill and the broker's row on pull N becomes single-candidate only after `link` has run, and is linked on master at pull N+1. The plan (line 113 "each broker row the pull stored is looked up for live file rows", line 115 "A pull that stored nothing links nothing", table line 33) keys the pull's linking only on stored rows; `mark_removed` and `supersede` are not stores, and the plan names neither removals nor `fills_give_way` as a linking trigger. Under the plan the file row and the surviving broker row both stay live: the position shows double the quantity and the broker check disagrees, indefinitely rather than until the next pull. SPEC.md line 78 defines the link by state ("is linked ... when there is exactly one such row"), which the plan's pull no longer satisfies. findings.title: The movement index keyed on the broker row's trade day misses two of the three date matches, and nothing holds the indexed linking equal to the scan
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/csv_import.rs:396 (`b.trade_date == c.trade_date || Some(b.trade_date) == c.settle_date || b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)`) and :412 (cash moved: two alternatives); tests :706-958 (no case exercises a settle-day match: `settle` appears only at :383, :396, :412); plan line 111 (index key "trade day, and for a movement its cash and settle day"), line 132 (the test counts rows, holds no equality)
findings.claim: An index keyed on (account, instrument, kind, quantity, trade day, cash, settle day) answers an exact key; a file row whose day is the broker row's settle day, or whose settle day is the broker row's trade day, has no key to look up unless the broker row is indexed under both of its days and the file row looked up under both of its own. The acceptance criteria hold the count of rows compared, not that the indexed `link` links what the scan links.
findings.failing_scenario: A feed dividend row on X, trade day = record day D1, settle day = pay day D2; the statement export the person imports dates the dividend on D2 (its `date` column). Master links by `b.settle_date == Some(c.trade_date)` (SPEC §2 trade-44: "on its trade or settle day") and counts the cash once. The plan's lookup by the file row's day D2 finds no broker row keyed on D1 → unlinked, the dividend counted twice on the Cashflow page and in the payer's rate.
findings.required_change: Index each broker row under each of its days and look each file row up under each of its own; add an oracle test that, on generated books, the indexed `link` produces the same `linked` and `ambiguous` as `candidates` on master, and include a settle-day case.

verdicts.why: The core of the finding holds on reading the code and the plan: master's `candidates` links a movement on any of three day alternatives (csv_import.rs:396) and cash moved on two (:412), per SPEC trade-44; the plan's index (line 111) names one exact key with a single trade day and settle day and says nothing about indexing or looking up under each day; and no acceptance criterion holds the indexed `link` equal to the scan (line 132 counts rows; the line-128 property test and `each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would` at figures.rs:612 never call `link`; line 134 only times and counts). The existing tests at csv_import.rs:706-968 exercise only same-day matches. The finding's literal scenario is wrong in one detail, though: a feed row never carries a settle day (wealthsimple/src/mapping.rs:361 sets `settle_date: None`), and the only broker rows with one are statement rows (statement.rs:316) which have no instrument (:319), so alternative 3 cannot fire against a feed dividend. The wrong figure is still reachable, through alternative 2 and through the key itself: the Activities file layout reads `settlement_date` onto every row, dividends and deposits included (broker/src/csv.rs:425, :435, :734), and the old app always fills that column (store/src/activities.rs:118). A file dividend dated D1 with settlement D2 against the feed's dividend on D2 links on master and finds no exact key; and a key that literally includes the settle day makes (D1, Some(D1)) unequal to the feed's (D1, None), losing even the same-day match for every Activities-export row, so the dividend or deposit is counted twice. Severity kept at medium: the plan's described key cannot reproduce the rule it says it keeps, and the plan's tests cannot detect that.
