findings.title: A no-instrument transaction put in the cash family loses the account-wide taint it carries
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1283-1318, esp. :1309-1312 and :1314-1317 (a multi-leg order with legs unstated naming no instrument taints every holding of the account) and :840-849 (the taint is merged into each book touched after it, in order); plan line 97 ("Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only") against the fifth coupling in the same paragraph
findings.claim: The family assignment rule as written sends the leg-unstated no-instrument order to the cash family, so inserting or removing one reaches the cash totals only, while the fifth coupling needs it to reach every holding of the account, in sequence (the taint applies to holdings touched after it).
findings.failing_scenario: A pull stores a Wealthsimple multi-leg order row the mapping marks `leg-unstated` with no instrument, dated D. Fresh build: every holding of that account carries `LegUnstated` from D, its positions and trades show waiting. Plan: the change reaches the cash family, no holding is rematched, the figures stay clean, and `Entity::Book`'s waiting count and the Trades page disagree with a fresh build until the next change to each holding.
findings.required_change: State that a transaction whose record carries `leg-unstated` and names no instrument belongs to the account-wide family (every instrument of the account), merging the account's families while one exists and splitting them when it goes; make the generator's "multi-leg order naming no instrument" exactly this row.

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says and the plan's written rule contradicts its own fifth coupling for this one row. On master, `apply` (rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1283-1318) treats a transaction whose record carries `leg-unstated` and names no instrument by setting `account_taint[account]` (:1310) and tainting every book of that account already open (:1311, :1314-1316), and `book()` (:840-849) merges `account_taint` into every book of that account touched afterwards, so the taint reaches every holding of the account from that row's position in the record on. The shared case `rust/crates/engine/tests/cases/multileg.json:28-45` is exactly this: `a2` in account A names no instrument, and A's round trip in X (`a1`) is expected to wait while B's in X shows 100.00. The plan lists the coupling (line 95, `account_taint`) and says the engine keeps "the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint" (line 97), but its family rule in the same paragraph puts this row in the per-account cash family ("Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only") and its reach rule ("a change reaches the families of every transaction ... it names") then reaches that cash family only. Built as written, inserting `a2` rematches A's cash family alone; X's family (A and B, coupled by instrument) is not rematched, and trade `a1` keeps 100.00 instead of waiting; removing `a2` leaves the stale taint. Either is a figure different from a fresh build. The plan does not say how an account "made whole" extends reach, and nothing in it exempts this row from the cash-only sentence, so it is not already handled in the text. Severity lowered from medium to low because the plan's own acceptance test (line 128) generates "a multi-leg order naming no instrument" and holds every step equal to a fresh build, and the right-to-refuse clause (line 148) says a missed coupling is added to the families, so a build that followed the cash-only sentence would most likely fail the suite before merging; the defect is in the written contract, and the fix is the one-sentence rule the finding asks for.
verdicts.evidence: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1289 reads the record's problems for `leg-unstated`; :1309-1312 `None => { self.account_taint.entry(account).or_default().merge(&gaps); self.out.books.keys().filter(|(a, _)| *a == account)... }`; :1314-1316 taints each; :840-849 `book()` merges `under`, `own`, `whole` (= `self.account_taint.get(&account)`) into every book of the account touched after. rust/crates/book/src/import/mapping.rs:338-356 produces such a row (instrument `None` when the rule names none or the lookup fails, `leg-unstated` pushed when `raw_type` contains MULTILEG). rust/crates/engine/tests/cases/multileg.json:41 (`a2`, account A, no instrument, `problems: ["leg-unstated"]`) and :45 (expect `a1` pnl gaps `leg-unstated`, `b1` pnl 100.00). Plan docs/plans/stage-3-the-record-by-change.md line 95 (fifth coupling, `account_taint`), line 97 ("plus the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint" ... "Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only. A change reaches the families of every transaction, instrument and adjustment it names"), line 128 (generator includes "a multi-leg order naming no instrument"; equality with a fresh build after every step), line 148 (right to refuse: a missed coupling is added to the families).

verdicts.why: The code does what the finding says (a leg-unstated record naming no instrument taints every holding of the account: ledger.rs:1309-1312 taints every existing book and sets account_taint, and book() at :840-849 merges it into every book touched afterwards; the shared case multileg.json "a multi-leg order whose row names nothing: everything the account holds waits" pins it, and mapping.rs:338-356 confirms such a row exists). But the plan already handles this coupling rather than sending it to the cash family. Line 95 lists it as the fifth coupling by name (`account_taint`); line 97 states the engine keeps "a disjoint-set over instruments, plus the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint", i.e. the account-wide taint is modelled explicitly as something that makes the whole account one unit, and families are "merged or split as links come and go"; line 128's property test generator explicitly includes "a multi-leg order naming no instrument" among the generated books and holds Engine::differences against a fresh build after every insert, revision and removal; line 148 commits to adding any coupling the property test shows missing. The build the finding describes (rematch the cash family only, holdings left clean) cannot pass acceptance criterion 2, so the plan does not permit the wrong figure. What remains is a wording imprecision: the sentence "Transactions with no instrument (cash moved) form one family per account; they affect the cash totals and cash rows only" is overbroad for the one no-instrument row that carries `leg-unstated`, and could say so in a clause. That is a clarity point, caught by the plan's own test, not a figure the plan would let come out different from a fresh build.
verdicts.evidence: ledger.rs:1289 reads the record's `leg-unstated` problem; :1309-1312 (`None` instrument arm) merges the gaps into `account_taint` and collects every book of the account, which :1314-1316 taints; :840-849 (`book()`) merges `account_taint` into every book accessed later, so every holding of the account carries LegUnstated whether opened before or after the row. ledger.rs:713-715 documents account_taint as "every holding in an account waits on: a multi-leg order naming no instrument". mapping.rs:338-356: `instrument` may be None independently of the MULTILEG flag, so the no-instrument leg-unstated row is real. tests/cases/multileg.json:27-46 is the shared case for exactly this row. Plan line 95: fifth coupling "every holding of an account, where a multi-leg order names no instrument (`account_taint`)"; line 97: "plus the accounts made whole by an account-wide taint ... merged or split as links come and go"; line 128: generator includes "a multi-leg order naming no instrument", equality with Engine::build held after every write; line 148: a missing coupling is added, never worked around.

findings.title: The header's beyond-held sentences change order when `beyond` becomes a map
findings.where: rust/crates/server/src/status.rs:206-216 (sentences in the order of `matched.beyond`, which is the match's order of application, ledger.rs:1200-1205); plan line 99 (`beyond` becomes a map by transaction) and line 36 ("Nothing on screen changes")
findings.claim: Iterating a map by TransactionId orders the sentences by record id (storage order), not by the order the match found them, so the header's text differs from today's for a book with more than one such sale.
findings.failing_scenario: Two sales beyond held, one in 2024 stored in the first pull and a back-dated 2023 row stored by a later import: today the header says the 2023 one first (applied first); as a map the 2024 one comes first (older record id). Same facts, different header line; a page comparing text sees a change.
findings.required_change: Keep an order on the listed entries (the match's order key, or the transaction's day and instant) and emit the sentences in it, or say in SPEC §4 the order they take.

verdicts.why: The mechanics hold. Today the header's beyond-held sentences come out in the order the match applies transactions, which is by trade date first. The plan turns `beyond` into a map keyed by transaction id and does not change status.rs. Transaction ids are UUID v7 record ids, so iterating that map gives creation (storage) order, not day order. Two sentences about the same facts can therefore swap places in the header. That breaks the plan's own promise that "Nothing on screen changes" (plan line 36). It also goes against status.rs's stated rule of ordering header sentences the way a reader looks them up, not by id. Severity stays low for three reasons. No figure changes. An incremental build and a fresh build still agree with each other, because both read the same map. SPEC §4 (pages-13) sets no order for these sentences, so the new order is a visible change, not a wrong value.
verdicts.evidence:
- status.rs:206-216 (master d6824aa7): `for b in beyond` walks `figures.matched.beyond` in its stored order. Nothing re-sorts it; only the check sentences are sorted, at :190 and :202.
- engine/src/ledger.rs:326: `pub beyond: Vec<Beyond>`. Entries are pushed at :1204 (and :1965) in match order.
- ledger.rs:2143 sorts the match by `order_key`. Per :660-675 that key is (trade_date, bucket, occurred_at, record_rank, source_key, leg_rank, content), so today the 2023 sale comes before the 2024 one.
- core/src/ids.rs:1 says ids are UUID v7, which are time-ordered. ids.rs:174-178 derives Ord on `TransactionId { record, leg }`, so a map keyed by it iterates in record-creation order. A back-dated 2023 row stored after a 2024 row therefore sorts second.
- Plan line 99 makes `beyond` (and the other lists) "a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about" and gives no ordering. Plan line 36 says "Nothing on screen changes".
- SPEC.md:397 (pages-13) lists the "took … more than the book held" sentences without setting their order.
- The plan's equality test (line 128) compares the engine against a fresh build, so it cannot catch this: both sides would show the same new order.

verdicts.why: I could not refute this finding. Today, `match_lots` puts every transaction in one global order before matching: first the trade day, then the time bucket, then the instant, the record's rank and the source key. `Matcher::beyond` pushes onto a Vec in that order, so the header's "took more than the book held" sentences come out by trade day. The plan (line 99) turns `beyond` into a map keyed by the transaction it is about. `TransactionId` derives Ord as (record, leg), and `RecordId` is a UUID v7 the book creates when it stores the record, so iterating the map gives the order the records were stored in. A back-dated row from a later import has a newer UUID and moves after older-stored rows, even though the match applies it first today. Plan line 36 says "Nothing on screen changes". The plan names no order for the listed entries, and SPEC §pages-13 names none for these sentences. The plan's property test (line 128) compares the engine updated change by change against `Engine::build`, which uses the same map. Both sides would iterate the same way, so the test cannot catch a change from today's order. No figure is wrong; only the order of sentences in the header changes. That is why the severity stays low.
verdicts.evidence:
- rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:2142-2143: the transactions are sorted by `order_key`, which is (trade_date, bucket, occurred_at, record_rank, source_key, leg_rank, content) (ledger.rs:660-676).
- ledger.rs:1200-1205 and :1965: `self.out.beyond.push(Beyond{..})` adds to the Vec in that applied order.
- rust/crates/server/src/status.rs:206-216: `for b in beyond { out.push(format!("{what} of {} in {}{day} took {} more than the book held.", ...)) }` emits the sentences in Vec order, and they reach the header through status.rs:118 and `failures`.
- rust/crates/core/src/ids.rs:1: "Each is a UUID v7, made by the book when a thing ...". ids.rs:27 and :104 make `RecordId` wrap `uuid::Uuid`. ids.rs:175-179 derives `PartialOrd, Ord` on `TransactionId { record, leg }`, so a map by `TransactionId` iterates in storage order.
- Plan line 99: "every collection in `Matched` that is a list today (`beyond`, ...) becomes a map by the transaction (or holding) it is about". It gives no iteration order.
- Plan line 36: "Nothing on screen changes."
- SPEC.md:397 (pages-13) lists "each sale or move that took out more units than the book held" and names no order.
- Scenario: sale A dated 2024 is stored in the first pull; sale B dated 2023 is imported later, so its record UUID is newer. Today the header shows B then A; under the plan it shows A then B.

findings.title: A transfer's receiving side can name another instrument; the fourth coupling must union by the instruments as the engine reads them
findings.where: rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1661-1665 (`link_of` returns `recv.instrument.unwrap_or(instrument)`) and :1596-1633 (the lots are placed on `dest_instr`); plan lines 94 and 97 ("the two sides of a transfer between accounts", "extended by the fourth across accounts")
findings.claim: The engine places the taken lots on the receiving transaction's own instrument, which the code allows to differ from the sending side's. If families are joined only across accounts of one instrument, a link whose sides read as two instruments leaves the receiving holding in a family that is not rematched when the sending side changes.
findings.failing_scenario: TransferOut of X in account A linked to a TransferIn whose transaction reads as Y in account B (a coin received under another id). A revised out row changes the lots that move: X's family is rematched, Y's is not, so B's holding of Y keeps the lots as they were while a fresh build moves the revised ones.
findings.required_change: Define the transfer coupling over the two linked transactions' instruments as read (both sides), not over one instrument across accounts, and generate such a link in the property test.

verdicts.why:
The code does what the finding says, and the case can happen on master. The engine puts the moved lots on the receiving transaction's own instrument (`recv.instrument.unwrap_or(instrument)`). Nothing keeps the two linked transactions on the same instrument after the link is made:
- The link is stored by record and leg.
- Revising a record clears that record's transactions, problems and sightings, but leaves `transfer_links` in place.
- The statements linker (`join_moves`) pairs an out and an in by cash amount and day only, with no check that the instruments match.
- Only the pull's `link_moves` requires the same instrument, and only when it creates the link.

The plan defines the transfer coupling as "the two sides of a transfer between accounts" and builds a family from "the first three, extended by the fourth across accounts". It never says that the two linked transactions' instruments must be put in one family. Under the "one instrument across accounts" reading, which is the natural one, coupling 1 already covers that case, so the transfer coupling would add nothing. A later revision of the out record names only the out transaction, so it reaches X's family only. Y's family is not rematched, and the receiving holding of Y in account B keeps the old lots, while a fresh build moves the revised ones. The plan's mention of families being "merged or split as links come and go" hints at unions, but it is not explicit. Its property test lists "transfers between accounts" and never generates a link whose two sides read as different instruments, so the test would not catch this. Low severity: it needs a link whose receiving side reads as another instrument, which is uncommon but reachable.
verdicts.evidence:
- rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1661-1665: `link_of` returns `(to, recv.account, recv.instrument.unwrap_or(instrument))`.
- ledger.rs:1596-1633: `place(dest, dest_instr, lots)` and `push_lot(dest, dest_instr, ...)` put the lots on the receiving side's instrument.
- ledger.rs:2153: `links_out` is built from every `ledger.transfer_links`.
- rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:502-507: `clear_derived` deletes only `transactions`, `record_problems` and `instrument_sightings` (plus adjustments), not `transfer_links`.
- rust/crates/book/schema/v27.sql:566-572: `transfer_links` is keyed on `(out_record, out_leg)` against `in_record`/`in_leg`, so it survives a re-derivation that changes the in leg's instrument.
- rust/crates/broker/src/statements.rs:1112-1127: `join_moves` links an out to an in using kind, account, day and cash only, with no instrument check.
- rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:613-624: `link_moves` checks `i.instrument == o.instrument`, but only when the link is made.
- Plan line 94: "the two sides of a transfer between accounts (`transfer_links`)".
- Plan line 97: "a family is a set of instruments joined by any of the first three, extended by the fourth across accounts" and "A change reaches the families of every transaction ... it names, before and after".
- Plan line 128: the property test generates "transfers between accounts" but no link whose sides name different instruments.

verdicts.why:
I could not refute this finding. On master the engine puts a transfer's lots on the receiving transaction's own instrument as the engine reads it. Nothing keeps the link's two sides on one instrument after the link is made, so the two sides can name different instruments.

The plan does not plainly cover this case. Line 97 says a family is "a set of instruments joined by any of the first three, extended by the fourth across accounts". Read literally, only the first three couplings join instruments, and the transfer coupling only spans accounts. Under coupling one, an instrument's family already spans every account. So the fourth coupling adds nothing unless it also joins the two sides' instruments, and the plan never says it does.

The scenario can happen, though rarely:
1. The pull links two rows only when their instruments are equal at link time. After that, a revision of the receiving record re-derives its transactions and can resolve them to another instrument. The link is kept, because derive deletes the record's transactions but not its transfer_links rows.
2. That revision reaches both X and Y, before and after, so it is handled.
3. A later revision of the sending record names only X's record. Under the literal reading only X's family is matched again. B's lots of Y keep the old lots, while a fresh build moves the revised ones.

The property test (plan line 128) catches this only if its generator links, or later revises, a side so that the two sides read as different instruments. The fallback at line 148 relies on that test.

Severity stays low: the case is rare, and the natural fix is one sentence. The plan should say the transfer coupling unions the instruments of both linked transactions as read.
verdicts.evidence:
Paths are under scratchpad/cm on master d6824aa7.

- rust/crates/engine/src/ledger.rs:1661-1665: `link_of` returns `recv.instrument.unwrap_or(instrument)`, the receiving transaction's instrument from the engine's own ledger. Lines 1596-1633 place the moved lots and the `left` units with `dest_instr`, and taint them there.
- rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:608-616: the engine reads transactions AsBook, as `COALESCE(j.into_id, t.instrument_id)`. A join maps an instrument wholesale (identity.rs:711-713), so a join moves both sides together.
- rust/crates/book/src/records.rs:243-276: `derive` (a revision) runs `DELETE FROM transactions WHERE record_id = ?` and re-inserts the resolved legs, possibly on another instrument. It does not touch transfer_links. The links are removed only on clear (book/src/clear.rs:160).
- rust/crates/broker/src/pull.rs:614-627: `link_moves` requires `i.instrument == o.instrument` only at link time.
- rust/crates/broker/src/statements.rs:1108-1130: `join_moves` links by cash amount, day and account, with no instrument check.
- Plan, line 94, lists the coupling as "the two sides of a transfer between accounts (`transfer_links`)".
- Plan, line 97, says "a family is a set of instruments joined by any of the first three, extended by the fourth across accounts". The fourth is not among the instrument-joining couplings.
- Plan, line 72, logs both sides' records only when a transfer_links row changes, not when one side's record is revised.
- Plan, line 128: the property test generates "transfers between accounts" and "add and remove a transfer link". It does not say the two sides can read as different instruments.
- Plan, line 148: the fallback depends on the property test exposing a coupling that was missed.

fine: Coupling 1 (one instrument across accounts): `places` (ledger.rs:735, :2164-2175) and `last_price` (:1188-1196) are keyed by instrument and read in global order; a family holding every account's transactions of the instrument reproduces both.

Coupling 2 (contract ↔ underlying): `underlying_taint`/`instrument_taint` (:1294-1307), `book()` (:840-849), `apply_delivery` (:1669-1724), `rolled_from` (:1534-1554, only legs on the same underlying), `expired_worthless` (:1266-1281) all stay inside contract ∪ underlying; two contracts on one underlying join through the underlying id even when the underlying itself has no transactions, provided the union is by id.

Coupling 3 (event legs): `event_groups` (:2180-2192) groups rows by account, day and the legs' instruments; `consumed` (:1758-1760), `stated`, `before`, `lieu_fraction` are all over those instruments — sound once the anchor row's instrument is included (low finding above).

Coupling 4 (transfer links): `links_out`/`links_in` (:2153-2154), `link_of`/`cost_on_arrival` (:1655-1665, by id), `place()` moving lots and `Trip.account` across accounts (:1129-1150, :1596-1633) stay within the two sides; the receiving instrument can differ from the sending one (:1664), so both ids must be unioned. The cash legs beside a move record (mapping.rs:978-992) have no instrument and match nothing.
Coupling 5 (account-wide taint): `account_taint` (:1309-1312, :843) reaches only the one account's holdings, from the record's day on; making the whole account one family is a correct superset.

Dust is not a cross-instrument coupling: `price_of` (:1188-1196) uses the instrument's own stated or last price; `is_dust`/`is_dust_worth` (dust.rs:16-39) read the account's `coin_minimum` and the rates, never another instrument.

Cash rows with no instrument: `Matched.cash` (:2244-2251) is a per-account, per-currency sum; per-(account, family) partial sums give the same totals (the only divergence is `Dec` overflow at 28 digits, unreachable by a book). `apply` returns at :1319 for a no-instrument row that is not multi-leg, so cash-only rows do not touch lots.

Sort order: `order_key` (:660-676) is a total key per transaction except for exact ties; a subset sorted by the same key keeps the global relative order provided `record_rank` is taken over the whole record (medium finding above). Ties fall back to the input order of `ledger.transactions`, and `engine/tests/cases.rs:837` already asserts the figures are unchanged under a reversed input, so holding transactions in a `BTreeMap<RecordId, _>` does not change results.

The `Effect::Open` look-ahead (:2210-2224) filters to the same account and instrument, so it never reaches outside a family; the one-day record loop (:2225-2242) chooses legs by `meets_opposite`, whose state is the leg's own instrument's, so the relative order of a family's legs is preserved on the subset (modulo the `len() == 1` test, medium finding above).

Expiry: `expiring`, `ended_on_record` and `expire_before` (:705-731, :1211-1243) are per (account, instrument); interleaving `expire_before` by the family's own days gives the same closes dated on the expiry; `record_units`/`dirty` (:1246-1262) are per holding and insert only on change, so running once per leg or once per record is the same.

Identity: `identify` (identity.rs:65-110) looks up trips by `TripKey` and by fills ∩ instruments, both inside the trip's family; `managed` is per account and `accounts.managed` is never updated after `add_account` (book/src/identity.rs:63-100, no `UPDATE accounts`), so an `account` log key reaches `BookFig` only.

Derivation: `build_positions` is per holding (positions.rs:138-287); `build_cashflow` keyed by transaction plus `stock_dividends` (cashflow.rs:52-100); `payer_rates` per instrument over every account's dividend rows and `matched.units` (cashflow.rs:205-287), within coupling 1; `broker_checks` per account over `matched.cash[account]` and `matched.units` of that account (equity.rs:112-196), and `held()`'s put-sale lookup reads the hold's instrument's units, so every account holding anything of a rematched family must be rechecked, which the plan's 'accounts' wording covers.

`Engine::past` (engine.rs:297-326) and the comparison tool build whole from the inputs, so the keyed ledger shape needs only the iterator the plan promises; `scope.rs:868` and `needs.rs:81` read the ledger at query time, not from a stale derived collection.

The change log itself: SQLite serialises writers, so `seq` order is commit order and a rolled-back row is never visible to the reader; a write committed between the log read and the keyed reads is re-read on the next pass with the same result (idempotent). `Change::Clock` still matching everything is correctly out of scope, since expiry depends on today.

A trigger fires inside the writer's own transaction on any connection, including raw ones that bypass Book (demo_facts.rs:80-82, book/tests/successions.rs:295); a rollback leaves no row (lib.rs:122-130, sqlite/src/lib.rs:112-125); the plan's reason for triggers over writers naming their changes holds for these.

`match_lots` sorts the transactions by its own key (engine/src/ledger.rs:2141-2143 `order_key`, with `record_rank` and the record's source_key), so holding them as BTreeMap<RecordId, Vec<Transaction>> changes no match order.

`instrument_sightings` INSERT OR REPLACE (identity.rs:865) replaces a row of the same (record, leg, instrument) key, so the INSERT trigger's `instrument` key covers the implicit delete; REPLACE's missing DELETE trigger matters only where the replaced row named a different key (transfer_links, covered in a finding).

A superseded or removed record's transactions, problems and sightings are deleted in the same write as its state change (`clear_derived`, records.rs:502-507; links.rs:93-94; records.rs:486-487), so the `record` key and the `instrument` keys of its sightings are both logged; removed records' problems are already dropped by the whole read (engine_inputs.rs:39-49), so the keyed reader has no new case to reproduce.

Child rows are written after their parent and deleted before it (journal_tags trades.rs:344-358, Clear journal clear.rs:190; adjustment_legs facts.rs:451-474 and 479-483; clear.rs:166-167; trade_group_members trades.rs:417-426), so a trigger that joins to the parent for its key (journal -> subject, adjustment_legs -> applies) finds it on both INSERT and DELETE.

`UPDATE source_records SET derived_version` (records.rs:287, identity.rs:720-726) and `set_state` log a `record` key whose re-read is idempotent; `rederive_all` runs before the start's build (figures.rs:185-188), so its rows are pruned with the start.

A trigger dropped by a later migration that rebuilds a ledger table through a new table and a rename (as migration 026 did for statements) is caught by the plan's coverage test run on a freshly migrated book, provided the test checks sqlite_master for the trigger rather than only that a write logs; `schema_text` (migrate.rs:362-374) also commits triggers to schema/v28.sql for review.

Clear data: `DELETE FROM transactions`/`trades` without WHERE (clear.rs:171,190) loses the truncate optimisation once DELETE triggers exist and writes one log row per row before the log is emptied; correct, if slower, as long as the log is emptied last in that transaction and the seq does not restart (the AUTOINCREMENT change).

A second process (compare.rs on a copy, capacity.rs on a scratch home, demo_facts.rs before the server starts, read_sources.rs) only appends to the log; the server's keyed re-read of what they name is idempotent, and none of them deletes log rows.

The log grows only with real changes: a pull whose payloads are unchanged writes nothing to a ledger table (records.rs:167-171, Outcome::Unchanged), statements, reads, holds and orders are not ledger tables, and `settle_successions` writes only when the wanted joins differ (identity.rs:707-714); the indexed `WHERE seq > ?` read stays cheap between starts.

`csv_import::candidates` already reads the engine's ledger (AsBook transactions, csv_import.rs:358-408), not `transactions_as_named`, so part D's index built from the same delta changes no matching; `transactions_as_named` (records.rs:588) is the pull's own index in the broker crate (pull.rs:586), outside the server boundary test's scan.
The WAL hook signals after the commit has landed (sqlite/src/lib.rs:63-70, 92-100), so a reader woken by it sees the log rows the commit wrote.

`Engine::differences` compares figures and quotes (engine.rs:644-652), not inputs: the property test (criterion 2) catches a stale key only where it moves a figure, which is why the omitted-key cases above are listed as findings rather than left to that test.

Within one import, a per-row lookup with a `used` set shared across the file's rows reproduces `a_broker_row_takes_the_place_of_one_file_row_only` (csv_import.rs:334-343, :790-798), given the ledger's order (finding 5).

`taken` (book.superseding(csv), records.rs:734-743) is a per-record fact readable by key from link_records' `to` side; excluding a broker row that already took a file row needs no whole read, and a broker row that superseded an old-database import row (pull.rs:544-554) stays a candidate today and under the plan alike.

A broker row revised while it supersedes a file row: the file row is not live (links.rs:93-94), so neither today's link nor the plan examines it; the revision reaches the figures through the record's own delta.

A broker row removed and later listed again, or superseded and re-stated: store_inner keeps the record's state and derives nothing unless it is live (records.rs:167-184), so it has no transactions to be a candidate under either scheme; a file row it had superseded stays superseded (records.rs:468-470), as documented.
`not_broker` (live person-source and file-source records, csv_import.rs:329-330) is a per-record source attribute; an index that never enters those sources as candidates is equivalent.
The fill price compared at the file's places (csv_import.rs:365, :371) is per pair and depends on the instrument's info; the plan's fill key rightly leaves price out of the key.

The import's `record_changed` before link and link's own `record_changed` after a taking (csv_import.rs:273, :350-352): a supersede writes source_records, transactions, record_problems and link_records (links.rs:93-108), all under part A's triggers, so the engine sees the superseded row leave through the log.

The import report's linked and ambiguous counts are filtered to this file's lines (csv_import.rs:275-283), so re-examining older rows under touched keys (the required change) changes no report figure for the file; a linked older row still triggers record_changed as today.
Statement rows that reconcile against a live file row are superseded directly in the pull (statements.rs:297-307, :319-322), not through csv_import::link; that path is unchanged by part D.

`fills_give_way` (fills.rs:198-216, broker_reads.rs:427) supersedes Bagholder's own fill records by the broker's row and is independent of file-row linking; a broker row that took a fill record can still take a file row today and under the plan, since `taken` counts only csv-source `from` records.

Equity and returns (equity.rs:70-78 build_equity from inputs.market.brokers only; scope.rs:1066-1079 equity_block over equity+benchmarks+filters): no record change can alter them; compared by differences anyway.
Benchmarks (engine.rs:274,438,445 from market.benchmarks, facts.rates, clock): untouched by a record change; compared by differences.
Needs (needs.rs:74-148): worked out on demand from the in-memory inputs and matched, never cached in the engine, so it is right whenever matched and the ledger are; not compared, and need not be.

Past-day holdings (engine.rs:403-420, 297-326): every held day is forgotten on any Ledger/Adjustments/Trades/Journal change (stale = Date::MIN) and rebuilt whole from the in-memory ledger on demand, so a keyed ledger cannot leave a past day stale (its cost, a full match per asked day, is outside this lens).

Markets views (wire/markets.rs:290,359-360,619-624) read positions through Portfolio's indexes and the instruments' names; keyed positions serve them provided the slice order is kept (finding on order).
Entity::Book (engine.rs:190-197,604-607): accounts, instruments, waiting (keyed by transaction at ledger.rs:1572,1738), activity count and today are all replaceable by key and are compared.

Couplings read from ledger.rs and matched against the plan's five: places (2164-2175) and last_price (1188-1196) per instrument across every account (1); underlying through terms at 750-752, taints at 1294-1306 and 1342, deliveries at 1669-1724, rolled_from at 1534-1553 within one underlying (2); event groups at 2180-2192 and legs at 1787-1799 including leg-named instruments with no row (3); transfer links at 2153-2154 and 1584-1647 (4; note `dest_instr = recv.instrument.unwrap_or(instrument)` at 1664, so the builder must join both sides' instruments, not only accounts); account_taint at 1309-1312 and 843 (5).

Contract expiry (ledger.rs:1211-1243, 2243): driven by the `expiring` map and the contract's own expiry date; which family's transaction triggers `expire_before` does not change the closes it makes or the units it records, so a family-only match expires the same contracts on the same day.
ended_on_record (ledger.rs:2158-2163) and rounding_held/count_row (824-838) are per (account, instrument): inside the instrument's family.

payer_rates keyed by instrument (cashflow.rs:205-286): its inputs are that instrument's cash rows in any account, its units in any account (matched.units), declared, frequencies and ex_dividends, all within the instrument's family or outside the record.

broker_checks per account (equity.rs:112-196): reads matched.cash[account], matched.units of the account, last_price and current_price of the instruments it or the broker holds, and dust; the families' accounts (every account holding an instrument of the family, plus the cash family's account) cover every input that a family rematch can move.

identify per family (identity.rs:48-110): anchors come from the whole trade list in memory, the moved/unclaimed search is over trips holding the anchor's transaction and instrument, which lie in the anchor's family; settle_trades (figures.rs:74-119) runs until clean at start, so untouched families have empty needs_trade/moved/joined/unclaimed when a keyed change arrives.

roles (ledger.rs:1483,1504), arrived (818, once per transaction via 1326/1366), dust (1202, 1433: never both for one transaction, since a beyond leaves nothing to write off) and disagreements (1373) are one per transaction and keyable as the plan says.

The order of ledger.transactions: the plan (line 88) calls it 'the record's order', but Book::transactions orders by account, trade_date, occurred_at, record, leg (records.rs:617); it matters only at ties of match_lots' total sort key (ledger.rs:660-676, 2143, same source_key and identical leg content across two records) and at overflow in sums, so a BTreeMap<RecordId, Vec<Transaction>> iterator changes no figure in practice.
The Trades view (views.rs:703-729) rebuilds rows by id and re-sorts by column, so a keyed trades collection serves it except for tie order (finding on order).

sized()/Generated::new: accounts, instruments and trades each scale by `times`, months fixed, trades drawn uniformly over invest accounts and shares (generated.rs:322-343, 365-374), so the ×4 book is breadth; stated as a finding, verified in the code
The probes' measurement windows (capacity.rs:587-589, 597-599) include the write, record_changed and, for import, link, as plan line 143 says

judge() (capacity.rs:688-707): Pi wall time at ×4 against the budget for waited-on ops, GROWTH_LIMIT on steps, allocations and bytes read for per-change ops; listed_disagree makes OVER_BUDGET shrink only; the listed ops measured once then seven times when within (run(), :740-746)

The change log read `WHERE seq > ?` on an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY is O(entries since last applied); dedup is over those entries, not the book; truncation at start and in Book::clear keeps it bounded across starts
The symbol/terms index built at a start from every instrument is a start's whole read, which the plan allows

Book::store's Unchanged path writes nothing to a ledger table (records.rs:167-175; record_refs at :177 is not read by the ledger), so a pull that re-stores known rows logs nothing; broker_connections is only inserted (identity.rs:36), so the `account` kind does not churn per pull

The Matcher's cross-holding state (expiring, ended_on_record, lieu_fraction, rounding_held, dirty, consumed, underlying_taint, instrument_taint, account_taint, places, last_price; ledger.rs:702-739) is keyed by (account, instrument), by underlying, by transfer link, by instrument across accounts, or by account: each falls inside the plan's five couplings; expire_before (ledger.rs:1211-1243) acts per contract and reads only its underlying's closes
Cash totals per account are a sum over transactions (ledger.rs:2244-2251), so holding them per (account, family) and summing is exact
The import probe's 20 rows name 20 distinct held shares (capacity.rs:593), so its families are 20 at both sizes; entries by symbol (held_by_symbol, contract_by_terms) are covered by plan E

Budget sources: ANSWER_MS 100 for add-trade, TO_FIGURES_MS 1,000 for import, PI_SLOWDOWN 2.1 applied to the ×4 wall time; the Verification table's figures are consistent with that arithmetic (347.1 × 2.1 = 729)

Change::Trades/Groups/Journal folded into one delta keeps the one-state rule (figures.rs:431-446) provided the record and the trades are read in one snapshot and applied under the lock — that condition is finding 3; the final state after one apply is the same as today's three applies followed by Ledger.

settle_trades (figures.rs:74-120) by key: the loop's end condition can be computed from the writes made or a key compare of the trades read back; `Identity` per family is consistent because a trade's anchor instrument places it in the family of its own trip (identity.rs:48-56, :86-108).

Change::Adjustments by family: match_lots:2178-2192 groups event rows by the anchor's account, day and the legs' instruments; apply_event:1786-1799 reads and moves only legs' instruments; reaching the families before and after the change (plan line 97) covers a leg naming an instrument outside the anchor's family and a cleared adjustment splitting them.
Change::Closes on an underlying by family: expire_before:1211-1243 and expired_worthless:1266-1281 decide each contract from its own lots and its underlying's close, both inside coupling 2.

Couplings 1 and 2 match the code: `places` per (instrument, source) over every account (ledger.rs:2164-2175), `last_price` per instrument (:1188-1196), assignment/exercise moving the underlying (:1669-1724), rolls by underlying (:1534+), underlying_taint (:1297-1306).

Per-family cash partial sums (plan line 99) reproduce match_lots:2244-2251 exactly, and broker_checks (equity.rs:112-196) reads only its account's cash, units, last_price and holds, so a family change rechecking its accounts is complete.
payer_rates and build_cashflow read per instrument/transaction and matched.stock_dividends (cashflow.rs:83), so rebuilding them for the recomputed families' instruments and rows is complete.
Engine::past (engine.rs:297-326) keeps a whole match over a filtered ledger; a by-record transaction map with an iterator in the record's order serves it, and the stale rule (:403-420) is unchanged.

The full build at a start is today's: Figures::open (figures.rs:176-191) runs rederive_all then builds whole; deleting log rows at or below MAX(seq) after that build is sound since nothing else consumes the log. The day turning keeps Change::Clock's whole rematch (engine.rs:434-440) as the plan says.

No figure's definition in SPEC §2 (Trade) or §4 (the broker check, its confirmation rule at equity.rs:146-154 and the holds at :212-251) changes; the matching rule for linking (SPEC trade-42..44) is kept in substance apart from the index lookups in finding 6.

The trigger table covers every table engine_inputs::ledger and facts().adjustments read (connections, accounts, instruments, instrument_sightings, option_terms, source_records, record_problems, transactions, transfer_links, trades, trade_groups, trade_group_members, journal, journal_tags, adjustments, adjustment_legs), with instrument_joins' key being the gap in finding 1.

The brief-22 oracle (capacity.rs:878-911) and each_writer_leaves_the_engine_as_a_fresh_build_would (figures.rs:612-666) keep holding as written; the boundary test (tests_boundary.rs:228-252) gaining `ledger`, `transactions`, `trades` does not catch engine-memory scans such as csv_import::candidates, which the plan replaces anyway.

entries.rs: held_by_symbol and contract_by_terms (:106-139) by an index of current names (instrument_sightings → `instrument` key) and transactions by id keep the kind-in-the-match rule; `waits` reads matched.waiting by key (:172).
